News.title: Meghan says she was informed about 'disturbing allegations' against her father in 2018
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has said she was informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father in 2018.

In a statement, Meghan said a letter containing allegations against Thomas Markle was sent to the Metropolitan Police that year and subsequently shared with her.

Her comments come after reports that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to her father had been found at his former home in the Philippines.

Thomas Markle, who is 82 and based in the US, denies possessing any such images.

Commenting after the allegations, first reported by The Sun newspaper, external, the duchess said: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said that when she received the letter outlining allegations against her father, she was "given assurance that these were being investigated".

She added she hoped it could be understood why she had kept her distance from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

This was "to protect them", Meghan said, adding that she had "trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families".

She described the allegations as "more sickening than one could ever imagine" and said her "sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children".

News.title: Watch: Moment part of Brighton's historic West Pier collapses
News.content:
A section of Brighton's historic West Pier has collapsed into the sea during the wet and windy weather brought by Storm Austen.

In footage obtained by the BBC, one side of the famous landmark in the East Sussex city can be seen falling into the water as it is battered by large waves.

The pier - which first opened in 1866 - attracted two million visitors at its peak, though its popularity declined after World War Two. While it was closed to the public in 1975, the increasingly ruined structure has become a symbol of Brighton for some.

Major sections fell into the sea during storms in late 2002, while two separate fires the following year destroyed most of what remained. Subsequent storms have destroyed its iron frame even further.

News.title: Burnham suggests stocking up on tinned food and bottled water
News.content:
The prime minister has advised people to stock up on tinned food and bottled water in order to be prepared for emergencies.

With storms battering the UK, and in the wake of online disruption caused by a major security flaw, Andy Burnham said "unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common".

The government has drawn up recommendations for households to have three days' worth of bottled water and tinned food to deal with a crisis such as a war, an online attack or a natural disaster.

Burnham added: "It's not about panic buying... It's about just taking sensible measures to have enough in the house to tide you over should there be a difficult situation."

At Labour's conference last month, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner joked that her emergency box, external would include a bottle of wine.

She said she'd include: "Mascara, concealer, I don't know, a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, a tin of baked beans because you've gotta have some baked beans, and I like a good tin of custard as well so I think that'll keep me going for a while."

Asked whether he agreed with her, Burnham told BBC Radio 5 Live's Matt Chorley: "Well, I'm not sure a bottle of wine is your best first port of call if you're in a slightly crisis situation, but it probably helps when you've done the hard work.

"But I'll stick to the basics I think - I do like my beans, so I have plenty of those in the cupboard, and soup.

"I think those are the kind of things that I would recommend people to have, as well as Twiglets, I'm not sure I can get by for too long without those."

Last month, the National Audit Office (NAO) warned Britain's food supply chain is at risk given the growing threat of cyber-attacks and the climate crisis and said the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra) had not done enough in recent years to improve supply chain resilience.

The chief executive of the Cold Chain Federation, which represents firms transporting temperature-controlled foods, also told the BBC the UK is being targeted by Russian cyber-hackers who "know that there are pinch points in the food supply system".

Speaking at a wildfire resilience summit in Liverpool, Burnham denied the government had failed to properly prepare, saying: "No, we're having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we're living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common.

"Obviously, weather events, and we're in a situation today where the UK is facing storms and obviously, we feel for the people without power in Cornwall right now.

"It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments. So we are having that conversation about resilience."

News.title: Bayern Munich manager Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at training
News.content:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital after collapsing as he watched the club's second team train on Friday.

The 40-year-old had been unwell with a virus and missed the pre-match news conference on Tuesday prior to Bayern's Champions League game against Arsenal.

The former Manchester City and Belgium defender was subsequently on the touchline for the match on Wednesday.

"Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's amateurs," said a statement from the Bundesliga club., external

"The first-team coach had been watching the second team's session.

"Kompany will undergo thorough examination in the hospital and remain in medical care.

"For the time being, his coaching staff will manage training and match operations."

Bayern's next game is against Freiburg in the German top flight on Sunday.

"Vincent Kompany's health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure his speedy recovery," said Bayern sporting director Max Eberl.

"Vinnie will receive all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs.

"His coaching team, in whom we have complete confidence, will take over his duties. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a speedy recovery."

Aaron Danks, one of Kompany's assistants, took the pre-match news conference for Bayern before the Arsenal game.

News.title: Glasgow museums remove mummified remains from public view over ethical concerns
News.content:
Two museums in Glasgow have removed the remains of Egyptian mummies from display over ethical concerns.

The mummified corpse of the priest Nekht was taken out of public view at Kelvingrove Gallery, while The Hunterian Museum has covered Lady Shep-En-Hor's body in a specially designed textile to protect it from being seen by visitors.

The institutions said the decisions followed a reassessment of their duty of care towards the deceased.

It comes after the International Council of Museums (Icom) revised its code of ethics, recommending that the "inherent dignity" of human remains be upheld.

Both museums said they would consider repatriation of the remains should they receive an approach from a country or institution.

Despite the new code of ethics, there is no uniform approach across Scotland's museum sector with different institutions given leeway on how to implement it.

A spokesperson for National Museums Scotland (NMS) said it was not considering any changes to the display of human remains in its collection.

NMS has a large collection of Scottish archaeological remains, external as well as mummified people from Egypt and Peru.

News.title: Detective raped by colleague says Met handling of case 'like being raped again'
News.content:
A Metropolitan Police detective, who was raped by a fellow officer, has told the BBC that Scotland Yard's handling of her case was "like being raped all over again".

Det Con Linda Williams was attacked in 2004 by PC David Carrick - a serial abuser jailed for life in 2023 for sexual offences against her and 11 other women.

Linda has post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) because of the attack and sought damages from the Met for failing to protect her from Carrick. The lengthy civil case left her feeling suicidal, she says.

The "worst thing", she says, was when lawyers acting for the Met commissioner challenged the severity of her PTSD on the basis that she had been raped only once.

The Met has told the BBC it "tried to reduce further distress and re-traumatisation to DC Williams' welfare and has aimed to deal with her claims as quickly and compassionately as possible".

"We recognise the unique and additional impact on DC Linda Williams, whose exposure to Carrick came as a result of her being a Met officer," the force added. "Her continued commitment to public service, in spite of the trauma she experienced, is commendable."

Linda, who has waived her legal right to anonymity to speak to the BBC, has settled her civil case and the Met has now paid her compensation without acceptance of liability.

In an unprecedented move for a serving officer, she is now calling publicly for Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley to resign. She believes he has failed to change police culture as promised and she still does not trust her own force to handle cases like hers.

When he took on the most important job in UK policing in 2022, Sir Mark pledged to change the Met. At the time, the force was viewed as being in crisis - following Sarah Everard's murder by a serving officer and other scandals including officers sharing photos of murdered sisters Bibaa Henry and Nicole Smallman.

News.title: Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen at site of Jordan shooting
News.content:
Six people were killed when gunmen opened fire on a funeral in central Jordan, a government spokesperson has said.

Another 28 people were injured in the church in the Karak governorate on Friday.

The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car and began shooting inside the church before fleeing the scene.

Security forces have been deployed to the area after the "heinous" attack, government spokesman Mohammad al-Momani said.

News.title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?
News.content:
Do you have three days' worth of food and water in your home?

That is what the government has told all of us to have on hand to get through a national emergency, as well as some other basic items.

Its "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need to get through a rocky few days.

On Friday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said unexpected events "seem to becoming more common" and everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".

As one expert warns the UK is "light years" behind our neighbours when it comes to preparing for major disruption, we've drilled down into what you need and why.

News.title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial
News.content:
Shares in the drugmakers MSD (known as Merck in the US) and Moderna have surged since both companies first hinted at the success of the vaccine in the summer.

But investors sold off stock on Thursday after financial analysts said the results were not quite as strong as those seen in an earlier, much smaller trial.

Both companies said they were now "engaging with authorities" suggesting they could file for approval from medicine regulators as soon as next year.

Widespread NHS use will also depend on cost, given that each individual patient will need to have their tumour genetically analysed and a personalised vaccine made for them.

The trial will continue so that the patients involved can be monitored â both to see if the cancer returns over time and to assess whether the drug ultimately helps them live longer.

Professor Alan Melcher from the Institute of Cancer Research in London, who wasn't involved in the research, described the results as "very impressive".

"It is an important proof of principle for the field, although we shouldn't get ahead of the evidence," he said.

"We can't assume from one melanoma trial that the same approach will work across all cancers, and longer follow-up will be important to understand the effect on overall survival."

The full trial results are due to be presented at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) cancer conference in Madrid on Saturday.

They have yet to be published in a peer-reviewed medical journal, where they can be scrutinised by independent experts.

News.title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets
News.content:
The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have received suspended prison sentences after they admitted to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.

Anthony Lee used "inside information" emerging from a private meeting called by then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to bet on the general election date months before it took place, Southwark Crown Court heard.

Lee and his wife Laura stood to win more than Â£23,000 had their cheating not been uncovered, the court heard.

Lee was sentenced to 10 months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, while his wife was sentenced to four months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for a year.

Amy Hind, a former Tory party employee who was working as an NHS business support manager, was also sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for a year, after previously pleading guilty to cheating on the date of the election.

Judge Tony Baumgartner, sentencing the three of them, said their conduct "risked undermining" the confidence the public has in the Conservative Party "as an institution", "undermining trust in the democratic process" and the "integrity of the gambling system".

The trio were among several people charged with betting offences by the Gambling Commission.

The trials of other defendants will take place next year and in 2028.

Former Conservative MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.

News.title: Mum sentenced for killing her three children
News.content:
A mother who admitted killing her three children has been sentenced to an indefinite hospital order in a secure psychiatric facility.

The bodies of Fares Bash, seven, Joury Bash, three, and nine-month-old Mohammed Bash were discovered on Blaise Walk in Sea Mills, Bristol, on 18 February 2024.

Appearing at Bristol Crown Court earlier, Yasmeen Ali, 44, admitted three charges of manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility, as her defence said she was suffering from an "acute psychosis".

She wept as details of the fatal injuries were read out. Describing her as a "loving mother", Judge Justice Linden said: "It is my view you would not have done what you have if you were well."

The judge sentenced Ali to an indefinite hospital order after hearing psychiatric evidence that her offending was "almost entirely attributable to mental disorder".

"For the rest of your existence, you will live with the knowledge of what you have done and the loss of your beloved children," he added.

"I am quite sure that you are heartbroken by what happened."

News.title: Trial set for men accused of synagogue bomb plot
News.content:
Two Iranian men have appeared in court over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb.

Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool, and Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, are accused of conducting hostile reconnaissance at Heaton Park Synagogue, which was subject to a fatal attack last year, along with the Jewish Museum in Cheetham Hill.

The pair, who arrived illegally into the UK on boats, are charged with engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts on or before 20 September. They deny the charges.

They appeared via videolink at the Old Bailey and a trial date was set at Manchester Crown Court for 15 June 2027.

It is alleged Ahmadyan and Salehi were in contact with an Iranian national who directed and co-ordinated the planned attack, with the third party most likely operating within Iran.

The men are accused of getting instructions to make a chlorine bomb and acquiring liquids, components and equipment required in order to manufacture or assemble an improvised explosive device.

They are also accused of using the internet to identify and research potential targets, acquiring images, plans and maps of potential targets and conducting reconnaissance of potential locations for attack.

The pair deny the charges against them.

The trial is estimated to last five weeks. The next court hearing is due to take place on 16 April next year.

Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of Heaton Park Hebrew Synagogue on 2 October last year, and began a knife attack while wearing a fake suicide belt.

News.title: PM defends Gogglebox appearance after Badenoch criticism
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has defended his decision to appear on a celebrity episode of Channel 4 hit show Gogglebox after opposition leader Kemi Badenoch said she was "amazed" he had time to do it.

Badenoch told BBC Breakfast that "even as a junior minister or as a secretary of state, I never had time to go on Gogglebox" and it "takes hours to do".

The Conservative leader was responding after Burnham was revealed in the line-up of a celebrity episode of the show in aid of Stand Up To Cancer - which will air later.

"I'm proud to support Stand Up To Cancer. I make no apology for trying to lead with a bit of lightness and at times a bit of humour, that's the way I go at things," Burnham said.

The former Greater Manchester mayor will appear on the programme alongside friend Steve Rotheram, the Labour mayor of the Liverpool City Region.

Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, Burnham continued: "It is always a moment in the annual calendar where we support Stand Up To Cancer through Gogglebox," Burnham said of the recurring charity special.

"Steve and I are proud to do it.

"I'm trying to give the country a lift - trying to give the county some hope.

"That's always my approach and it's what I'm trying to do.

"It may not appeal to everybody when it comes to Gogglebox.

"It's Stand Up To Cancer night and I've always been somebody who puts my shoulder behind the fight against cancer."

News.title: Man charged over Belfast knife attack pleads not guilty
News.content:
A man charged in connection with a knife attack in north Belfast that sparked serious disorder in the city has pleaded not guilty to attempted murder.

Hadi Alodid, 31, of Duncairn Avenue in Belfast, has also denied possessing a bladed weapon and a charge of threatening or abusive behaviour.

Alodid is accused of carrying out the attack on Stephen Ogilvie in June.

Stephen Ogilvie, who is in his 40s, lost his left eye in the incident and sustained damage to his right.

Alodid, who has been in custody since the attack, was led into the dock in handcuffs at Belfast Crown Court, where three charges were put to him.

Dressed in a grey prison tracksuit, Alodid stood with his arms folded as an Arabic interpreter translated the proceedings for him.

He responded to all three charges in English with the words "not guilty".

A date was set for his trial in early February.

A number of review hearings will be held prior to that.

The attack, which the court heard took place in the vicinity of Kinnaird Avenue in north Belfast, happened on June 8.

Videos circulating online at the time showed a number of people, including one wielding a hurling stick, confronting the apparent attacker until police arrived.

Alodid was arrested at the scene and remanded into custody.

Following the attack, violence erupted across Belfast, which saw homes and vehicles set alight.

News.title: 'Sexually obsessed' stepdad jailed for murdering student
News.content:
This article contains distressing details.

A man who was "sexually obsessed" with his stepdaughter has been jailed for a minimum of 35 years for murdering her at her university flat on her 20th birthday.

Nathan Owens, 34, from Hartlepool, killed Carla Georgescu in her room at the University of Lancashire property in Preston in February and then staged the scene to make it look like she had taken her own life.

Judge Jacobs said Carla had been described as polite, kind, intelligent and articulate with "a very gentle way" but she had suffered "a horrific brutal attack".

He said Owens had a "longstanding sexual obsession with Carla" that was hidden from her and her mother.

News.title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme
News.content:
Households will need to earn less than Â£110,000 to qualify for the government's new loan scheme for first-time buyers, or Â£140,000 for homes bought in London.

As first reported by The Times, external, the earnings limits are expected to be confirmed at the Budget next week.

The Your First Home scheme will offer government-backed equity loans worth 20% of new-build properties in England bought from participating developers.

The loans, which will also be subject to an initial interest-free period, are designed to help people buy a home with deposits as low as 2.5%.

Previous schemes to help first-time buyers did not restrict eligibility by income but faced criticism for stoking house prices by allowing relatively wealthy households to borrow more.

Unveiling the Your First Home Scheme at last month's Labour conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would focus on those who "really need support".

The Times reported that ministers had initially decided to set the earnings limits at Â£90,000 for homes outside outside London and Â£110,000 in the capital, before concluding this would deny access to too many middle-earning couples, such as teachers and nurses.

The government has also argued that the scheme will help to boost housebuilding, after ministers conceded they are set to miss a target to build 1.5 million homes in England by the next election.

News.title: Who is supporting Gianni Infantino and how many votes will secure re-election as Fifa president?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.

England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027.

But as the dust has settled on his privatisation ploy, Infantino’s bid for a third term has strengthened. His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf, the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”.

Infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president. Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino:

Who has formally withdrawn its support for Infantino?

Uefa (55 members) 🇪🇺

Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian.

The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.

More recently, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions.

Concacaf (41 members) 🌎

Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject.

After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.”

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief.

England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿

The English FA is one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027.

Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme.

open image in gallery FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino ( PA )

Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

The Football Association of Wales was one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino.

“The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿

The SFA’s chief executive Ian Maxwell told the BBC that the governing body’s position has “been clear” since Uefa’s collective statement.

“We have aligned ourselves with the Uefa position and 55 nations are stronger than one voice.

“Their statement since then has talked about a lack of confidence in the Fifa leadership and the Scottish FA agree completely with that decision.

“The SFA will not be voting for Gianni Infantino come the re-election in early 2027.”

Republic of Ireland 🇮🇪

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance.

"Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.”

Italy 🇮🇹

The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) took a few weeks to take official action but it has now withdrawn its support for Infantino's candidacy in the next Fifa presidential election scheduled.

"This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC's position - in full agreement with Uefa and its president Aleksander Ceferin - regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions," FIGC said in a statement.

Finland 🇫🇮

Finland kickstarted this process of formal withdrawals, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino.

Serbia 🇷🇸

The Football Association of Serbia then sent a similar letter to Fifa.

“We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read.

Sweden 🇸🇪

Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election.

"This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists."

open image in gallery Infantino has officially lost the endorsement of numerous Uefa nations ( PA )

Croatia 🇭🇷

As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president.

"This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time."

Albania 🇦🇱

The Albanian Football Federation also took the same stance, aligning with Uefa.

“The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed.

Greece 🇬🇷

The Greek Football Association has backed Uefa’s push for a change in Fifa’s leadership, similarly withdrawing support to underscore a united European front in opposition to Infantino.

"The Greek FA (EPO) has taken a clear position against a candidacy of Gianni Infantino," EPO presdient Makis Gagatsis told reporters. "We saw things happen at the World Cup that are not acceptable to football public opinion. Then... came a programme to sell World Cup rights and we are clearly against it, so we withdrew our support of the Fifa president."

Germany 🇩🇪

The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance.

“The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board."

Former Germany national team director Oliver Bierhoff further reiterated the nation’s loss of trust in Infantino: "We have to take care of football. It is already commercial but it is a property for all of football. The world views may be different but in the last weeks and months a lot happened so that we have no trust any more that it will be going in the right direction."

Denmark 🇩🇰

Denmark are in a similar position to Germany, having not endorsed Infantino’s re-election bid prior to the scheme’s reveal.

There is also a precedent for their opposition to Infantino, with federation president Jesper Moller not supporting his re-election efforts back in 2022: “There is only one candidate ... but Denmark will not be supporting the current president.”

Norway 🇳🇴

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) have been one of the most vocal bodies to call for Infantino’s resignation, and while they have not yet officially sent a letter to withdraw their support in him, such action is expected in the coming days.

NFF president Lise Klaveness told the Guardian: “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now. We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

open image in gallery Lise Klaveness has called on Infantino to resign ( Reuters )

Netherlands 🇳🇱

The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is also yet to officially withdraw its support but is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read.

Romania 🇷🇴

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) were among the countries to resolutely reject the sell-off proposal, calling it “a dangerous initiative to turn football into a private asset.

As a result, the FRF will withold support for Infantino’s re-election for the time being, with a statement reading: “FRF is suspending the discussion regarding the support of Fifa President Gianni Infantino for a new term, until further clarifications.”

Northern Ireland ☘️

The Northern Irish football association (IFA) has expressed “concerns” over Infantino’s leadership but has not officially withdrawn its support yet, unlike neighbours Ireland.

"We take our responsibilities as a member association of both Uefa and Fifa seriously," said an IFA spokesperson. "We support the current Uefa position on the matter and will continue to engage constructively on issues relating to football governance. We are of course aware of the recent developments and wider concerns within the football community. We are considering these matters carefully and will continue to engage through the appropriate governance structures and channels.”

Jordan 🇯🇴

Jordan were the first non-Uefa member association to publicly oppose Infantino after federation president Prince Ali bin Hussein levelled accusations of blackmail against Fifa.

Prince Ali alleged the organisation offered assistance with the kingdom's issues in exchange for his endorsement, following Infantino's withdrawal from a World Cup stake sale proposal. Among the problems cited was the association's eight-month wait for prize money, due since December for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

After taking to X to reveal the outstanding payments, the Jordan Football Association received the prize money two days later - but Prince Ali has not changed his stance over not endorsing Infantino: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

New Zealand 🇳🇿

New Zealand have broken rank with Oceania’s confederation by withdrawing their support for Infantino.

"After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within Fifa have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust,” a statement read.

Who is supporting Infantino?

Confederation of African Football (54 members) 🌍

Caf, the governing body for African football, was the first confederation to unanimously back Infantino.

“We are committed to continue working together with Fifa, its member associations, other football confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of football worldwide,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said.

Motsepe later added that the position of embattled president Infantino can only be decided by Fifa elections.

Asian Football Confederation (47 members) 🌏

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has endorsed Infantino an apparent turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticised the head of football’s world governing body for a breach of trust.

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress meeting in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

“We affirm our full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the Fifa president.” Sheikh Salman said. “You’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well.”

Argentina 🇦🇷

Argentina became the first member from South America to voice its support for Infantino, on the same day that confederation Conmebol - which had thus far only expressed support of Infantino - expressed concern over Fifa’s procedures.

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the Fifa board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Argentina president Javier Milei (left) behind Infantino at the "Board of Peace" hosted by US president Donald Trump ( AFP/Getty )

Paraguay 🇵🇾

Paraguay also followed suit as Infantino’s Conmebol support base surfaces.

Their federation published a letter of support addressed to Infantino, writing that it "reaffirms its commitment to continue working alongside Fifa”.

Mexico 🇲🇽

Mexico joined Argentina from the Americas, breaking rank from the United States, Canada and the rest of Concacaf that had condemned Infantino’s plan and aligned itself against his leadership.

The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) stated: "The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made... by President Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations."

Grenada 🇬🇩

Grenada’s federation (GFA) has also broken away from the Concacaf block and reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

“The GFA reaffirms its support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and expresses its sincere appreciation for his continued support for football development in Grenada and across the Caribbean over his period of service in office and for the years to come,” a statement read.

Saint Kitts and Nevis 🇰🇳

Like Grenada, the Saint Kitts and Nevis Football Association (SKNFA) has welcomed Infantino’s decision to scrap the plan, called for respect of Fifa’s institutional processes and backed the president to continue.

It said: “The SKNFA concluded by reaffirming its support for Infantino’s leadership and vision, and said it looks forward to supporting him as he completes his current constitutional mandate and continues efforts to advance football development across Fifa’s 211 Member Associations.”

Qatar 🇶🇦

Qatar was the first football association to publicly back Infantino, even though they later welcomed the decision to scrap the plan.

"While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among member associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Qatar's FA has backed Infantino to continue as president ( Getty Images )

Sri Lanka 🇱🇰

Like Qatar, Sri Lanka welcomed the decision to scrap the investment plan and has since reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

"One of President Infantino's defining leadership qualities has always been his willingness to listen to the views and concerns of Member Associations. This decision is a clear reflection of his inclusive leadership style, built on dialogue, mutual respect, and a genuine commitment to serving the global football community," its statement read.

Kuwait 🇰🇼

Like others, Kuwait welcomed the decision to halt the plans but Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Al-Sabah, the president of the Kuwait Football Association, affirmed his support for Infantino.

A statement read: “He concluded by affirming the Kuwait Football Association's confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino, and its support for efforts aimed at developing the game and enhancing its opportunities for growth in a way that serves all national associations and achieves the shared interests of global football.”

Lebanon 🇱🇧

Lebanon, who granted Infantino citizenship last year, have backed the Swiss-Italian, with FA president Hashim Haidar all but echoing the same sentiments as Kuwait.

“Haidar reaffirms the Lebanese Football Association’s support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and his confidence in the decisions he makes in the best interests of global football, as well as in his efforts and initiatives aimed at developing the game,” he said, while also asserting that Infantino’s proposal “could be re-examined ... in a away that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity”.

Indonesia 🇮🇩

The president of the Indonesian FA supported Infantino’s sell-off plan and has now backed him for another term.

Hailing Fifa as a “strategic partner that is truly present” in its football development, Erick Thohir said: “This is proof of President Infantino’s vision that football development must not be centered on a single region; it must proceed worldwide.”

Philippines 🇵🇭

Philippines have also backed Infantino and backed for co-operation among confederations.

"We stand behind President Gianni Infantino's leadership, and trust that continued dialogue among all confederations and member associations will keep the global game moving forward together,” the Philippines confirmed.

Mongolia 🇲🇳

Joining the Philippines, the Mongolian Football Federation has put out a statement in support of Infantino.

Bhutan 🇧🇹

The Bhutan Football Federation has published a letter that extends its “sincere appreciation” to Infantino for scrapping the plans, hailing him for demonstrating “true leadership” by “prioritising consensus over commerce”.

“We stand united with Fifa and President Infantino in their ongoing efforts to serve the global football community,” wrote federation president Dasho Ugen Tsechup.

Morocco 🇲🇦

The location of Infantino’s crisis meeting on Wednesday, Morocco have stuck by the Swiss-Italian as one of his most loyal allies.

“What has been achieved in recent years through Fifa’s development programmes, particularly in Africa, represents an important accomplishment that must be preserved, to the benefit of all member associations,” said the Royal Moroccan Football Federation’s president Fouzi Lekjaa.

open image in gallery Infantino held his crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco ( AP )

Egypt 🇪🇬

Similar to their north African counterpart, Egypt have maintained their endorsement of Infantino.

"The Egyptian Football Association reiterates its full trust in President Gianni Infantino's leadership and its continuous support for any initiatives that benefit Fifa member associations and the future of world football,” a statement read.

Mauritania 🇲🇷

Ahmed Yahya, the country's representative on the Fifa Council, was one of a number of African football leaders to say he was backing Infantino early on, pledging his support before Caf took its stance.

Niger 🇳🇪

Same as above, with Hamidou Djibrilla from Niger coming out quickly in support of Infantino.

Sudan 🇸🇩

Sudan’s federation joined five other Arab nations - Qatar, Lebanon, Morocco, Egypt and Mauritania - in writing a joint statement backing Infantino.

"Recognising the important role of Arab football in bringing people together and strengthening co-operation among football associations across the Arab world, we ... express our full support for Mr Gianni Infantino, president of Fifa, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," the statement read.

"We deeply appreciate Mr Infantino’s sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game’s role in bringing people and communities together. We look forward to continuing our close cooperation with him towards a stronger and more prosperous future for world ‌football, expanding opportunities and further enhancing Arab football’s contribution to ​the global game."

DR Congo 🇨🇩

DR Congo's federation (Fecofa) president Veron Mosengo-Omba, who was only elected in May, spoke out in “full support”. of Infantino. The two studied at university in Switzerland together.

Fecofa said it had "greatly benefited" from Fifa's programmes, citing investment in development and infrastructure.

Nigeria 🇳🇬

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has largely aligned itself towards a supportive stance for Infantino's leadership, with former NFF president and deputy chairman of Fifa's Men's National Teams Competitions Committee, Amaju Pinnick, backing his initial sell-off plan.

Comoros 🇰🇲

The president of the Comoros Football Federation, Said Ali Athouman, also backed Infantino’s scheme due to the financial benefits to smaller nations.

"Our problem is how to obtain money,” he said. “Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete? The richest nations can train players, have infrastructure and equipment, and it's no coincidence that they then achieve results. Most European countries don't have ​these problems.”

open image in gallery A number of African nations have fallen in line with the stance of Caf president Patrice Motsepe ( Getty )

Malawi 🇲🇼

Fleetwood Haiya, Malawi's football chief, echoed the same concerns in his support for Infantino.

He told BBC Sport: "Our government is not able to make sure that they have medical supplies in hospitals and at the same time to look at football. Malawi needs money."

Uganda 🇺🇬

The Ugandan federation are said to have echoed Malawi’s sentiments, with football officials from the federation telling BBC Sport that Fifa investment has transformed their game both on and off the pitch.

Gambia 🇬🇲

Lamin Kaba Bajo told BBC Sport that his federation not just stood by Infantino, but would do "everything within our means" to get him re-elected.

"That's my personal opinion as president of the federation, and a good number of African memberships also stand on that line. He is here to stay,” he said.

Djibouti 🇩🇯

The Djiboutian Football Federation has similarly welcomed the decision to withdraw the sell-off proposal, with president Souleiman Hassan Waberi saying the climbdown “demonstrates a firm commitment to preserving the unity, solidarity and cohesion that define the football family”.

He said in a statement: “I reaffirm my full support for Fifa President Mr Gianni Infantino and for all initiatives aimed at promoting the sustainable, transparent and inclusive development of football around the world.”

South Africa 🇿🇦

While not an official statement from the federation, South Africa’s Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of South Africa, Gayton McKenzie, posted on X saying that Infantino had been "very good to African football".

"Africa should be cautious in joining the public lynching of Infantino,” he warned. “He has been very good to African football. We can debate his ideas but let's not forget who has been a friend to us. Many of those calling for his head want the old status quo back too."

Who is yet to take a stance?

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC), with its 11 member associations, stopped short from pulling its support for Infantino in their statement after welcoming the scrapping of the sell-off plan, very much staying on the fence as it called for a “review”.

A statement read: "The OFC recognises the progress achieved over the last decade in advancing football development in Oceania under Fifa's leadership and encourages Fifa to use the review as an opportunity to identify and implement any changes that may be necessary."

Meanwhile, South American body Comnebol, with its 10 member associations, expressed “concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken” and welcomed the decision to withdraw the plans, affirming it will “not support any action” that “ignores or deviates” from the “democratic procedures that represent the 211 Fifa member associations”.

However, as a long-time ally of Infantino, it did endorse him to get elected for a third term earlier in the summer, with Conmebol eager for his 64-team World Cup plans to go through for the 2030 edition. They have not explicitly confirmed this stance since the scandal, though.

State of play

As things stand, Infantino has 105 member associations backing him for re-election, while 95 members are outwardly confirmed to be opposing him. This is taking into account the endorsements of confederations, which are being considered as a blanket vote from all members under that governing body unless a member has broken rank.

For example, Jordan’s opposition to Infantino means he is not included in the other 47 AFC member associations supporting Infantino, per the confederation’s endorsement, while the likes of Mexico, Grenada, and St Kitts and Nevis are all separate from the other 38 Concacaf members in opposition.

This suggests that Infantino is teetering on securing re-election, theoretically needing just one more vote. However, each nation has a vote for itself and some could go against their confederation’s stance to turn the tide against the Swiss-Italian come March’s election.

News.title: Delia Smith shares heartbreaking first words after husband’s death
News.content:
Delia Smith has spoken publicly for the first time about the death of her husband, Michael Wynn Jones.

The couple, who were majority shareholders at Norwich City Football Club for 26 years, married in 1971.

Speaking to the Amol Rajan Connection podcast, Smith said she would have to learn how to be "half a whole" after her husband died.

Smith explained that Wynn Jones had been very ill for the last six weeks of her life, and she had been at his side "night and day."

Wynn Jones died aged 85 in September. Norwich City said he died "peacefully at home" and would be "greatly missed" by the club.

News.title: Three ways to avoid buying a new Halloween costume this year - and what to do with old ones
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

On an unusually hot day in Los Angeles, Braddock Sandoval perused tables heaped with wigs, a Darth Vader mask, a black tutu, and various other garments.

Sandoval, a chemistry professor at Occidental College, had dropped by a campus clothing swap aimed at keeping unused Halloween items out of the trash. Looking to pick up a free outfit, he selected a Hawaiian flower necklace and a shark costume to try on.

"I think there’s too much cheap plastic waste in this world. So the idea that people are recycling costumes is fantastic, both for budgets, like me, but also just for the planet," Sandoval said with a laugh. Guided by his finds, he planned to attend an upcoming Halloween dance party dressed as a great white shark eating a tourist.

Each October, Halloween outfits take center stage, but millions are thrown into landfills after being worn just once. Most are manufactured from synthetic plastics that do not readily decompose, aggravating environmental pollution. Across Southern California and the rest of the nation, thrift outlets and costume swaps are helping prevent these outfits from going to waste. By allowing people to hand in clean garments and select pre-owned replacements, these initiatives save resources and curb the emissions linked to manufacturing new goods.

open image in gallery Braddock Sandoval, a chemistry professor at Occidental College, with a costume he picked out during a Halloween costume swap ( AP Photo/Jae C. Hong )

This year, the National Retail Federation projects that Americans will spend roughly $4.4 billion on Halloween attire. Figures from the Environmental Protection Agency indicate that in 2018 alone, consumers tossed out approximately 11.3 million tons (10.25 million metric tons) of textiles. To shop more sustainably, experts advocate adhering to three simple practices: reduce, reuse, and recycle.

The spooky side of Halloween costumes

Shelie Miller, a University of Michigan professor who researches the environmental footprint of consumer goods, noted that Halloween costumes mirror fast fashion, as they are frequently produced cheaply from plastic materials. They break down easily, she explained, and are "not really intended to stick around for a very long time."

The broader ecological consequences are considerable. Clothing generation represents between 4% and 10% of global carbon emissions, Miller observed, while textile dyeing accounts for around 20% of industrial wastewater emissions worldwide.

Synthetic fabrics used in many garments and costumes can release microplastics during washing, which then flow into aquatic systems. These microplastics have been detected in oceans, air, food, drinking water, and human tissues, with growing evidence indicating potential risks to human health. Furthermore, many synthetic fibers are derived from petroleum, which releases pollutants when burned, driving global warming and exacerbating severe weather.

open image in gallery People gather at a Halloween costume swap at Occidental College in Los Angeles ( AP Photo/Jae C. Hong )

"The process of making these, the Halloween costumes, it’s incredible," said Zack Bowersox, a senior lecturer in political science at Washington University in St. Louis who teaches a class on fast fashion and the environment.

Instead of traditional stitching, costume components are frequently heat bonded by melting the plastic edges together. "After the season, they’re not meant to even be thrifted or returned, they’re just meant to be thrown away. And that’s where most of them end up, it’s in the landfill. Something like 80% of those suits end up in the landfill," Bowersox said.

Miller pointed out that consumers can celebrate Halloween without purchasing disposable outfits.

"Whenever we buy anything, we’re not just buying the one thing, we’re buying all of the environmental impacts of everything that went into making that product," Miller said. "So whenever we’re using any sort of single-use product, whether we’re talking about single-use plastic or single-use costumes, we really have to be thinking about is this really how we want to spend our time, money, resources, and is there a better way?"

Fashion lover launches a Halloween costume swap

Lexy Silverstein, a sustainable fashion advocate, created the Ultimate Halloween Swap last year after reflecting on the money and resources spent on outfits worn for only a few hours before being discarded.

An avid fan of the holiday who loves dressing up, she felt compelled to evaluate her own shopping habits.

open image in gallery Samuel Hernandez, center, looks for a costume for his grandson ( AP Photo/Jae C. Hong )

"That’s a lot of costumes that I’m buying and wearing once and getting rid of," she told herself, before considering how other recurring occasions, such as back-to-school season, also spur high consumer spending.

Her inaugural swap gathered hundreds of donated costumes, including 10 boxes supplied by the LA Clippers basketball team. Following that initial success, she expanded the initiative across Southern California, including the Occidental College event where Sandoval picked up his shark suit. Silverstein now aims to organize swaps for other high-consumption periods, such as back-to-school drives, prom season, and winter coat exchanges.

Washington University in St. Louis has developed a similar program. Its campus thrift store relies on items gathered during student move-out periods, when clothing and accessories are often abandoned. For the second year in a row, the university hosted a pop-up market allowing students and staff to purchase pre-owned costumes at low cost.

Cassie Hage, the university's assistant director at the Office of Sustainability, said this year's inventory included Austin Powers outfits, kiwi costumes, a demon character from the television series "Stranger Things", and matching platypus onesies that delighted a group of friends who found them.

open image in gallery Sustainable fashion advocate Lexy Silverstein smiles while carrying a bag of costumes dropped off for a Halloween costume swap ( AP Photo/Jae C. Hong )

"They were kind of dancing around" in them, she said. "That was just a really fun moment to watch."

How to reduce, reuse, recycle

Experts note that thrifting, joining clothing swaps, and raiding wardrobes belonging to friends or family members are effective strategies to avoid buying new items. Costumes can be pieced together from everyday clothes or existing items modified for a fresh look. Silverstein also suggests exploring rental choices on resale platforms such as Facebook Marketplace, Depop, and Poshmark.

If buying a new item is unavoidable, Bowersox suggests selecting accessories or garments made from plant-derived fibers like cotton or linen. Although officially licensed goods may cost more, he noted they frequently offer greater transparency regarding where and how they were produced.

Alison Linder, assistant sustainability coordinator at Occidental College—which hosts its own thrift shop featuring seasonal items—encouraged people to set up local exchanges with classmates, neighbors, or friends.

"It’s just as easy as asking your friends for a loan and offering to share what you have," she said. "And just by doing that simple thing, you save money and you’re helping the environment."

News.title: Popular grocery store gelato recalled in 9 states
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Check your freezer: Lidl has issued an urgent recall of a gelato sold in its grocery stores.

The recall was initiated after routine testing found Listeria in a lab sample, according to a notice from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

One lot of Lidl’s Gelatelli Coffee & Vanilla Gelato with Coffee Sauce & Cookie Pieces was affected by the recall.

The 16oz pints were sold at Lidl stores in Delaware, Georgia, Maryland, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Virginia and Washington, D.C between July 19 and October 15.

Affected pints have the UPC 4 0564897 22458, Lot number 085261, and Best By date of March 26, 2028.

open image in gallery Gelatelli coffee & vanilla gelato has been recalled ( US FDA )

Customers are urged to check their freezers and discard the gelato or return it to Lidl for a refund.

No illnesses have been reported.

“The health and safety of our customers is our top priority. Lidl US regrets any inconvenience related to this voluntary recall,” the company said in the FDA announcement.

Listeria is a bacteria that can cause the infection listeriosis. It is rare and can go away on its own, but some cases can be dangerous to elderly people, pregnant women and people with already weakened immune systems. The disease’s most common symptoms are fever and flu-like symptoms, including fatigue and muscle aches. Headaches, confusion, loss of balance and even seizures are possible.

The gelato recall is the latest affecting customers.

open image in gallery Lidl has recalled one of its gelato flavors ( Reuters )

Last week, more than 1.5 million pounds of various meat products were recalled over serious potential health concerns.

Kayem Foods Inc. initiated the recall after learning that the items may not have been stored at the correct temperature. It has since been deemed a Class I recall by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service, meaning “there is a reasonable probability that the use of the product will cause serious, adverse health consequences or death.”

An investigation that began after a customer reported receiving a warm product delivery on October 1 revealed that a warehouse cooler experienced temperature fluctuations while storing the items, according to FSIS.

Approximately 1,584,361 recalled items were manufactured between March 31, 2026 and October 7, 2026 and are labeled with the establishment numbers “EST. M/P 7839,” “EST. P 20935A” or “EST. M 9520” inside the USDA inspection mark. Affected items were shipped to retail and food service locations across the U.S. and Hong Kong.

Products include various brands of hot dogs, bacon, sausage, and deli meat. A full list of affected items can be found here.

News.title: What’s on for October half-term 2026: Best days out and Halloween events
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Looking for things to do with the kids this October half-term? From Halloween trails and after-dark rollercoasters to family-friendly attractions and indoor activities for rainy days, there are plenty of ways to keep everyone entertained during the school holidays.

I've rounded up some of the best October half-term days out across the UK, including Halloween events at Thorpe Park, Alton Towers, Legoland Windsor, Warwick Castle and Chessington World of Adventures. Whether you're planning a big family day out or looking for something affordable to fill an afternoon, you'll also find ticket deals and money-saving tips to help keep costs down.

Thorpe Park Fright Nights

Thorpe Park has a brand new scare maze for Halloween thrill-seekers ( Thorpe Park/Merlin Entertainments )

Thorpe Park is celebrating 25 years of fear with its annual Fright Nights event, which returns with a brand-new scare maze, Tenement, alongside live shows and rides after dark.

Fright Nights are running now until 1 November, making it a great option for older children, teens and adults during October half term.

The park's biggest rides, including Hyperia and Saw - The Ride, will be running after dark, while the scare mazes and shows add an extra dose of Halloween atmosphere.

Thorpe Park tickets are currently on sale from £39 per person. Pre-booking online can save up to 40 per cent compared with paying at the gate, where tickets start from £66.

See more money-saving tips in our guide to the best Thorpe Park deals and discounts

Legoland Brick or Treat

The popular “brick or treat” event is back at Legoland this autumn ( Legoland Windsor/Merlin Entertainments )

If you're looking for a Halloween day out that's suitable for younger children, Legoland Windsor is bringing back its popular Brick or Treat celebrations.

The Halloween event is running daily until 1 November, so it covers the October half-term holiday.

Children can meet spooky Halloween characters, dance at the new Lord Vampyre's house party live DJ show and cheer on the return of family favourite Monster Jam. You can also enjoy the park's usual rides and attractions, making it easy to fill a whole day.

Legoland tickets start from £37 when booked in advance, compared with £68 on the gate, giving you a saving of up to 45 per cent.

If you want to turn your visit into a short break, overnight stays start from £123 per person. This includes a stay in a themed bedroom, one day's park entry, early ride time, a free Lego gift and breakfast.

Check out our Legoland discount codes page for deals and offers

Alton Towers Scarefest

New to the Scarefest line-up for 2026 is an immersive dining experience ( Alton Towers/Merlin Entertainments )

For thrill-seeking families, Alton Towers is going all out for Halloween with its annual scarefest event.

Scarefest is running from 16 October to 1 November. Alongside the scare mazes and Halloween entertainment, visitors can experience some of the resort's biggest rides after dark, including The Smiler, Nemesis Reborn and Wicker Man.

There's also child-friendly Halloween entertainment, including the CBeebies Land monster ball, so younger visitors can still enjoy the fun.

New for 2026 is an immersive Halloween dining experience (extra cost), featuring a three-course banquet and entertainment throughout the evening. It's restricted to guests aged 14 and over, with under-18s required to attend with an adult.

Alton Towers day tickets start from £37 when booked in advance, compared with £68 on the day.

There’s also an £80 “thrills combi” ticket, which includes access to all three scare mazes, an early or late scare maze timeslot and access to the rides until 9pm.

Warwick Castle

Enjoy more than 15 live shows and attractions, including a scarecrow disco aimed at younger visitors, mystery mazes and much-loved The Witches of Warwick show.

With a mixture of family-friendly entertainment and spookier attractions, there's something for families of all ages. But if you're visiting with particularly young children, it’s still worth checking the event details before booking some activities.

There are centres across the UK, including London, Birmingham and Brighton, with themed activities and experiences running during the school holidays.

As well as seeing sharks, rays, turtles, penguins and other marine life, children can take part in Halloween and autumn activities designed to keep different age groups entertained.

Tickets are usually cheapest when booked online in advance and vary depending on the location, but you can often save more by combining your visit with another nearby Merlin attraction.

Take part in pumpkin parties, storytelling, games, trails and themed selfie spots at selected properties, giving families the chance to combine a day out with a bit of history.

News.title: Trump expresses concern about NFL game and civil unrest in Paris
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday the NFL “could have probably postponed” the upcoming game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints because of street protests in the city.

France is bracing for more demonstrations Saturday against the high cost of living, with museums closing and the government deploying a larger security presence to prevent a repeat of last week’s violent unrest.

The game Sunday — the first regular-season NFL game in France — is being held at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of the capital.

“I think maybe it’s looking like tomorrow is going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it,” Trump told reporters. “I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match ... because France is really in trouble.”

The U.S. State Department late Thursday issued a security alert, saying: “Numerous groups submitted plans for protests on Saturday, October 24. Americans in Paris for the NFL game on Sunday, October 25 should also exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings. While permits may be filed for demonstration routes, last-minute changes can happen and protests can occur outside planned routes.”

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said this week that preparations were made in consultation with U.S. and French authorities. Street protests, he said, “are not unusual in France.” The league did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump's remarks.

Soccer team Paris Saint-Germain’s game against Lyon has been moved from Sunday to Monday evening at the request of Paris police, the French soccer league said. The game was scheduled for Sunday night in Parc des Princes.

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said Friday that “the NFL is alert to what’s going on.”

“This game means a lot to the NFL. If it was unsafe, then I’m sure we wouldn’t be here,” Rodgers said at the team’s hotel in Paris.

A weekend event for Steelers fans was canceled Thursday because of security concerns.

News.title: Burnham says he will ‘make no apology’ for Celebrity Gogglebox appearance
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Burnham has responded to Kemi Badenoch after she accused him of dodging "difficult" tasks to protect the UK by taking part in a celebrity edition of Channel 4’s Gogglebox.

The Prime Minister said he would "make no apology" for attempting to "lead with a bit of lightness" after the Tory leader questioned how he found time for the show.

He added he was "proud" to back Stand Up To Cancer, the charity highlighted in Wednesday’s episode.

“That’s the way I go at things and connect with people as best I can, Burnham said.

“And perhaps if a few more people watch it tonight and then support Stand Up To Cancer, that will be job done.”

Mr Burnham is set to become the first prime minister to appear on the show on Friday night.

Burnham will be on the show alongside his close friend, Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram ( Simon Dawson/No 10 Downing Street )

In a clip released ahead of the show on Friday, Mr Burnham can be seen tearfully reacting to the stories of people diagnosed with cancer, which he described as “utter devastation”.

Sitting on a sofa alongside his close friend, Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram, he says he “just couldn’t imagine” the ordeal, adding: “The only thing that does give some hope is there is so much incredible research going on, and some of the main cancers of years ago, there’s been such big progress on them.

“But it’s utter devastation isn’t it, if you’re that couple I don’t know how you cope with that.”

Mr Burnham is not the first Labour leader to appear on Gogglebox for Stand Up To Cancer, after Jeremy Corbyn featured on the Channel 4 programme in 2017.

Alastair Campbell, Tony Blair’s former spin doctor, and Boris Johnson’s father, Stanley, have also taken part over the years.

Wednesday’s episode will also feature actor Stanley Tucci, comedian Joe Lycett and the Sugababes.

Speaking to the Press Association earlier, Mrs Badenoch questioned the Prime Minister’s decision to take part in the show while he had other commitments to attend to.

Referring to the government’s advice to the public to stockpile food, water and other essentials to prepare for possible emergencies in the future, she said: “I don’t mind them giving advice.

“I worry that between the Prime Minister being on Gogglebox and then talking about stockpiling canned goods, they’re not actually doing the really difficult stuff that will protect the country.”

News.title: Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy
News.content:
A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

News.title: Oil hits five-month high amid fears of fresh strikes on Iran
News.content:
The price of oil has hit a five-month high amid fears Donald Trump will ramp up strikes in the Middle East following the midterm elections.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, climbed as much as 2.8pc to more than $116 a barrel, pushing down stock markets in the US and Europe.

It followed a New York Times report that the US and Israel had drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the midterm elections.

Oil has climbed more than 4pc this week, increasing pressure on stock markets at the same time as fears grow about the valuations of AI companies.

European shares fell on Friday, with the FTSE 100 down as much as 0.8pc, the Cac 40 in Paris down 1pc and the Dax in Frankfurt down 1.1pc.

On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell as much as 1pc, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell at a slower pace than the previous day.

Traders were rattled on Thursday after Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, warned that a “scarcity of capital” was hampering the rollout of the technology.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq in New York dropped by 2.6pc on Thursday while the S&P 500 fell 1.2pc on its worst day since July.

Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta was one of the worse hit in the sell-off, as its shares finished trading almost 7pc lower.

Overnight, the sell-off spread into Asian markets. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped by as much as 2.3pc and was down more than 4pc on the week.

The Kospi index in South Korea declined as much as 4.1pc on Friday but recovered to be marginally higher as markets closed.

The stock market turmoil led to a jump in safe haven assets like bonds.

The yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds, a benchmark for the cost of borrowing for governments around the world, fell by the largest amount since March 2023.

News.title: Europe’s record-breaking summer heat estimated to have killed 50,000 people
News.content:
More than 50,000 people are estimated to have died across Europe as a result of this summer’s record-breaking heatwaves, according to research.

In the UK alone, researchers estimate there were 4,354 excess deaths this summer.

The number of excess deaths across Europe is double the number recorded in 2025 and it is also far higher than the previous record of 29,000 deaths. This was recorded in 2022 when the continent also endured exceptionally high temperatures, with the mercury hitting 40 degrees celsius for the first time in the UK.

According to the Met Office the UK saw its hottest ever summer this year with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Mainland Europe experienced its third hottest summer, with temperatures particularly high in the south and west.

Researchers from Imperial College, London and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) looked at 854 urban areas in 30 countries across Europe. Using temperature records and modelling based on the relationship between heat and mortality they estimated the number of heat-related deaths that occurred between June and August.

They said findings from previous years’ excess heat mortality modelling matched official figures released later by national health authorities.

Because the study only looked at urban areas – making up 40 per cent of the population of the countries studied – researchers believe the number of deaths is likely to be an underestimate.

According to the study, published in Nature Health, southern and western Europe were hardest hit. Italy experienced the highest number of excess deaths (13,303), followed by France (7,268), Spain (6,824), Germany (6,340) then the UK.

There were an estimated 22,000 deaths among those aged 85 and over but researchers pointed out that an estimated 6,000 people under the age of 65 are also likely to have died as a result of the heat.

Around a third of the deaths took place in late June, when average temperatures across Europe were more than 5°C above what would be expected during this time of year. Researchers say in early summer people were less likely to have acclimatised to the sweltering weather. This period was marked by both extremely high humidity and unusually high night-time temperatures, making it difficult for people to cool down.

Researchers also estimated that more than two thirds of the total excess deaths were attributable to climate change. Across the continent as a whole Europe was an average 2.9°C higher than would have been expected. However, in some places temperatures were as much as 12°C higher.

Dr Clair Barnes, extreme weather and climate change researcher at Imperial College, said extreme heat was having a severe impact on public health.

“It is yet another reminder both of the imperative of rolling out targeted interventions to protect those who are most vulnerable to this increasingly extreme heat, and of the growing need to rapidly transition away from fossil fuels to slow the pace of change and limit future warming.”

Dr Pierre Masselot, assistant professor of statistics and epidemiology at LSHTM and one of the study’s authors, said “climate change is everybody’s problem”.

“It is not just hot regions that are suffering any more with some parts of Western and Northern Europe experiencing extreme heat and historically high health burden. And the whole population is affected, as shown by the significant death toll among younger age groups.

“It is becoming increasingly clear our cities are poorly adapted to rising heat, and it is critical we improve our efforts towards adaptation. This means cooling the cities through more green spaces and less pollution, and providing health care for affected populations.”
