News.title: Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history
News.content:
Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

News.title: Harry Brook hits historic double century – but England still lose to Sri Lanka
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to the fourth match of the autumn tri-series in Pakistan. After two wins for the hosts, the two touring sides face each other for the first time in Rawalpindi, the last match here before the circus leaves for Lahore. England and Sri Lanka played each other only last month in this format, England winning at Chester-le-Street and the Oval by a distance, those victories sandwiching a narrow defeat at Headingley where, if you remember, Harry Brook’s side were cruising until Jos Buttler ripped his left hamstring. He did eventually come back out to bat on one leg as his rattled team-mates flapped and fell to Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka and Eshan Malinga.

On Tuesday against Pakistan, England again were flying with both ball and bat but they let the middle-order rebuild, losing control of the rate. Their two most experienced white-ball bowlers, Adil Rashid, who looked rusty after breaking his hand in August, and Sam Curran, who missed the end of August and all of September following groin surgery, went for 6.87 and eight runs an over respectively. Then, after a promising opening partnership, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull, Tom Banton flicked straight to midwicket and Will Jacks later fell in identical fashion when well-set to marshal the chase. Arafat Minhas ended up with six for 40, bowling Harry Brook with a beauty, and there will be more trial by spin today.

Although there was some talk of England failing in end-of-days Bazball fashion, it most reminded me of the teething troubles of Eoin Morgan’s side in 2015 and 2016 when they were experimenting with players, viz this Rose Bowl collapse. We have to acknowledge that Joe Root, the best player of spin, was undone by one that kept low from Naseem Shah and both Brook and Jordan Cox lost their wickets to very good deliveries from Arafat, a bowler, on a feast day. Dunith Welllalage will return to try to replicate his line of attack today but he is a bowler that England know well. He has had his days against them but they have also given him some tap in the past.

News.title: Health authorities race to investigate first human death linked to Shamonda virus
News.content:
A French man has become the first person to contract Shamonda virus, a disease previously only found in animals and spread through midges.

The patient, who had a weakened immune system, has since died, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).

Shamonda virus was first identified in Nigeria in the 1960s and has this year been detected in farm animals all across Europe.

It was confirmed to have spread to the British Isles in September, after being found in a cattle herd on the island of Jersey. There have also been cases in Ireland.

The French patient, who was immunocompromised, died earlier this month while infected with the virus, but it is unclear if the infection contributed to his death, the ECDC said in a statement.

Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death and how the infection was acquired are ongoing.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director of the World Health Organization (WHO) said in a statement on X that he was “in contact with French authorities, who are collecting information to better understand the source of infection.”

He added the patient was “immunocompromised, which made them more vulnerable to infection and severe disease.”

There was “no health risk to the general public identified at this time”, the French health and agriculture ministries said in a joint statement.

Dr Ben Brennan, Group Leader and Senior Lecturer, MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research, University of Glasgow, said: “This is an important scientific finding, as it is the first reported human infection with Shamonda virus [..] at present, there is no evidence that Shamonda virus causes widespread human disease, although further investigation is needed to understand its ability to infect people.”

In animals, Shamonda virus attacks the central nervous system and can lead to severe inflammation and haemorrhage. It can also lead to miscarriages.

Affected horses have been reported to exhibit seizures, lethargy, fever, muscle twitching, and difficulty walking.

Authorities are also still trying to ascertain whether the man himself was infected by a biting midge – the route of transmission between animals – or if he could have been infected by close contact with livestock.

It is thought he was infected in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating in midges and animals earlier in the year.

“Despite decades of circulation of the Shamonda virus in Africa and Asia, no human cases had been documented until now. This is therefore an exceptional case occurring in a severely immunocompromised patient,” French health authorities said in a statement.

The UK Plant and Health Agency said some of the neurological signs of the disease in horses resemble West Nile fever, human cases of which reached a record high on mainland Europe this year.

News.title: What happens when you get malaria during pregnancy?
News.content:
Huge strides have been made in recent years in combating malaria but one group is more at risk than ever before: pregnant women.

They are uniquely vulnerable to the disease and because sub-Saharan Africa shoulders the burden of global cases the continent’s rapidly growing population means far more women are exposed today than at the turn of the millennium.

According to a recent study, 52 million pregnant women in Africa face the threat of malaria each year, up from 37 million in 2000.

And the toll is heavy: malaria in pregnancy kills at least 10,000 mothers and 210,000 infants every year.

Malaria in pregnancy is uniquely dangerous, and the disease acts very differently to how it does in someone who is not pregnant.

“Pregnant women are one of the most vulnerable groups to malaria, it can lead to severe anaemia, immune suppression, and in the worst cases, mortality,” Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK told The Telegraph.

Malaria parasites infect and feed on red blood cells, dividing and multiplying in the bloodstream. This makes them easily detectable through a simple blood test, which allows life-saving treatment to be administered quickly.

But in pregnancy, the parasites are notoriously evasive.

Instead of floating in the bloodstream, they colonise in the placenta – the organ that feeds and sustains the baby.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal chief Edu lands new role at League Two side after move fails to work out
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal chief Edu lands new role at League Two side after move fails to work out

Edu's stint at Nottingham Forest ended prematurely with the ex-Arsenal chief now taking on a surprise advisory role at Northampton, who are second bottom of the Football League

View 2 Images Edu has secured a shock role near the bottom of the Football League

Former Arsenal sporting director Edu has landed himself a new role with Northampton Town, who are sitting 23rd in League Two.

‌



‌



The Brazilian was crucial in beginning the recent rise of the Gunners during his time at the Emirates, choosing to hire Mikel Arteta and then backing the Spaniard in the market. However he left north London to join Evangelos Marinakis‘ group of clubs, including Nottingham Forest, last year.

‌



That move has not worked out for Edu, who cited a desire to work in a multi-club model, and he was quickly moved on from the City Ground.

‌



He's since become a member of the board of directors at Bulgarian side Levski Sofia and will now combine that with becoming a senior advisor to Northampton - a role that was confirmed by the club's co-chair Joao Xavier.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Cobblers have recently been taken over by a Brazilian consortium including former Chelsea and AC Milan star Alexandre Pato. Xavier said an open forum on Thursday: “We are very proud to have Alex [Pato] with us and Edu with us too. We became friends as he had a role at Nottingham Forest and I asked him to help me learn more about English football.

“Edu is a senior advisor for one of our partners, acting as an advisor for Levski Sofia and also here, helping us navigate the sporting questions here at the club, not day to day, just when we ask him and when we need him.”

‌



Edu's decision to quit Arsenal came as a surprise to the club, who had become serial challengers for honours towards the end of his tenure. He presided over several landmark deals, including the club-record signing of Declan Rice from West Ham.

View 2 Images Northampton have won two of their 10 games this season

‌



Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Jurrien Timber were also signed under his watch as Arsenal morphed into one of the best teams in Europe. Their upward trajectory has continued despite his departure.

Now he faces new challenges, with clubs of a far lesser stature than Arsenal. It may only be early in the season but Northampton face the prospect of relegation to the National League. The club have jumped between the third and fourth tiers of the pyramid for years but haven't been a non-league outfit for more than a century.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Three punishments facing club as Kyle Walker forced to backpedal
Sports.content:
The latest news and updates on Manchester City's ongoing 114 financial charges case against the Premier League

Hello and welcome to the Manchester City 114 financial charges blog on Mirror Sport!

It has now been over a month since City were found guilty by an independent panel of all financial breaches brought forward by the Premier League.

The process of an appeal hearing and one for their potential sanctions have both started with City continuing to deny any wrongdoing. However, if the guilty verdict is upheld, there seems to be three likely punishments, which are a points deduction, a huge fine and immediate expulsion from the Premier League.

The stripping of titles seems unlikely with former player Kyle Walker part of the squad that won it all. He has spoken on a number of occasions about the charges, with his latest verdict clarifying a previous comment that caused controversy.

With all of that being said, stay with us throughout the day for all the latest news and updates...

Sports.title: Man Utd fans sent new stadium survey as 100,000-seater ground gathers pace
Sports.content:
Man Utd fans sent new stadium survey as 100,000-seater ground gathers pace

Manchester United fans will be consulted and have the chance to give their view on the club's new stadium as plans continue over a new venue for the club

View 2 Images Man Utd have signalled their plans to build a new 100,000-capacity stadium (Image: Foster and Partners / SWNS)

Manchester United will involve fans in a survey as they get the chance to feedback on the club's plans for a new 100,000-seater stadium, with concept images already being released.

The controversial ‘circus tent’ design is only an impression of what the finished venue could look like and the plans are not set in stone, and could still be influenced by what fans say.

Supporters have been invited to take part in a number of focus groups to discuss key details which could help decide on how the new state-of-the-art stadium takes shape.

The survey will be distributed to season ticket holders, cup season ticket holders, executive members, official members and supporters who have purchased hospitality within the last three years. It will close at 12pm on Friday November 6, reports The Sun.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Collette Roche, CEO, New Stadium Development, said: “Our proposed new stadium is one of the most significant projects Manchester United will undertake in the next 100 years, and it is vital that we shape it together with our fans.

“Above all else, this is a football stadium built for them, so getting the details right matters. We are committed to thorough and transparent engagement, ensuring supporters help inform key decisions on atmosphere, affordability, accessibility and the traditions that have made Old Trafford so special for so long.”

“By working together, we can create a world-class football stadium that supports success on the pitch, reflects the identity of Manchester United, and gives fans a home they can be proud of for generations to come.”

View 2 Images Man Utd fans will be given the chance to influence the new stadium

The club have also said there will be further opportunities for fans to provide their views on other major topics, one of those being pricing, which continues to be a hot topic after some controversial decisions taken by Ineos, who have removed concession prices.

Despite the obvious emotional attachment to Old Trafford it is well documented that the stadium, once renowned as one of Europe's best, has fallen well behind the standard set by the modern stadia. That owing to a continued lack of investment, but Ineos have looked to revamp the club's infrastructure, recently presiding over major improvements to the training ground.

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka delivers Arsenal huge injury blow as extent of thigh issue revealed
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka delivers Arsenal huge injury blow as extent of thigh issue revealed

Arsenal star Bukayo Saka could be out until December with a thigh injury sustained in Wednesday night's Champions League draw at Bayern Munich

View 2 Images Saka is set to be out until December (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Bukayo Saka has delivered Arsenal a huge blow and could be out until December with a thigh injury sustained in the Gunners' draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.

‌



‌



Saka is undergoing further scans on the injury which will determine the exact lay-off but Arsenal are already resigned to Saka being out for several weeks.

‌



The England star will also miss the Three Lions' Nations League fixtures next month including the group decider in Spain on November 15 after another massive setback.

‌



Incredibly, this is Saka’s 11th injury since September 2024 and is a huge blow for Arsenal’s title defence and Champions League games as he will be sweating on being ready to face Real Madrid at the Emirates on December 9.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He will definitely miss the Gunners' trip to Anfield on November 1. Manchester City travel to the Emirates on November 29 and it's the north London derby at Tottenham a week later.

Arteta said: “When a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, he's restricted to movement, they are not good signs.

‌



“He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury. We will know more probably tomorrow."

Arteta insisted he does not fear that Saka is suffering from burnout but admits that he has become a “different” player and he may be in danger of losing some of his robustness.

‌



View 2 Images Saka will miss England's Nations League fixtures in November (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Arteta said: “Well, it's certainly been different in the last year or so. Obviously the demands that we are putting to every player are immense.

‌



“The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

“So look at us now, we have to play on Sunday afternoon, then we have to go away, we have to play on Wednesday evening, then we have to play on Saturday. So you go less than 66, 67 hours between games.

‌



“On top of everything that we are putting, every hour is important. If they can support all the demands that we are putting to the players in that sense, that would be as well really appreciated from everybody.

“And I'm saying for every team as well, because we know what we are demanding from those players."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino winning fight to retain FIFA control as world tour reaps rewards
Sports.content:
The Gianni Infantino world tour has reaped rich rewards. Now we are looking at the very real prospect of Infantino being elected as FIFA president for a fourth and final term.

And at this rate, Infantino could even get back in unopposed as the deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18. The latest boost has come in the form of endorsement from the head of the Asian Football Confederation.

President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa Salman told the confederation's Congress in Tokyo - which was attended by Infantino - that "we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you as you seek a new mandate as president.”

That is a major U-turn by Sheikh Salman who just two months ago signed a joint letter with the heads of Uefa and Concacaf criticising Infantino over his failed World Cup sell-off plan.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Back then, the letter spelt out a damning indictment on “deception” and accused Infantino of a “profound failure of judgement... these are not the qualities football deserves in its leadership.”

But what was a clear change of direction and blow to the rebellion against Infantino, Sheikh Salman said it was time "to move forward”.

‌



Sheikh Salman said: “I've spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.

"Yes, we had some issues, we spoke about them in the past, but let's not relate the two things together. As one Asian family, we are ready to move forward, united in your support, Gianni."

Infantino has a strong power base in Africa and South America and therefore Sheikh Salman's endorsement could be crucial as it means the FIFA president has continents sewn up.

At the election in Rabat in March, Uefa will have 55 votes, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10.

‌



The deadline for candidates is looming but the only serious rival to Infantino to publicly declare is former Tottenham and Switzerland defender Ramon Vega.

Any candidate then needs the support of five national associations to make the ballot paper and Vega believes his campaign has the necessary backing.

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger had been touted as a potential replacement for Infantino (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

The clamour has been for Arsene Wenger to stand but there is no public suggestion he is ready to go head-to-head against Infantino. Just that people want him to.

‌



But here’s the thing. The reluctance from standing probably comes from the fact you cannot risk losing to Infantino. That would be damaging.

Infantino looked damaged beyond repair after the summer but has gone round the world on a charm offensive - and it appears to have worked, outside of UEFA of course.

Infantino has also proposed to increase the amount of money handed out for football development across the world by $3.4bn (£2.6bn).

Uefa has since told FIFA it must release key documents and answer all questions relating to its governance and decision-making by 2 November. But the reality is that Infantino is winning his fight.

‌

Sports.title: Antonio Conte issues statement to 'clarify position' on Man Utd job prospects
Sports.content:
Antonio Conte issues statement to 'clarify position' on Man Utd job prospects

Antonio Conte has posted a statement on social media hitting back at reports he's looking for control and major wages in his next job

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has spoken out against reports about his approach to his next move (Image: Getty Images)

Antonio Conte has come out and rubbished reports that he's making demands for full control during talks over his next job - with the Manchester United hotseat among those he's linked with.

‌



‌



The Italian is out of a job having left Napoli in the summer following two years in the role, winning the Scudetto in his debut season. His stellar CV boasts league titles with Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and the Naples outfit.

‌



All of which have seen him tipped to replace Michael Carrick if United, who have won just two games in 11 to begin the season, opt to make an early change.

‌



In previous roles, Conte has been accused of making major demands to those above, especially when it comes to recruitment and retention, with the Italian previously being outspoken when missing out on specific transfer targets, but the 57-year-old has rubbished those theories.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He said on his social media account: "Following recent media reports in Italy and abroad, I feel it is appropriate to clarify my position. My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage.

"Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

‌



"I have read reports of financial demand and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, ad well as reservations about what has been described as my 'strong personality'. These are reports are unfounded, as here is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

View 2 Images The Italian has never been shy of speaking his mind, calling out his bosses in previous roles (Image: JUSTIN TALLIS, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"Should a concrete opportunity arise that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager."

Conte's last job in England saw him axed by Tottenham after he took aim at the club for their continued failures. Prior to that he won the title at Chelsea and then delivered the FA Cup, but it was well documented that he missed out on several of his preferred players in his final summer.

Article continues below

The Italian has been linked with the role on the red half of Manchester previously but pundits have been split on whether he would be the right fit, especially given his relatively short stints in recent roles.

Sports.title: Football fans given chance to buy special shirts and support veterans during Poppy appeal
Sports.content:
Football fans given chance to buy special shirts and support veterans during Poppy appeal

From this weekend, football players across the UK will wear poppy emblems on their shirt and these will then be auctioned off.

View 2 Images England legend Terry Butcher is backing the initiative after his son, a veteran, died while suffering from PTSD. (Image: MatchWornShirt)

This autumn MatchWornShirt is proud to stand together with football clubs throughout the UK in support of the Royal British Legion’s Poppy Appeal.

‌



‌



As a symbol of respect, football clubs across the UK will wear shirts featuring an emblem of the poppy. After the matches, these unique shirts will be signed by the players who wore them and made available to own via auction, exclusively on the MWS website and app. The net proceeds of these auctions will go to the Royal British Legion.

‌



This is the eighth consecutive year that MWS has teamed up with the Royal British Legion, having raised well over £4m for the Poppy Appeal. The Royal British Legion’s Poppy Appeal takes place from Thursday 22 October until Armistice Day on Wednesday 11 November 2026; every year the RBL leads the nation in Remembrance across the UK to honour the contribution of our Armed Forces community, past and present.

‌



Since it was first worn as an act of Remembrance more than 100 years ago, the red poppy has become an enduring symbol of support for our Armed Forces. This year, the Royal British Legion’s Poppy Appeal highlights the fact that when someone serves, their family serves too, facing unique challenges and sacrifices alongside their loved one.

View 2 Images Chelsea are one of the clubs to be proudly displaying the poppy emblem on their shirts (Image: MatchWornShirt)

‌



Ben France, Head of Corporate Partnerships at the Royal British Legion, said: “When a partner or parent serves, they often spend months away at a time, missing birthdays, anniversaries and first days at school. The impact on family life is the top reason for serving personnel considering leaving their job.

"The RBL is there to support armed forces families during and after service, providing guidance during deployment, helping with financial hardship, support after a bereavement, or caring for a loved one in old age. By bidding in our annual shirt auction, you can help raise vital funds for the Royal British Legion to support the Armed Forces community for life.”

‌



James Flude, Head of Business at MWS, said: “The Royal British Legion’s Poppy Appeal is a powerful reminder of the sacrifices made by our Armed Forces community and their families, and we’re incredibly proud to support it for the eighth consecutive year. We’ve really seen our community get behind this partnership, and last year showed how much fans value these shirts.

"Salah’s Liverpool shirt against Aston Villa topped our 2025 Poppy Appeal auction, and Haaland’s appeared twice in the top five from Manchester City’s fixtures against Liverpool and Bournemouth. Even Elliott Anderson’s shirt from Forest’s game against Leeds went for over £5,800. Every shirt carries the poppy, and every bid helps ensure vital support continues for veterans and service personnel.”

Article continues below

Every donation to the RBL’s Poppy Appeal helps to provide vital support to the Armed Forces community and ensures their unique contribution is never forgotten.

Sports.title: Man Utd chief was axed over manager pick as ANOTHER civil war breaks out in boardroom
Sports.content:
Man Utd chief was axed over manager pick as ANOTHER civil war breaks out in boardroom

Manchester United's boardroom is once again divided over the club's next steps as a decision looms over the future of struggling manager Michael Carrick

View 3 Images Uncertainty over Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United is reportedly a factor in the club's latest 'civil war' (Image: Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick's current predicament at Old Trafford has led to a case of deja vu for Manchester United. Reports of 'civil war' in the boardroom are all too familiar for a team that found itself in a very similar situation not long ago.

‌



‌



United's struggles for on-field results have recently bled into the media via both players and Carrick himself. However, that feeling of discontent is seemingly not limited to the dressing room as those in the upper echelons allegedly clash, too.

‌



Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club's hierarchy for not doing enough in the transfer window following a recent Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid. Captain Bruno Fernandes then questioned Carrick's tactics following a 4-1 defeat at Como, leading to comments from the manager suggesting his players weren't working hard enough.

‌



The Daily Mail has now reported on a growing rift between director of football Jason Wilcox and head of recruitment Christopher Vivell. This is said to be largely in relation to whom the club should appoint as Carrick's successor if he is fired, which is exactly the kind of disagreement that previously led to a massive change at board level.

Erik ten Hag sent on immediate scouting mission in new role days after tearing Man Utd apart READ MORE :

Wilcox's predecessor, Dan Ashworth, also left the club under a cloud of controversy in December 2024. Ashworth arrived at Old Trafford to much excitement in the summer of that year, given his superb work in the same role at Newcastle.

However, United co-owners INEOS decided to part ways only five months into his tenure. The Athletic later reported this was at least partly down to indecision over whom should replace Erik ten Hag when he was sacked in October 2024.

‌



Ashworth was reported to have played a prominent role in Ten Hag's contract extension that year but supposedly had limited involvement in Ruben Amorim being appointed as his replacement. Instead, chief executive officer Omar Berrada took the reins in negotiating that appointment as a clear divide emerged.

3 View 3 Images United director of football Jason Wilcox was recently criticised by defender Lisandro Martinez (Image: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock) 3 View 3 Images Director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is reportedly in disagreement with Wilcox over whom should manage United next (Image: Ronny Hartmann / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

United paid £4.1million to terminate Ashworth's contract early, just one month after Amorim was appointed. It was viewed by fans as a terrible use of funds for a club that's grown too accustomed to waste in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era.

‌



Carrick will lead United out once again at home to Bournemouth on Sunday. However, there's no getting away from the sentiment it's a case of 'when' and not 'if' the club moves on, with the team failing to win any of its last seven games.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



As things stand, a number of potential successors have been bandied about at United. Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are each reported as candidates, helped by the fact they're all currently free agents without a club.

A new manager won't rid United of that feeling of disharmony at boardroom level, however. And while Carrick's job is the main talking point up for discussion at Old Trafford, it may not be long before other changes are made among the hierarchy, too.

Sports.title: Rodgers' magnificent obsession lands in Paris
Sports.content:
A book on the shelf behind Aaron Rodgers is entitled 'A Magnificent Obsession', to which he sees the irony-meets-humour in relation to his own NFL love affair.

It is the game he cannot say goodbye to, but one he will say goodbye to at the end of this season, which he has insisted shall be the last of his stellar Hall of Fame career.

Just moments earlier Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy had been asked about the difference in the Rodgers of now compared to the Rodgers with whom he had worked and won a Super Bowl in Green Bay. More grey hairs was the first answer.

But at the age of 42 Rodgers will lead the Steelers out as a prized attraction when they face the New Orleans Saints in the NFL's historic Paris debut at Stade de France on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Phoebe Schecter has been impressed by the Pittsburgh Steelers' ability to keep winning despite below-par performances, with Aaron Rodgers continuing to lead the way

Live NFL Sunday 25th October 1:00pm

"To steal a line from one of my all-time favourite movies, 'Obsession is a young man's game'," Rodgers told Sky Sports.

"And the NFL is the young man's game. I'm hanging on and enjoying this last one."

So often the four-time MVP has likened his latter years to being on the proverbial 'back nine' of his NFL career, continuing to ride the highs and lows of a game that hasn't always fallen in his favour.

"I think I'm on the 18th green!" he laughed."

Rodgers has thrown for a ninth-most 1,487 yards and 12 touchdowns to five interceptions across Pittsburgh's 4-2 start to the season, having been reunited with former Packers coach McCarthy following Mike Tomlin's exit. His quest to win an elusive second Super Bowl ring may not have materialised as planned, but he is at peace with what awaits at the end of his 22nd campaign.

"I've given a lot to this game, the game has given me a lot in return. I've got zero qualms about this being the end, zero fears about what's next. I'm just trying to live in the moment and enjoy this time with these guys."

Rodgers has long embraced opportunities to reach different corners of the world through football, last year being a leading advocate for Pittsburgh's historic appearance in Dublin and now preparing to be part of another milestone for the NFL in France.

"There's definitely only one moment in France," he said. "I'm going to enjoy this for the next couple of days. It's fun to be out here.

"It's fun to be a part of the first. As you get older you don't get a lot of firsts. To be in the first game in Paris is special.

He and the Steelers landed in the French capital on just Friday morning following a red-eye flight from Pittsburgh, while the Saints came into town on Monday as the designated home team.

"I've played in three countries now, and each of them we've left on Thursday early evening. Would have been nice one time to come over on a Monday," he said.

Sports.title: Raskin 'really happy' at Rangers but unsure about future
Sports.content:
The Belgium international looked set to leave Ibrox in the summer; he is under contract until 2028; Raskin scored in Rangers' 2-2 draw at Dundee in their last Scottish Premiership match; they host St Johnstone on Saturday

Nicolas Raskin is "really happy" at Rangers but is unsure about what the future holds for him.

It was widely believed that the 25-year-old midfielder, who signed from Standard Liege in January 2023, would move on after being part of the Belgium side that reached the quarter-final of the 2026 World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual winners Spain.

However, after missing a few games amid speculation about his future, Raskin has become a mainstay in Derek McInnes' side.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nicolas Raskin produced an outrageous strike against Dundee

Asked if he had expected to leave in the summer, he replied: "Of course, when you're an ambitious player, you want to keep going higher and higher and higher, so I thought there was a point where maybe I could try to go and get a new challenge after the World Cup.

"But like I said, I've never been pushing for something because I'm really happy here, it's a big club.

"This club helped me to join the Belgian national team, which is a big thing. So I'm really calm with that.

"If something comes and everybody would be happy with it, then I would have looked to see if I could do it or not. But I don't need to push anything.

Sports.title: Doyle: O'Brien to scoop Futurity prize with Noble Exhibit
Sports.content:
As our ambassador Hollie Doyle gets closer to her comeback following a five-month injury lay-off, she looks ahead to some exciting action on Sky Sports Racing from Doncaster this weekend.

Lucky 13 for O'Brien in Futurity

It looks like being a lucky 13th for master trainer Aidan O'Brien in the William Hill Futurity Trophy Stakes (1.30) at Doncaster on Saturday - live on Sky Sports Racing.

The Ballydoyle maestro heads the market with NOBLE EXHIBIT, who will be partnered by Ryan Moore in his pursuit of a first Group 1.

The son of Frankel looks the perfect type for this end-of-season assignment following his impressive win in the Group 2 Beresford Stakes at The Curragh - like the Futurity, a traditional pointer to next season's Classics.

He coped well with the yielding ground that day so the soft conditions on Town Moor shouldn't be an issue for the handsome chestnut.

Burke rightly bullish about Burning

Karl Burke has been bullish in his assessment of Noble Exhibit's most dangerous rival Burning Up, who confirmed his liking for soft ground when defying a penalty in a Haydock Park novice before going close in better company at Newmarket.

His second to O'Brien's more experienced Haffner in the Group 2 Royal Lodge can be upgraded as he just got caught out in the dip before running on strongly. This more conventional track should be ideal for him to cement his own classic credentials.

Godolphin have obvious claims with the jet-setting Al Hudaiba, who won a Grade 1 in Canada last month after taking the Superlative Stakes at Newmarket in the summer. He's quirky though and doesn't appeal to me as much as his market rivals.

Tiger to roar home in Listed sprint

BENGAL TIGER will be hard to beat in the Listed William Hill Remembering Sue Wright Prospect Stakes (2.05) at Doncaster. Better known as the Doncaster Stakes, this 6f sprint for two-year-olds is the ideal stepping stone for the son of No Nay Never who won his maiden as Naas by an incredible 12 lengths.

This race looks set to be dominated by the Irish with Paddy Twomey's Hi Corbett Court proving his liking for testing ground when beating all but a better-fancied stable companion in a valuable sales race at The Curragh.

Richard and Peter Fahey take them on with Crystal Queen who was second in an Ayr nursery after struggling in Group races in the summer but she needs to take a big step forward.

State ready to supplement festival win

Adam Kirby has his team in fine form and I'm expecting ANCIENT STATE to supplement his course and distance win at the Leger Festival in the Richard James Hone Memorial Handicap (12.55) at Doncaster.

The four-year-old has run well in Class 2 company since last month's success and will definitely enjoy the ease in the ground with a relatively light weight to shoulder.

Mick Appleby's Al Shabab Storm went close in the Portland at this track before chasing home his highly progressive stable mate Coul Angel at York and gets on well with talented 5lb claimer Harry Vigors. He's a big player but has to give a lot of weight to Ancient State.

Chapple-Hyam gelding value for repeat success

DESPERATE DAN won the William Hill Epic Boosts Handicap (3.19) at Doncaster last year off the very same mark and has what it takes to follow up for his shrewd trainer Peter Chapple-Hyam.

Lightly raced this year, he's got his ground and should be sharpened up by the addition of blinkers with top northern jockey Paul Mulrennan doing the steering.

Ralph Beckett's Shipbourne benefitted from more positive tactics on the All-Weather at Southwell last month and could build on that back at the scene of his 7f win at the track in the summer.

Ground ideal for Channon contender

Jack Channon does well in competitive handicaps and has a live contender in the William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap (3.55) at Doncaster with GALYX.

He bolted up at Beverley in soft ground off a 5lb lower rating and this track will suit him just as well. Off 85 he's still well within his range to win again off a relatively low weight.

I also like Michael Bell's proven soft ground performer A Major Payne who won nicely at Goodwood and still looks quite progressive.

Comeback date edges ever closer

My return to race riding edges ever closer following another positive week of training and riding out on the gallops in Lambourn and Newmarket.

I'm still firmly focused on making my comeback in early November, five and a half months after breaking my left leg in that horrible fall at Bath in May.

I've been stepping up my rehabilitation at Oaksey House in Lambourn but nothing beats being back in the saddle and I'm enjoying getting back on a horse at my boss Archie Watson's Saxon Gate Stables.

I don't have an exact date for my return but once I've had my BHA fitness test next week I should know more. It's been a long, difficult road but I'm so excited to be getting back to what I'm so passionate about.

Sports.title: Carrick delivers 5min 27sec monologue and says he will hold brolly to keep everyone dry
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick began his Friday media conference with an extraordinary 5min 27sec monologue that cited Manchester United’s values of “humility”, “resilience” and “earning the right to win” in what could be read as a public address to his players after the season’s dismal start.

The head coach, whose job is under threat, later stated “100%” he could turn United’s form around and sought to underline his selfless attitude by saying he would hold an umbrella for “everyone else to stay dry” while he got wet.

The downpour on Carrick intensified on Wednesday when Bruno Fernandes questioned his tactics after a 4-1 Champions League loss at Como and the 45-year-old did not rule out dropping the midfielder or stripping him of the captaincy when Bournemouth visit on Sunday. “I’ll always do what’s best for the football club,” he said. “The most important thing for me is the team, first and foremost – the squad, the dynamics in the squad.”

Carrick decided to make his speech, delivered without being asked a question, after events in Como and Lisandro Martínez’s criticism of Jason Wilcox a week earlier for the director of football’s recruitment.

United have won only two of 11 games and are 13th in the Premier League. Carrick said: “We need to respect what it takes to be here, respect what it takes to win, what you have to do to win. I’m not entitled to be here. Entitlement cannot be at this football club. We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean that you’re entitled to just win.”

Carrick, a highly decorated United player for 12 years until 2018, cited two of his former teammates. “Ryan Giggs, arguably one of the greatest to play for this club, it was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United. Wayne Rooney was top goalscorer of this football club. His biggest thing was playing for the team, sacrificing for the team, and what was good for Manchester United.

“Sir Alex Ferguson, the best manager of all time, the greatest for me … his main priority was Manchester United. Going back to Sir Matt [Busby], Sir Bobby [Charlton], the resilience was beyond belief of what they showed and the way they rebuilt this football club [after the Munich disaster of 1958].”

Carrick insisted he could embody these values and transform United’s campaign. “One hundred per cent, yeah,” he said, before confirming he had spoken to the hierarchy and players about the crisis.

“There’s always conversations going on. It’s pretty obvious how we’re all feeling. The responsibility for me to be in this position is to lead.”
