Pro-Lula demonstrations in cities across the country have attracted millions of people, helping galvanise the president’s voters and cut into Bolsonaro’s lead. Bolsonaro has held his own rallies, hoping to capitalise on momentum and consolidate support from other conservative parties.

The two candidates held a combative debate on October 18, exchanging insults and accusing each other of corruption.

Questions of outside intervention have also been a theme in the campaign’s closing days, with US social media giant Meta facing allegations that it restricted pro-Lula activity online in a bid to support Bolsonaro.

Concerns about foreign interference, in particular from the US, have loomed over the campaign since the beginning.

The Trump administration has repeatedly sought to intervene in Brazilian politics, previously introducing steep tariffs and penalties against judicial officials in a bid to have the case against the elder Bolsonaro tossed out and mirroring rhetoric on the Brazilian right to cast doubt on the reliability of the country’s voting system.

Trump has himself used false claims of widespread fraud to ignore unfavourable election results, and observers have expressed concern that the US could throw its support behind Bolsonaro based on such claims even if he were to lose the race.

What do polls show?

After his victory in the first round, Bolsonaro emerged as the race’s de facto frontrunner. But polls continue to show a close race, with Lula cutting into Bolsonaro’s lead but continuing to trail within the margin of error.

Speculation that Bolsonaro might pull ahead decisively following the first round, after other conservative candidates failed to advance to the run-off, has not yet appeared in new polls.

A Nexus poll released on Monday showed Bolsonaro winning 46.5 percent of the vote in the second round, with Lula taking 45.9 percent. A poll from the previous week had shown Bolsonaro with 47.9 percent and Lula with 45.1 percent.

Another poll by AtlasIntel and Bloomberg, also released on Monday, showed Bolsonaro with 49.8 percent versus 47.6 percent for Lula. An October 9 poll had shown Bolsonaro with 51.1 percent and Lula with 45.7.



A Quaest poll released on October 21 showed Bolsonaro’s lead continuing to drop, with Lula winning 44 percent and Bolsonaro 45 percent.

World.title: Conte dismisses reports of Man United takeover with Carrick’s job uncertain
World.content:
Former Chelsea and Napoli coach Antonio Conte said he was not in advanced negotiations to replace Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, and called reports that he had demanded full control at the club “unfounded”.

Conte, who won the Premier League with Chelsea and also managed Tottenham Hotspur in England, was responding to speculation that he had requested full control while also making financial demands of the struggling Old Trafford club.

United sit 13th in the Premier League and 20th in the Champions League standings following Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 thrashing by Italian side Como, increasing scrutiny on Carrick.

“My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage,” Conte said in a statement.

“Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management,” he added, referring to his time in Naples where he won Serie A in the 2024-25 season.

“It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

“I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my ‘strong personality’.

“These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.”

Conte only interest in concrete opportunity with Man United

Conte, who last coached Napoli in the 2025-26 season, said that if a concrete opportunity arose, he would enter talks with the club involved and “jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement”, taking into account the needs of both parties.



“Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact,” the 57-year-old Italian added.

In an interview with The Athletic earlier this month, Conte said he would like to manage a club that has “lost sight of their history” so he can help “make it shine once more”.

Defeat against Como extended United’s winless run to seven games in all competitions, and skipper Bruno Fernandes said his team had adopted a “mood of defeat” while also questioning the tactics, with Carrick apologising for the performance.

Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, another name linked with the United job, also distanced himself from the speculation on Friday.

The 33-year-old, England’s youngest top-flight manager, said he was focused solely on Brighton, who sit third in the Premier League after a string of impressive performances.

“I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days and, beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and what he has done with Manchester United the last season,” Hurzeler told a news conference.

“He’s a great human being, a great personality. There’s nothing more to say about that.”

Brighton’s free-scoring start to the Premier League season has seen Hurzeler touted as a possible successor should United make a mid-season managerial change for the third consecutive campaign.

The Seagulls sit third in the table, behind only Manchester City and champions Arsenal, before Sunday’s trip to Liverpool.

“I am really focused on my job here. I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days,” said the 33-year-old German.

Brighton’s scoring streak came to an end in a 0-0 draw at Czech side Jablonec in the Europa League on Thursday.

Despite an excellent start to the campaign, which also includes coming from 2-0 down to beat United 3-2 at Old Trafford in the League Cup last month, Hurzeler believes his side can still improve.

“There is still improvements we can do, still a lot of potential to get out of the players, and therefore I really want to work on that together with my players, together with my staff,” he said.

“I have great experts around me. I have a great group of players who support me, who give everything for this club, and we built this over the last years.

“We had tough periods, we have good periods, but I think to build these kind of relationships, you need time, you need connections, and you don’t take these things for granted.”

World.title: Mississippi releases video of 1-year-old’s fatal police shooting
World.content:
NewsFeed Mississippi releases video of 1-year-old’s fatal police shooting

Mississippi released bodycam footage of the fatal shooting of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley, who was in a moving car when a police officer on a shoplifting call opened fire. The officer was cleared of criminal wrongdoing, but the boy’s family says the shooting was unjustified.

World.title: Finland nearing opening of world’s first permanent nuclear waste repository
World.content:
Facilities are being built in many countries, but Finland is the first to licence its underground storage facility.

Finland has granted an operating licence for the world’s first permanent underground repository for spent nuclear fuel.

The government handed Onkalo, in western Finland, the licence on Thursday, waste management company Posiva said.

Although the move does not allow the opening of the facility, it is expected to start operations soon, the firm said. However, 22 years after construction began, no exact date has been decided yet.

“This is a great and historic day for both Posiva and Finland,” the company’s Chief Executive Officer Ilkka Poikolainen said in a statement.

“Before final disposal begins, Posiva will finalise the commissioning stage, carrying out the necessary tests and inspections which STUK [the Finnish Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority] also needs to verify and approve.”

With space for 6,500 tonnes of uranium, Onkalo, which means “cave” in Finnish, will provide permanent storage for spent fuel from Finland’s five nuclear reactors.

The fuel will be enclosed in copper canisters that are highly resistant to corrosion inside the geological repository. The canisters will then be lowered into holes drilled into the bedrock, which will be filled with bentonite clay and finally sealed with a steel-reinforced concrete plug.

The waste will remain highly radioactive for tens of thousands of years. After about 100,000 years, the levels will be about the same as the uranium ore of which the fuel is made, according to Posiva.

Countries have been wrestling with what to do with dangerous nuclear by-products since the first plants were built in the 1950s. Currently, most of it is in temporary storage.



Final repositories are being built in other countries, including neighbouring Sweden and France, but Finland is expected to be the first to open its underground storage facility.

The cost of the Onkalo site has been estimated at $1.16bn.

World.title: Dembele to miss Ballon d’Or event as PSG game moved amid protests in France
World.content:
Paris Saint-Germain’s game has been postponed following a request by police amid a wave of violent protests in France.

Share Dembele to miss Ballon d’Or event as PSG game moved amid protests in France on social media

Paris Saint-Germain’s home Ligue 1 game against Lyon scheduled for this Sunday has been postponed until Monday, the French league announced, following a request by police amid a wave of violent protests in the French capital.

The decision means the reigning Ballon d’Or, Ousmane Dembele, will miss Monday’s awards ceremony in London, for which he and a number of his PSG teammates have been nominated.

The 29-year-old French international forward was once again among the favourites to win the award, having helped his nation to the FIFA World Cup 2026 semifinals while leading PSG to their defence of the UEFA Champions League crown.

“The LFP takes note of the police decree prohibiting the staging of the game between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais on Sunday at 8:45 pm [19:45 GMT] … and has decided to reschedule the match for Monday at 8:30 pm,” the French league said in a statement on Friday.

French authorities are braced for another weekend of protests in Paris and across the country, after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago.

Defending champion PSG and Lyon were level on 14 points at the top of Ligue 1 heading into this weekend’s eighth round of games

Monday’s match will clash with the Ballon d’Or awards ceremony in London, where several PSG players are on the men’s shortlist: holder Dembele of France, Morocco’s Achraf Hakimi, Georgia’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Brazil’s Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, and Vitinha of Portugal, Willian Pacho of Ecuador, and Fabian Ruiz and Ferran Torres of Spain.



French officials will mount a “massive” security operation for protests planned on Saturday, with troops reinforcing police, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Tuesday, after rioting and looting swept through Paris and other French cities on October 17.

The PSG-Lyon game is among several high-profile sporting events scheduled in the French capital area this weekend.

The Pittsburgh Steelers are due to face the New Orleans Saints in an NFL regular-season game at the Stade de France on Sunday, an event expected to require a significant police deployment.

Separately, Toulouse’s Ligue 1 home match against Troyes has already been pushed back from Saturday to Sunday at the request of local authorities, the LFP said on Wednesday.

World.title: Deadly shooting near Paris investigated as 'crime of terrorism', minister says
World.content:
One person has been killed and five others wounded - three seriously - in a gun attack in a Parisian suburb which authorities are investigating as "terrorism".

Several drive-by shootings took place on Friday - first in Trappes to the south-west of Paris, and then in nearby La VerriÃ¨re. The rampage lasted almost 15 minutes, said Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez. A12-year-old girl is among the wounded.

The suspected attacker has been arrested. The motive remains unclear, but the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) said the incident appeared to be "murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise".

NuÃ±ez told reporters in Trappes: "It's clearly a terrorist crime, that's what [the prosecutor] has said."

The Mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, said that "an individual fired shots from his vehicle at several people he encountered" on Friday morning.

The gunman drove through several neighbourhoods in a grey Renault Clio, according to witnesses. Rabeh said he had "fired randomly" with the seeming intent of causing "as many casualties as possible... he wanted to cause carnage", he said.

The mayor said people had been targeted at a petrol station, a medical centre and a playground in Trappes before the attacker had driven on to nearby La VerriÃ¨re.

A police union official said the suspect had been detained in La VerriÃ¨re on the main N10 road that runs through the town.

World.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
World.content:
Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, after gunmen opened fire on a church, officials have said.

At least 34 others were injured in the church in the village of Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday.

The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing, in what government spokesperson Dr al-Momani Mohammad described as a "heinous attack".

Jordan's King Abdullah II said the authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties."

Dozens of people had been inside the church for the funeral when the shooting began, Khaled Burqan, one of the mourners, told Jordan's al-Mamlaka state-run TV.

He said two attackers armed with a rifle and a pistol had been firing at the mourners for several minutes.

In a news conference, Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya described the incident as a "terrorist" act carried out by a "group of extremists" and said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators.

He added that the incident was "painful and horrific" and "unparalleled in the history of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan".

No-one has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.

World.title: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
World.content:
The incident has already begun to influence the ongoing election campaign, with Netanyahu - who has built his campaign on the promise of security - saying that his Likud party would cancel campaign events which had been set for Friday morning.

Speaking later from the scene, Netanyahu said that the military would "demolish this place and completely transform it," referring to the Hebron neighbourhood where the attackers are said to have come from.

It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.

Netanyahu likened his plans to previous operations in West Bank refugee camps where residential buildings were demolished and thousands were displaced.

He also said he had reviewed plans for the largest military operation in the West Bank in decades - though did not say when it could be carried out.

He added that he had imposed cordons around the city of Hebron - which has around 200,000 residents - and the nearby city of Halhul.

Netanyahu's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for Israel to launch a campaign in the West Bank "exactly like in Gaza or Lebanon," while far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for Israel to dismantle the Palestinian Authority.

On Thursday, Foreign Minister Israel Katz accused opposition leaders of undermining the government by criticising Netanyahu's warnings of an attack ahead of the election, saying they would be "responsible" for any future attack on the country.

Opposition chiefs, including frontrunner Gadi Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, offered their condolences to the families of the killed troops and praised those who killed the attackers.

The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers' vehicle, and that they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint - so instead decided to open fire there.

At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN.

Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says - not including those killed in Friday's attack.

World.title: White House says Melania Trump brokers truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
World.content:
Last month, some of the remaining Oleshky residents told the BBC harrowing accounts of how they were surviving in the city that was being constantly shelled and cut off from food and water.

They said that children remaining in wider Oleshky were suffering from malnutrition, a lack of medical services and were "degrading" without access to education.

Many also told the BBC there was only one hospital partially operational, opening a few days a week to perform critical amputations.

The local population was living under a "full blockade" by Russian forces, according to Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.

Ukraine says it has attempted to deliver supplies to the area but has not had success in recent months.

The Kremlin in September acknowledged that Oleshky was facing "a critical situation" and "problems with supplies of food and medicine", but added that "Russia's military was working to resolve them" and blamed Kyiv.

Oleshky is trapped between the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and Russian forces.

The city was home to 24,000 people before Russia's full-scale invasion. Now Ukraine estimates that some 6,000 people remain in the city and its surrounding areas, including 200 children.

While the US first lady is relatively lower profile than some of her predecessors - and only occasionally seen at White House events - she has become involved in addressing humanitarian issues stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war.

In August 2025, Melania Trump penned a letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin, telling him it was "time to protect children and future generations worldwide".

Although she did not mention Ukraine by name, just days later at the White House Zelensky handed over a letter from his wife Olena, thanking her for her efforts on children.

In a rare public appearance in October the same year, the US first lady said that Putin had answered directly in writing and that her representatives were working with the Russian president's team to repatriate Ukrainian children from Russia and vice versa.

Some 34 children have reportedly been returned since 2025, including five this July.

According to US President Donald Trump, his wife has also privately expressed scepticism about Putin and his desire to achieve peace.

"I'd get home, I'd say, 'First lady, I had the most wonderful talk with Vladimir. I think we're finished'," Trump said in July last year.

"And then I'll turn on the television, or she'll say to me one time, 'Wow, that's strange because they just bombed a nursing home'."

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
World.content:
Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits had been reversed by Elon Musk who owns the satellite system.

The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations.

The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had "put it back".

Asked on Friday, Trump said: "If there is a problem, I will get it straightened out."

Trump added: "I have not spoken to him. I might have to, but I have not. I've heard it was fixed, but if it's not, I'll speak to him."

Musk previously said he was not behind the slowdown, which affected Ukraine's ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations.

Trump told reporters he did not think the tech billionaire had too much power.

The Ukrainian defence ministry sources said the military was constantly monitoring the performance of both the Starlink and Starshield networks.

They added that there was "currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted".

Last week, Kyiv said uplink speeds to the low Earth orbit satellites had been restricted, affecting the speed at which drones could travel. Any drone travelling faster than 100mph lost its connection, officials said.

Shortly after, Musk said that Starshield, which Ukraine uses for some of its operation, was controlled by the US military and suggested that the Pentagon could be behind the issues.

The White House has since repeatedly denied deliberately placing limits on the network in Ukraine.

World.title: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
World.content:
An oil spill from a tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz is spreading along the United Arab Emirates (UAE) coastline, forcing the closure of some beaches and coastal areas.

Satellite images from Monday show the beginnings of the oil spill from a ship matching the location and dimensions of Gem No.2, which was damaged between 9 and 10 October during a record surge of vessel strikes by Iran.

The slick of oil had spread more than 35km (22 miles) from the tanker by Wednesday, the satellite imagery showed.

UAE authorities said on Thursday that the incident is affecting beaches near the northern city of Umm Al Quwain and verified video from Friday shows the oil washing ashore, colouring the water black.

World.title: Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn
World.content:
Mink farming will end in Denmark by August 2029 after the government decided to drop plans to pursue an exemption to an EU-wide ban on the practice.

Denmark was once the largest producer of mink fur in the world, but the industry has declined due to global bans on fur farming, a decline in the fur trade and an earlier outbreak of a Covid strain in the nation's mink population.

The ban is due to come into effect on 7 August next year, and is followed by a two-year transition period to phase out the practice.

Danish Nature Minister Christian Rabjerg Madsen said the government had chosen animal welfare.

"A business should not continue just because it has existed for a long time. It should also make sense for society, for the economy and for the animals," he said.

The Danish government had initially sought an exemption for its mink industry when the EU added the mammal to its list of invasive species in 2025, prohibiting people from keeping them.

However, the current coalition government, elected in June, reversed this decision and decided not to proceed with the application on Friday.

Social Democrat MP Brigitte Vind said it was "a good day for animal welfare".

"It is absolutely the right decision not to apply for a special scheme for mink breeding in Denmark," she said.

The Danish Mink Association, which represents breeders, has been approached for comment.

Denmark is one of the few European countries to still produce mink fur, one of the more common pelts used in making fur garments.

However, its production has slipped behind that of other countries, such as Poland and China, in recent years.

The industry faced a crisis during the coronavirus pandemic, when the government ordered a mass cull of mink after a mutated strain of Covid-19 was found in the animals. Approximately 15 million were killed.

At the time, the country had huge export markets to China and Hong Kong. The government later admitted it had no legal basis for the culling.

There are now approximately 15,000 mink left in Denmark.

No costs have yet been determined for closing Denmark's seven remaining mink farms, but an animal welfare spokesperson for one of the governing coalition parties previously estimated it would be around 14m Danish krone (Â£1.56m), local media report, but the final amount could be higher.

The wearing of fur is a controversial subject within fashion circles, with publications and fashion brands choosing not to use or promote it several years ago.

But it re-entered the spotlight last year, with celebrities and fashionistas wearing both vintage and so-called faux fur.

World.title: PSG v Lyon moved as Paris prepares for more protests
World.content:
Paris St-Germain's Ligue 1 match against Lyon has been pushed back 24 hours to Monday as the French capital prepares for another weekend of protests.

The fixture at the Parc des Princes in Paris had been scheduled to kick off at 19:45 GMT on Sunday but will instead take place at 20:30 on Monday.

The Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP) announced the postponement in a statement, external on Friday after French police prohibited the fixture from taking place on its original date.

French authorities are preparing a major security operation for demonstrations planned for Saturday.

Around 550,000 people took part in demonstrations last Saturday to protest rising fuel prices, education standards and the cost of living, which have escalated after weeks of student protests.

Marches took place in several major French cities, including Paris, backed by unions and student groups, and were marred by some incidents of violence, looting and destruction.

The security challenge is further complicated by Sunday's NFL match between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, an event expected to require a significant police deployment.

The game will be played in Saint-Denis, about 10km from Place de la Bastille, where the protests are expected to begin.

The disruptions have already affected France's domestic football schedule with Toulouse's Ligue 1 home game against Troyes moved from Saturday to Sunday at the request of authorities.

Reigning French and European champions PSG are second in the standings after seven matches, while Lyon lead the table on 14 points, ahead of the holders on goal difference.

The match will also now be played on the same day as the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London.

Injured PSG pair Ousmane Dembele, the 2025 winner, and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are among the contenders for the award.

World.title: Ebola: FG orders strict screening at Nigeria’s entry points
World.content:
The federal government has directed relevant agencies and health institutions to strictly enforce Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) screening and other entry protocols at Nigeria’s designated points of entry following reports of non-compliance with approved measures.

The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following concerns raised by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) over reported breaches of the government-approved protocols.

The directive was contained in a circular dated 22 October and signed by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, on behalf of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate.

The ministry said consistent and non-discriminatory enforcement of the protocols was necessary to reduce the risk of cross-border transmission and protect public health and national security.

Screening, surveillance

Under the directive, relevant ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs), health institutions and other stakeholders are required to comply with prescribed Ebola screening, health declaration, surveillance and other applicable entry requirements.

The ministry also called for stronger coordination, communication, and information sharing among the institutions responsible for implementing the measures.

It said these efforts would support effective disease surveillance, early detection and prompt responses to potential public health threats.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The directive comes as Nigerian health authorities respond to a confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), involving a woman who recently arrived in the country from Uganda.

The authorities have also begun contact tracing to identify people who may have been exposed to the virus.

Reporting breaches

The ministry directed relevant institutions to document and report any actual or attempted breaches of the approved protocols promptly through established channels.

It also urged them to support officials responsible for enforcing the measures and to establish monitoring and accountability mechanisms to sustain compliance.

The ministry stressed that personnel responsible for enforcement should be allowed to perform their duties professionally and without undue interference.

It further directed the immediate, widespread circulation of the advisory to relevant departments, units, field offices, and personnel to ensure they understood their responsibilities.

All concerned MDAs were instructed to treat the directive as a priority, promptly address identified lapses, and maintain compliance with the approved entry protocols.

The ministry said the measures were intended to safeguard public health and national safety.

World.title: First HoldCo’s nine-month profit leaps 63% to N744.5 billion
World.content:
First HoldCo Plc logged a 65.1 per cent rise in net profit in the first nine months of 2026, relative to the same period of last year, according to its latest unaudited results issued on Friday, boosted by a general improvement across its income sources

The financial services group posted the strong results as gross earnings climbed to N2.9 trillion from N2.7 trillion a year ago, thanks to increased contribution of its commercial banking business to its revenue pool.

The commercial banking division accounted for 94 per cent of turnover and 87.4 per cent of post-tax profit.

Net interest income, the difference between the interest banks earn on interest-bearing assets and what they pay depositors and account holders, fell 16 per cent to N1.3 trillion.

Interest expense as a percentage of interest income rose to 39.8 per cent from 34.5 per cent a year ago, indicating increased cost pressure on net interest income.

The banking group set aside N207.1 billion to cover impaired assets, 28.3 per cent lower than the amount it provisioned for the same purpose in the corresponding period of last year.

Net fee and commission advanced 48.1 per cent to N316.4 billion, driven by improved financial advisory fees and higher income from brokerage and intermediation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The performance also benefited from a 19.9 per cent surge in foreign exchange gains and a 26 per cent rise in net gains on the sale of investment securities.

Also boosting profit, First HoldCo posted N104.6 billion in net gains from financial instruments at FVTPL, up from a N72.8 billion loss a year ago.

Other operating income expanded by nearly sixfold to N142.1 billion.

Beyond improved income generation, the strong results also benefited from cost-cutting measures.

The banking group cut personnel expenses by 3.4 per cent and other operating expenses by 12.8 per cent, largely by reducing spending on advertising and corporate promotions.

Profit before tax rose 60.8 per cent to N566.5 billion, while profit after tax rose to N744.5 billion from N450.9 billion.

Total assets rose to N32.2 trillion from N27.3 trillion as of the end of last year.

In July, First HoldCo’s board of directors announced a policy to pay at least 60 per cent of the group’s profit after tax as annual dividends.

The financial institution said the move highlights its directors’ confidence in its earnings capacity, enhanced capital position, improving asset quality, diversified revenue streams, and robust outlook for sustained profitability and growth

World.title: Nigeria NOW! opens its project boardrooms to global investors in Abuja
World.content:
Platinum group metals, gold, nickel, copper, lithium and rare earth elements lie together in one mineral province in Kaduna State, which the Minister of Solid Minerals Development announced in June as world-class and the Nigerian Geological Survey Agency has verified. The Ministry opens its doors to global investors at Nigeria NOW!, held at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja on 19 and 20 November.

Processing is following the discoveries, as lithium facilities of $600m in Nasarawa State and $200m near Abuja sit alongside a $400m rare earth processing project in Nasarawa, and mining lease applicants must now submit value-addition plans. Annual mining revenue has risen from about N6bn before the current administration to more than N70bn by the end of 2025.

The routes to export markets are moving too, as the Federal Executive Council has approved deep seaports at Bakassi and Ondo as public-private partnerships, with the Bakassi port alone valued at $2.27bn.

With a month to go, investors and developers travelling to Abuja will meet these projects at close quarters. In investor boardrooms, the Government of Nigeria will review specific projects in depth, from large-scale infrastructure to multilateral programmes such as Mission 300.

Speaking to Energy News Network in September, Tunde Arisekola, Senior Advisor, Geological and Minerals Information at the African Minerals Development Centre, who joins the minerals session on the first day, said that “first and foremost all international investors coming to Abuja should understand that Nigeria is ready and open for business”. In the same interview he described Nigeria’s economy as “stable, safe, peaceful and welcoming to all international investors”.

The programme opens with a welcome from the Chief Host, H.E. Dr Oladele Henry Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, followed by sessions on how the Ministry of Power will drive capacity into Nigeria’s industrial hubs and on the policies opening the minerals sector to foreign investment, including domestic processing and value addition. The second day turns to the pipeline of transport and port infrastructure and the $1bn Domestic Green Bond, and closes with an investors’ clinic on the 2025 Tax Act.

Lagos State Government, a Nigeria NOW! partner, now regulates its own electricity market after NERC transferred oversight to the Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission. Hon. Biodun Ogunleye, Lagos State Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, told Energy News Network that “capital follows bankable cashflows”. The state’s job, he said, is “to create both the infrastructure plan and the commercial architecture that makes that plan financeable”.

On Friday 20 November, YES! Nigeria runs alongside the main programme under the theme “Empowering Today’s Entrepreneurs, Building Tomorrow’s Industrialists”. Abuja University and Philomath University are partners, and the Youth Sustainable Development Network is Community Partner. Its opening session hands the stage to young Nigerians already at work in the sector, among them Damilola Hamid Balogun of YSDN and Emmanuel Terwase of Boost Power.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria NOW! is held under the patronage of the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, with the Lagos State Government, the Nigerian Indigenous Women in Mining & Natural Resources Organisation, Women in Mining, Nextier and The Electricity Hub as partners.

World.title: The seventh Kano social influencers conference, By Jibrin Ibrahim
World.content:
This week, I was in Kano attending the Seventh social influencers summit. As I have said before, I am a fan of the annual event and I have attended all of them since it started in 2019. It is a great rendezvous to catch up with the latest in the trilateral intersections between technology, media and social change. The digital revolution has fundamentally transformed how individuals across the globe interact, communicate, and conduct various aspects of their daily lives. Among the most impactful development in this revolution is the rise of social media, which has redefined social norms, behaviour, and interactions, especially, but not only, among the youth.

Social media platforms have transformed the ways in which ideas, trends, and behaviour are propagated. At the heart of these shifts are individuals often termed “social influencers” – people who, through content creation and networked presence, affect what others see, think, or do. While earlier theories of influence focused on mass media and celebrity endorsement, the rise of peer-to-peer networks and algorithmic recommendation systems has made influencer roles more diffuse, accessible, and powerful.

The theme this year is preparing citizens and deploying artificial intelligence (AI) and innovation for accountable governance. Concerns discussed include the nature, risks and possible outcomes of the AI revolution, what Nigeria should do to engage AI, deploying AI for accountable governance, the development of digital rights and transformation of the global order. Our reality has been radically transformed explained Shina Badru of Technology Times. The ancient Nigeria of 2001 when one organisation called NITEL, had a monopoly of all the 750,000 fixed telephone lines and the joke of 30,000 wireless lines to the revolution today of 197 million GSM lines and generalised internet access that continues to expand, becoming faster and more intrusive on our daily lives. It has changed the nature of mass communications as well as inter-personal communications but it has also transformed modes of production. Remaining part of this dynamics and ensuring it is mobilised for our advantage has become an existential imperative. The ancient world of 2001 Nigeria is not going to return. But what does Nigeria, and indeed most of the world controls.

The leading technology and AI companies in the world are American and their leaders run the digital revolution and emerging AI industry. They are Alphabet (Google), Microsoft, Meta (Facebook) and Amazon. Working with a few AI developers like OpenAI and Anthropic, they control big data at the world level and know almost everything about all of us including our political views, lifestyle, family and location at all times. They have accelerated inequality at the world level creating massive wealth in a few hands on one hand and misery, hunger, declining incomes on the other. Even Europe today finds itself in turmoil as protests rock the streets as citizens suffer consequences of marginalisation of vast populations by a few individuals like Elon Musk who is armed with the ideology that empathy has been the strategic blunder of Western civilisation which must be eliminated to enable them control the world for their benefits. As they accumulate trillions, these individuals have become mad and do not even realise their families cannot spend the money they are accumulation in the next one million years. The tech trillionaires have become the new definition of insanity.

The genocide in Gaza has enable us to see how they work with the American war machine using AI to wipe out entire families and neighbourhoods who have a different political opinion. The world might be saved by the fact that China is also rapidly developing its capabilities in industry and in digital technology and AI and medium powers are beginning to organise their self-defence through BRICS and other regional organisations. Nigeria is missing the boat and as the rest of the world works on protecting its data, Nigeria is signing treaties handing out our own data to the United States. That is a key challenge for us today.

Our approach to this terrifying world must be clear says Surrayya Al-Amin, the spoken word artist. Let’s start with stopping our tendency of tearing our country Nigeria at the seams and let’s sew and heal the divides. The second poet to perform, Halima Abubakar called on Nigerians to learn to speak for the voiceless and build a narrative that could galvanise us to use AI to build a new world in which all citizens benefit from the output of development. It begins by ensuring all women and children have access to education. Building on this advice, Dr Usman Bugaje recalled our rich trajectory as African we should build up. The first three universities in the world – University of al-Qurawuyyin in Fez Morocco (859, AD), Al-Azhar in Ciro Egypt, (970, AD) and the University of Sankore in Timbuktu (970, AD). All three were engaged in teaching a broad curriculum that included theology, mathematics, medicine and the sciences and all of them were founded by women or in honour of a woman. These were the principles on which the host university for the event, Khairun University in Kano. The VC of the University, informed participants that inclusiveness is one of the most important principles they stand for and 55% of their students are offered scholarships by the propriotor so that no one is left behind.

The allure of social media lies in its ability to connect users across vast distances, offering a virtual space where they can share experiences, ideas, and content in real-time. For Nigerian youth, this connectivity provides a vital link to both local and global communities, enabling them to participate in a shared cultural dialogue that transcends geographical boundaries. Unfortunately, however, the social media has created a world that is increasingly shaped by the influence of fake news and hate speech. Indeed, fake news and hate speech are becoming the markers of our time determining electoral outcomes in addition to social and political dynamics in the contemporary world. They matter because they are narratives that are designed to confuse and disinform, to cause pain, to hurt people and to push communities to incite one another to kill and maim. The main effect of fake news and hate speech is that they make objective facts less influential in shaping public opinion. They trend and determine “news flows” because they have been designed to focus on appeals to personal belief, prejudice and emotion.

Hate speech and fake news have existed for a long time but over the past decade their scale and banalisation have increased significantly and become insidious in our society. This is because of the complete transformation that has occurred in the technology and use of the social media. Mass communications have historically been structured and controlled through regulatory controls of the organisations that operate them. Strong penal, political and financial sanctions, including the threat and practice of the closure of organs provide for a strong control regime that could impose order and minimum quality in the mass media. In some instances, authoritarian regimes used their power to impose propaganda narratives and hateful speech on media organs and in such cases the structure of control was even stronger. The contemporary situation has been transformed considerably.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

We live in a post truth world that is fuelled significantly by algorithms run by tech companies and social influencers help them create agency. It is a multi-trillion-dollar industry of mass surveillance, misinformation and the spread of false and targeted propaganda that was producing vast profits for the tech companies. In this new world, the main interlocutor in communication becomes a small screen on a hand-held electronic device and the target of communications are social media friends most of whom are not known to the communicator. Gradually, people became deeply engaged with people they do not know and specific forms of narratives emerge on the basis of aggregation around specific ideas and values. In the process, the values of truthfulness and respect were replaced by the numbers you can reach and the impact you can have on people and in the process producing “the triumph of the visceral over the rational, the deceptively simple over the honestly complex”. Understanding complex processes was no longer important, positions are taken on the basis of belief and opinion and interactions with social media “friends” are used to validate the position.

The agency for social influencing is governed by algorithms which are complex systems designed by platforms to personalise the user experience and maximise engagement. They determine which content users see in their feeds, in what order, and what recommendations they receive. These algorithms are sets of rules and calculations used by platforms like Facebook, Instagram, or TikTok to determine what content shows up in your feed. This system can create “echo chambers,” limiting exposure to different perspectives. As AI develops, and the social media grows, the great challenge of our age is seeking to benefit from its advantages and avoiding its risks and dangers.

World.title: Police probe invasion of hospital, staff assault after ex-footballer’s alarm
World.content:
The police in Imo State have begun an investigation into an allegation by a former Super Eagles striker, Emmanuel Emenike, that some political operatives invaded his hospital in Owerri and assaulted the hospital’s staff members before arresting others.

The police spokesperson in Imo State, Henry Okoye, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday.

The former Nigerian footballer co-founded the facility, Emenike Hospital, in May 2024.

It is a 40-bed hospital operated by AGCare, a healthcare operations management company.

Emenike’s alarm

In a post on his Instagram page on Wednesday, Mr Emenike said the operatives arrived at the hospital accompanied by officials of the Imo State Waste Management Agency.

The former Nigerian striker claimed that the security operatives were from Oji Police Divisional Headquarters and that they “assaulted staff and patients, and took away the hospital administrator and cashier.”

The footballer said the Wednesday’s incident happened after an earlier invasion of the facility on 25 September by police operatives on the order of the Division Police Officer in Owerri Urban Division.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He uploaded CCTV footage from the hospital which showed the state waste management agency’s personnel and armed police operatives taking some staff members away amid the chaos that enveloped the hospital.

Mr Emenike appealed to the police authorities in the state and the Imo State Government to investigate the incident and facilitate the release of the staff members.

“Ensure anyone injured receives medical care and that witnesses can report safely.

“Preserve and review available CCTV, incident records and other evidence. Take appropriate action (on the) official or agency for an unlawful act,” he said.

The former Super Eagles star argued that enforcement operations should not endanger patients, disrupt emergency care or use violence against hospital staff.

READ ALSO: Angry youths protest alleged killing of entertainer by police

“Public institutions must act within the law, and allegations of abuse must be investigated transparently,” he stated.

Police investigation

Mr Okoye, a deputy superintendent of police, said the police authorities in the state were aware of the footage showing when three staff members were “arrested over alleged violations of the state’s waste management laws.”

“In response to the incident, the Commissioner of Police, Audu Bosso, has directed a thorough and impartial investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the arrest and determine the roles played by the officers involved,” he said, pointing out that the staff members have been released.

The spokesperson reiterated that the state police command was committed to professionalism, discipline, accountability, and respect for the rule of law.

“Any police officer found to have acted unlawfully or engaged in misconduct will face appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with established procedures,” he vowed.

“The Command urges members of the public to remain calm and assures them that the matter will be handled fairly and in accordance with the law.”

World.title: Group calls for disability-inclusive electoral security practices
World.content:
TAF Africa, All-Rights Foundation, NSCDC, Election security. The All-Rights Foundation (TAF Africa) has called on the Nigeria Police Force and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) to adopt and implement disability-inclusive security practices to strengthen the protection, safety and participation of persons with disabilities during electoral processes.

The group made the call at a two-day conference it organised in Abuja.

The event, held on Thursday and Friday, brought together stakeholders, including the European Union Ambassador, a representative of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), and the Board Chairman of TAF Africa.

The programme focused on encouraging security institutions to integrate the needs and rights of persons with disabilities into electoral security arrangements, aiming to promote safer, more inclusive participation in elections.

Speaking at the event, the European Union (EU) Ambassador to Nigeria, Gautier Mignot, said the event should strengthen accountable governance and the principle that every citizen should be able to participate in public life

“Democracy is measured by whether every eligible citizen can participate freely and safely and meaningfully without discrimination,” he said.

Mr Mignot noted that the NSCDC plays an important role in ensuring safe, peaceful elections, urging the corps to include disability concerns in its operational planning and personnel training.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also highlighted challenges faced by persons with disabilities, including inaccessible electoral information, communication difficulties and intimidation.

Mr Mignot therefore urged the NSCDC to identify practical ways to include persons with disabilities in its security arrangements.

“A person with disabilities has the same right to political participation as every other citizen,” Mr Mignot said, adding that their right to vote and participate in electoral processes must be respected and protected.

The INEC chairman’s speech

Also speaking, INEC Chairperson Joash Amupitan, a professor, said election credibility depends on ensuring every eligible citizen can participate freely and safely without discrimination.

Mr Amupitan, who was represented by an INEC National Commissioner, May Agbamuche-Mbu, stressed the need to provide reasonable assistance to voters with disabilities without affecting their independence in making electoral choices.

“The Independent Electoral Commission recognises that the credibility of elections is not measured merely by the conduct of voting, but also by the ability of every eligible citizen to participate freely and safely without discrimination,” he said.

Mr Amupitan said voters with hearing or visual impairments, and those with limited mobility, need different forms of assistance, including clear visual communication, directions, and accessible routes to polling areas.

He also said the NSCDC’s role should complement, rather than duplicate, the responsibilities of the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies.

He added that security personnel must be trained to communicate appropriately with people with different disabilities, and that risk assessments should be conducted before election day to identify inaccessible entry points, crowded polling areas, and potential communication difficulties.

Earlier, TAF Africa Board Chairman Vincent Anigbogu, a professor, said every Nigerian, including persons with disabilities, hasthe right to participate in the electoral process safely, independently, and with dignity.

Mr Anigbogu noted that internally displaced persons often face challenges such as insecurity, limited access to voter registration and polling facilities, inadequate information and difficulties with documentation.

“These challenges can discourage participation and undermine confidence in the electoral process,” he said.

He stressed that election security arrangements should consider displaced persons’ circumstances and provide appropriate, accessible support.

“It is therefore important that election security arrangements recognise the different circumstances of this group and provide appropriate, accessible and rights-based responses,” he said.

He added that security personnel played an important role in protecting vulnerable voters, as they often respond first when voters face threats, violence, intimidation, or emergencies at polling units.

“Security personnel are particularly important in addressing these challenges,” he said.

World.title: UBA commences contempt proceedings against WEMPCO directors over alleged disobedience of court order
World.content:
The Federal High Court, presided over by Justice Aluko, has granted an application by United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc for substituted service of Form 49 on directors of Wempco named as alleged contemnors in the case of UBA v. Wempco.

The application forms part of proceedings seeking to determine whether the named individuals disobeyed an order of the court and whether they should be committed to prison for contempt.

The directors named as alleged contemnors are Lewis Shui Ngor Tung, Phillip Shui Chei Tung, M.A. Ola Yusuf, Tung Lawrence Blake, Aali Aare Hadji Tokunbo, Paul Shui Po Tung, Tung Robert, C.L. Ip and Taiwo Alli.

In advancing the application, counsel to UBA argued that service of Form 49 on the alleged contemnors was necessary to enable them to appear before the court and show cause why an order of committal should not be made against them.

He also argued that the Directors of Wempco and some members of staff took illegal steps in an attempt to disobey the Order of Court.

The court’s decision to grant substituted service provides a procedural step towards bringing the notice to the attention of the individuals concerned in accordance with the court’s directions.

Form 49 is a notice requiring an alleged contemnor to show cause why an order of committal to prison should not be made against them for alleged disobedience of a court order.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Federal High Court had earlier made an Order of Mareva Injunction and appointed a Receiver/Manager over some of the Assets of Wempco following the indebtedness of Wempco to UBA in the sum of N61,445,695,993.76 (Sixty One Billion FourHundred and Forty-Five Million Six Hundred and Ninety Five Thousand, Nine Hundred and Ninety Three Naira, Seventy Six Kobo).

World.title: CBN outlines market infrastructure supporting Nigeria–China financial flows at Beijing investor forum
World.content:
BEIJING — The Central Bank of Nigeria is developing financial-market infrastructure to support transactions between Nigeria and China and strengthen investor confidence in cross-border financial flows, a CBN official told an investor forum in Beijing.

Dr Okey Umeano, Deputy Director, Financial Markets, said the work extended beyond bilateral swap arrangements to the markets and mechanisms banks need to conduct transactions.

He identified fixed-income market development and work on repurchase agreements, or repos, among the measures supporting the financial infrastructure for RMB–naira activity.

“Even with the policies that are in place, we’re also building infrastructure to support what the market is doing,” Umeano said.

His remarks placed market functioning at the centre of the discussion about deeper financial ties. The objective, he explained, was to give both direct and portfolio investors confidence in their ability to move funds through the financial system.

Umeano said the CBN was building the infrastructure around its policy framework to support continuity and provide confidence over longer investment horizons.

Banking executive Kayode Solola of Standard Bank Group reinforced the importance of efficient payment infrastructure. He said reliable connections between financial systems would give businesses greater certainty about how transactions would be processed and completed.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Solola also highlighted the work required to develop financial flows in both directions. Exporters accustomed to earning dollars would need to consider receiving renminbi, helping build the corresponding flows that could support wider RMB use.

He described those discussions as ongoing, indicating that broader adoption would depend on changes in commercial practice alongside improvements in financial infrastructure.

Flutterwave CEO Olugbenga Agboola provided an example of private-sector payment arrangements already serving the corridor. He said the company had developed a model through which Nigerian businesses could pay participating Chinese suppliers in naira.

Agboola linked adoption to trust in the payment provider, confirmation that funds had been paid and greater exchange-rate predictability.

The discussion connected the CBN’s market-development work with the practical requirements of banks, investors and businesses. It also highlighted the distinct roles of policy, financial markets and payment providers in supporting transactions across the corridor.

For Umeano, the longer-term objective was a financial framework that continued to function reliably beyond the officials implementing it, giving investors confidence that the arrangements supporting their transactions would endure.

World.title: Eko Power assures solar users of no penalties
World.content:
Eko Power Ltd. says customers who invest in solar energy will not be penalised or disconnected for low electricity consumption.

Mr Abiola Aloba, General Manager, Corporate Communication Unit of Eko Power, said this in a statement on Friday in Lagos.

The company’s clarification followed a complaint by Mr Raphael Awoseyin on Oct. 19, alleging repeated visits by its personnel after installing an 18-kilowatt solar power system at his property.

Awoseyin said that the personnel inspected his prepaid meter over suspicions of meter bypass because it was recording little or no electricity consumption.

He also alleged that the company issued him a disconnection notice and demanded N112,606 as a loss-of-revenue charge.

Aloba, however, said that the company had cancelled the charge in full and withdrawn the disconnection notice, adding that Awoseyin had never been disconnected.

“The ‘Loss of Revenue’ demand has been cancelled in full. It should not have been made, and the customer doesn’t owe us,” he said.

Aloba said Eko Power supported customers investing in alternative energy sources and would not penalise them for reducing their dependence on the national grid.

“Eko Power supports customers who invest in solar. Low electricity consumption is not a reason to disconnect anyone,” he said.

He explained that the customer’s prepaid meter, which had been in service for many years, was found to be faulty during testing.

According to him, the company replaced the meter at no cost to the customer and would not impose back-billing, reconciliation charges or other costs arising from the incident.

Awoseyin said that he relied mainly on solar energy during the day and used electricity supplied by Eko Power as backup at night.

He explained that he briefly switched to the company’s electricity supply to demonstrate that his meter could record consumption.

According to him, the meter recorded consumption during the demonstration, but the company’s personnel returned the following day with a disconnection notice.

Awoseyin said his last electricity token purchase was in July 2026 and that he still had some units remaining.

He alleged that the personnel attributed the low consumption to a faulty meter and demanded N112,606 to recover the company’s alleged revenue loss.

Awoseyin said he offered to have the meter tested but was told that the company needed to recover the amount because it was losing revenue.

World.title: 1 die, 3 injured in alleged attack on NDC candidate’s convoy in Ebonyi
World.content:
The Police in Ebonyi have confirmed one person dead and three others injured following an alleged attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) House of Assembly candidate.

The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Joshua Ukandu, confirmed this on Friday in Abakaliki with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN).

Ukandu said the incident occurred at about 4 p.m. on Thursday at Amaezekwe community in Ezza South Local Government Area of the state.

The PPRO said the command received a distress call reporting a disturbance in the community and immediately dispatched operatives to the scene.

“Upon arrival, the operatives found four individuals with gunshot wounds and a burnt vehicle.

“One of the victims was confirmed dead at the hospital, while the three others are receiving medical treatment,” he said.

Meanwhile, the NDC candidate for Ezza South Constituency in the state, Mr Offia-Nwali, said suspected political thugs attacked his motorcade and set his Toyota Hilux vehicle ablaze.

In a statement issued to newsmen in Abakaliki, Offia-Nwali said he and members of his entourage escaped unhurt during the incident.

He expressed sympathy with those affected by the attack and urged youths in the state not to allow themselves to be used by politicians to pursue personal ambitions.

“No political ambition is worth the life of any young person,” he said. (NAN)

World.content:
Fintiri
