World.title: 2027: NDC guber candidate pledges to industrialise Delta
World.content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Delta Governorship Candidate Mr Chris Iyovwaye, has pledged to drive industrialisation as vehicle for job creation and sustainable development in the state if elected in 2027.

Iyovwaye made the pledge during a consultation with Chief Emmanuel Nwachukwu, Managing Director, Benco Pools, and his grassroots movement on Friday in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area of Delta.

The NDC delegation, led by Iyovwaye, includes the party’s Delta North senatorial candidate, Mr Victor Ochei, and other candidates from Ika Federal Constituency.

Others were the party’s candidates for Ika North-East Constituency I, Mr Sylvester Chukwuedo, and Ika South Constituency, Mrs Ogor Tony-Obuh.

Iyovwaye criticised poor management of Delta’s common patrimony and the lack of innovative leadership capable of translating resources into tangible benefits.

He said industrialisation would drive economic growth, create employment and promote sustainable development if supported by practical policies and measurable results.

The governorship candidate said the NDC remained committed to changing the state’s development trajectory through policies that would unlock its economic potentials.

Iyovwaye also expressed confidence in the quality of the party’s candidates across all levels, including its presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi.

He called for the support of Nwachukwu and his associates, saying Delta has greater economic potential than the reflected current level of development.

Also, Ochei thanked Nwachukwu for receiving the delegation and recalled his earlier visit to the business leader a few days before the consultation.

He described the developing relationship as a partnership with the potential to benefit all parties, particularly the people.

The other candidates outlined their commitment to effective representation and development and reinforced the delegation’s message of coordinated engagement across Ika Federal Constituency and Delta North.

The party’s Delta North Senatorial Chairman, Mr Aaron Ebenuwa, also led members of the party leadership on the visit.

World.title: Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA – The Federal Government has secured a total of 653 convictions of persons arrested across the federation for their involvement in various acts of terrorism.

The convicts, some of whom were found guilty of aiding insurgents or concealing information about their operations from security agencies, were among the 1,060 persons brought before the court in the third phase of the ongoing mass trial of terror suspects.

Speaking to newsmen shortly after stepping out of the courtroom on Friday, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, disclosed that a total of 880 cases had been heard, out of which the court convicted 653, acquitted seven and discharged 27 of the defendants.

He said the exercise would continue and the final figures would be announced after the conclusion of the trial.

Describing the current phase of the mass trial as the largest since the FG commenced the special court sessions for the prosecution of terror suspects, the AGF attributed the success of the exercise to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration.

He expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho.

The AGF also commended the prosecution team, the defence counsel and the security agencies for contributing to the smooth conduct of the proceedings.

Among the agencies he acknowledged for their contributions were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN).

According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country.

On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants.

He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects.

He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively.

On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise.

He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities.

World.title: C’River: DSS intercepts GPMGs, AK-47s, other weapons; arrests two
World.content:
Cross River State Deputy Governor, Dr Peter Odey, flanked by heads of security agencies, during the parade of suspects arrested for importation of arms into the state on Friday.

….as Gov Otu warns political sponsors of violence

By Ike Uchechukwu

The Department of State Services have intercepted a cache of sophisticated weapons, including General Purpose Machine Guns (GPMGs) and AK-47 rifles, along the Bekwarra–Ogoja axis of Cross River State,

Following the interception, Governor Bassey Edet Otu has warned politicians and their sponsors that the state will not become a theatre of bloodshed.

Vanguard learned that four suspects were reportedly trailed from northern Nigeria through Benue State into Cross River. Two were arrested, while two others escaped with gunshot wounds.

Governor Otu, speaking through his Deputy, Dr Peter Odey, said the government would confront decisively any threat to the peace, security and democratic stability of the state.

“The peace of Cross River State is non-negotiable. No political ambition, personal interest or desperation for power is worth the life of any citizen.

“We will not allow anyone, regardless of status, political affiliation or connections, to import violence into our state or turn our communities into killing fields,” the Governor warned.

At the parade of the suspects and display of the recovered weapons, Odey said preliminary investigations suggested the arms might be linked to the prevailing political atmosphere.

“The discovery of these weapons is a serious security concern. Arms of this nature, if placed in the wrong hands, could be used to intimidate political opponents, terrorise communities, disrupt lawful political activities and inflict irreversible harm on innocent citizens.

We will not sit idly by while anyone attempts to undermine the safety of our people,” he stated.

He said the incident would not be treated as isolated, stressing that the democratic space must remain open to peaceful competition.

“Politics must be a contest of ideas, character, vision and service, not a contest of weapons.

“Those who believe that they can gain political advantage through intimidation, criminality or the sponsorship of violence are gravely mistaken. The law will take its full course against anyone found culpable,” he said.

Odey disclosed that the arrested suspects would be charged to court, while investigations were continuing to establish the origin of the weapons, trace the network responsible for their movement and identify their alleged sponsors and intended recipients.”

“The people who physically move weapons are only one part of the investigation.

“We must establish where these arms came from, who arranged their transportation, who financed the operation and who was expected to receive them. Anyone found to have participated in this criminal enterprise will be brought before the law,” the Deputy Governor said.

He warned that no one would be allowed to hide behind political office, party membership or community influence.

“Our position is clear: nobody is above the law. We will not shield anyone because of political affiliation, social standing or relationship with persons in authority.

“If investigations establish that anyone sponsored, procured, transported or intended to deploy these weapons for criminal purposes, such a person will face the consequences prescribed by law,” he declared.

The Deputy Governor urged politicians and supporters to exercise restraint and reject any temptation to recruit, arm or mobilise individuals for violence.

“Every political actor has a responsibility to protect the peace of this state. We must not allow political differences to divide our communities or turn neighbours against one another.

Whoever seeks public office must be prepared to earn the confidence of the people peacefully and democratically. There can be no justification for the use of illegal arms to pursue political objectives,” he added.

Odey assured residents of the administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property and safeguarding the electoral process, and urged the public to report suspicious movements to security agencies.

He commended the Department of State Services (DSS) and other agencies for their vigilance and swift response.

“The security agencies deserve commendation for acting promptly to prevent a potentially dangerous situation from escalating.

“Their work underscores the importance of intelligence-led policing, inter-agency collaboration and the vigilance of citizens.

“We encourage them to sustain this effort and ensure that every link in this investigation is thoroughly examined,” he said.

World.title: 2027: Adopt Rainbow Coalition model to avoid political violence, Wike urges govs
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has urged state governors supporting the reelection of President Bola Tinubu to emulate his Rainbow Coalition model, saying it has brought political cooperation, peace and stability to the FCT and Rivers State.

He spoke on Friday during an interactive engagement with political leaders, traditional rulers, women and youths in Kuje Area Council.

Some APC governors led by Senator Hope Uzodinma of Imo State had earlier kicked against the coalition and distanced themselves from its activities. However, the president recently reviewed the composition of his campaign council, incorporating leaders of the coalition and appointing Wike to coordinate his campaigns in Rivers State and the FCT.

Wike said the coalition had shown that politicians from different parties could work together in the interest of the people instead of allowing partisan differences to fuel hostility, violence and division.

“If Nigerian politics can come to this level, we will not be hearing about fighting; we will not be seeing ourselves killing one another,” he said.

He explained that the arrangement had brought politicians from the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP together to pursue shared political objectives despite their differences. The same model, he added, is being implemented in Rivers State.

According to the minister, candidates emerging under the arrangement would enjoy the backing of stakeholders across party lines. He cited former FCT Senator Philip Aduda, saying his support extends beyond the APC to the broader coalition.

Wike said the arrangement was meant to encourage inclusive representation and keep office holders accountable to the people.

He cautioned Kuje residents against repeating what he described as a political mistake in the 2023 elections, urging them to prioritise accessibility, accountability and performance when choosing representatives.

The minister questioned the relationship between the FCT’s current senator, Ireti Kingibe and the people of the territory, alleging that the incumbent had not adequately engaged communities to understand their challenges. He contrasted this with Aduda, saying effective representation requires a senator to understand the everyday experiences of the people.

“Aduda knows them. Aduda knows when they have problems. Aduda knows when they are sleeping, and Aduda knows when they are crying. That is the essence of representation,” Wike said.

He urged residents not to entrust their future to politicians he described as “political gamblers”, insisting that electoral decisions should rest on demonstrable records rather than promises. He also called for greater political cooperation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

On infrastructure, Wike assured residents that the road linking the Airport Road–Tipper Garage corridor to Gwagwalada would be completed and commissioned by the end of December.

He recalled that traditional rulers in Kuje had named the road a priority during an earlier visit, asking the administration to fix its poor condition before presenting other demands.

The minister said the first phase of the project had been commissioned, with Vice-President Kashim Shettima representing President Bola Tinubu during activities marking the administration’s third anniversary.

He urged residents to compare the road’s former condition with its present state, describing the project as part of efforts to improve connectivity and living conditions in the FCT’s satellite communities.

Responding, the Hakimi Agwai, Kuje Area Council, Shuaibu Pada, assured the minister of Kuje’s bloc votes, saying the people would reciprocate his gestures with their votes. He appealed for road construction to be extended to interior communities, including routes connecting Rubochi, Kwali and other neighbouring settlements.

The FCT APC Chairman, Tanko Yamawo, commended the administration’s infrastructure programme and political engagement. He described the willingness of stakeholders from both parties to sit at the same table as a significant development in Kuje’s political environment, adding that improved roads had reduced travel difficulties between Kuje and neighbouring communities.

The PDP Chairman in the FCT, Ismael Dogara, said this was the first time campaigns were being held in the FCT without any smashing of cars recorded anywhere, a peace he credited to the unity fostered by the minister. He said residents who once took to the streets to demand amenities from the Federal Government no longer needed to protest, and that the people were ready to pay Wike back.

The Kuje Council Chairman, Samuel Shekwolo, described Wike as a “responsible and giving father” who united indigenous and non-indigenous communities. He said the minister had changed the narrative of young men who believed Kuje was designated only for a prison station because of its lack of development.

World.title: Tinubu condoles family of Nollywood veteran, Francis Duru‎‎
World.content:
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu has expressed sorrow over the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Richard Francis Duru, extending his heartfelt condolences to his family, colleagues, fans and the Nigerian film industry.

The veteran actor, Duru, passed away at 57.

‎

‎The President, in a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, described the loss of the respected actor as a painful moment for Nollywood and the nation’s creative community, which has benefited immensely from its pioneers’ dedication, talent, and contributions.

‎

‎He acknowledged the important role veteran actors like Duru played in the growth and development of Nigeria’s film industry, particularly in shaping its artistic identity, nurturing emerging talent, and projecting Nigerian stories, culture, and values to audiences at home and abroad.

‎

‎President Tinubu noted that the legacies of artists who devote their lives to entertaining, educating, and inspiring society endure long after their departure.

‎

‎He affirmed that Duru’s contributions to Nollywood will remain part of the industry’s rich history and cultural heritage.

‎

‎President Tinubu prayed for the peaceful repose of the departed actor’s soul and asked God to grant his family, friends, colleagues, and admirers the strength and fortitude to bear the irreparable loss.

‎

‎He assured the Nigerian creative community that his administration recognises the invaluable contributions of the arts and entertainment industry to national development, cultural preservation, and the country’s global image.

World.title: Tech Firm Takes Will Preparation Online to Protect Nigerians’ Assets
World.content:
•Says digital estate planning will expand opportunities for lawyers

Wale Igbintade

A Nigerian technology company, Castle eWill and Trust Limited, has launched a digital estate-planning platform designed to simplify Will preparation, encourage succession planning and make estate-planning services more accessible to Nigerians.

The platform enables adults to prepare, update, securely store and manage their Wills and Trusts online, with the aim of helping individuals protect their families, preserve their assets and ensure that their wishes are respected after death.

The Chief Executive Officer of the company, Mr Olumide Olaiya, said the initiative was founded on the belief that everyone should have the opportunity to plan for the future of their loved ones, regardless of their financial circumstances or location.

According to him, the company hopes to become Africa’s most trusted digital platform for estate planning, Will preparation, Trust administration and probate support.

Olaiya said many Nigerians postponed preparing Wills because they considered the process uncomfortable, complicated or relevant only to wealthy individuals.

He explained that Castle eWill was seeking to change the perception by providing an accessible starting point for estate planning while encouraging users to obtain appropriate professional legal advice.

The platform’s Will preparation process comprises five stages, beginning with the provision of personal information, followed by details of executors, trustees, beneficiaries and assets.

Users are subsequently required to provide particulars of their gifts and wishes, supply information about witnesses, and review and confirm the document before printing it and submitting it to the relevant High Court Probate Registry.

Olaiya said the process was designed to make Will preparation more straightforward while incorporating safeguards to protect users’ information and support the authentication of their documents.

On data protection, the company said files were encrypted before being written to disk, while attempts to access them were logged.

The platform also incorporates identity-verification measures, including email confirmation, authentication of government-issued identification documents and comparison with a live camera check.

According to the company, these measures are intended to establish that the individual making a Will is the person identified in the document.

Another feature is a QR seal attached to every Will generated through the platform.

Castle eWill said scanning the code enables recipients to verify the document’s identity, version and date of issuance, helping institutions, including banks and registries, determine whether a copy is genuine and current.

The platform also sends reminders encouraging subscribers to review their Wills every 12 months and following significant life events that could affect their estate plans.

Such events include marriage, the birth of a child and the acquisition of property.

Addressing concerns that digital Will-making services could diminish the role of legal practitioners, Castle eWill maintained that its platform was intended to expand, rather than undermine, opportunities for lawyers.

The company argued that making estate planning more accessible could bring more Nigerians who had never consulted lawyers about Wills or Trusts into the process, thereby creating additional demand for professional legal services.

The company also expressed its intention to collaborate with lawyers across Nigeria to provide these services.

Drawing a comparison with developments in the banking industry, Castle eWill said the introduction of internet banking and mobile applications had expanded access to banking services rather than eliminated the need for banks and banking professionals.

It maintained that a similar approach could apply to legal services, with technology helping more people take the first step towards succession planning while lawyers provide the expertise required to address complex legal issues.

According to the company, professional legal advice remains particularly important in estates involving complicated family structures, corporate assets, jointly owned properties, customary and Islamic law, foreign assets, taxation, guardianship, business succession and competing claims among beneficiaries.

The company maintained that technology could widen access to estate planning, while professional legal judgment remained essential to ensuring that individuals and families received appropriate advice and that their wishes were properly documented and implemented.

World.title: Knorr Partners CAPA to Celebrate Nigeria’s Culinary Community
World.content:
Knorr has celebrated Nigerian food culture and culinary expertise as the headline sponsor of the Culinary Arts Practitioners Association Nigeria (CAPA) Day 2026. Through its participation, the brand recognised the chefs, caterers and food professionals whose skills and creativity shape the meals that bring people together and make special occasions memorable.

The event was held on Tuesday, at the Hall of Odin, Oniru, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Held under the theme “Root to Relevance,” CAPA Day 2026 explored the relationship between culinary heritage and innovation, with discussions around knowledge sharing, sustainability and the future of food.

Culinary experts, including the president, Chiamaka Nwakalor-Egemba, popularly known as Chef Amaka; the vice-president, Ladipo Ayodeji, known as Chef Dee; and Tolani Tayo-Osikoya, known as Chef T, joined fellow practitioners to celebrate the traditions, skills and ideas shaping Nigeria’s culinary industry.

As part of its participation, Knorr hosted a cooking showcase featuring its Smokey Party Jollof Seasoning, demonstrating how the seasoning could be incorporated into different dishes.

The event also recognised culinary talent through a competition, with Chef Adesuwa Edogun (Chef Eva) emerging in first position, followed by Chef Mujidah Adegbayi (Chef MOA) in second place, Chef Ummulkhuthum (Chef K) in third place, and Chef Adeola Kukoyi in fourth place.

Speaking on Knorr’s sponsorship for this year’s event, Dexter Adeola, Foods Marketing Innovation & EWA Strategy Lead at Unilever, said, “We are proud to be part of CAPA Day 2026 and to support the culinary professionals who play an important role in Nigeria’s food culture. Their skill and creativity help preserve our food traditions while bringing new ideas to the kitchen. Our participation reflects our commitment to celebrating these professionals and the role they play in bringing people together through food.”

The event also marked the induction of new members into CAPA.

World.title: KC Luxury Arrives in Court in Ambulance, Seeks Bail Over Health Crisis
World.content:
•Nurse says KC Luxury cannot enter courtroom; NDLEA opposes medical bail, cites flight risk

Wale Igbintade

Businessman and social media influencer, Afolabi Michael Kazeem, popularly known as KC Luxury, was brought to the Federal High Court in Lagos in an ambulance while receiving oxygen on Friday, as his lawyer urged the court to grant him bail for specialised medical treatment over his deteriorating health.

A nurse attending to the defendant, Bukki Yahya of the Police Hospital, Falomo, Lagos, told Justice Musa Kakaki that Kazeem could not be moved into the courtroom because of his condition.

Yahya said the defendant was admitted to the hospital on October 7, 2026, and diagnosed with asthma and sepsis.

“My Lord, I am Bukki Yahya, the nurse attending to the patient, Afolabi. He was diagnosed with asthma and sepsis when he was brought to the Police Hospital, Falomo.

“He is inside the ambulance in the court premises, but we can’t move him here because he is with oxygen,” she told the court.

The nurse testified after a correctional officer informed the court that Kazeem was critically ill and had been hospitalised.

Following the testimony, Kazeem’s counsel, Chief Emefo Etudo, questioned why his client had been brought to court in such a condition.

“If, for instance, the defendant was in the intensive care unit and is like this, why should they bring him to court?” the lawyer asked.

Justice Kakaki subsequently directed that the defendant be returned to the hospital, saying, “You can take him back to the hospital.”

After the court’s directive, Etudo proceeded to argue a fresh bail application dated October 16, 2026, seeking Kazeem’s release to enable him to obtain specialised medical treatment at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH).

The lawyer told the court that his client’s condition had deteriorated, alleging that he had suffered a lung collapse and required specialist medical attention.

Etudo said the Police Hospital had referred Kazeem to LUTH because it lacked the facilities required for the surgical management of his condition.

He further alleged that the defendant was withdrawn from LUTH and taken to a correctional centre on October 13, despite his medical condition.

According to the defence, Kazeem’s condition worsened while he was being conveyed to the correctional facility, forcing those accompanying him to return him to the Police Hospital, where he was admitted to the intensive care unit.

Etudo argued that the alleged deterioration in his client’s health and the circumstances surrounding his removal from LUTH constituted fresh grounds for the court to reconsider his continued detention and grant him bail.

He said the defence had filed an affidavit of urgency, a 21-paragraph affidavit in support of the application, a written address and relevant exhibits. He added that a reply to the prosecution’s counter-affidavit had also been filed on October 22.

Opposing the application, prosecution counsel, Abu Ibrahim, urged the court to dismiss it, arguing that the defence was attempting to reopen an issue already considered by the court.

Ibrahim said the prosecution had filed an 11-paragraph counter-affidavit, sworn to by Ebuka Okwonkwo, on October 22.

He contended that the court had addressed the relevant medical issue in its October 2 pronouncement concerning Exhibit AK2, arguing that the defence should have challenged the decision on appeal rather than file another application on substantially the same grounds.

The prosecutor also questioned whether the medical evidence presented by the defence sufficiently justified the defendant’s release.

“Your Lordship looked at the application. The ailment is the same. It is the same asthma. But maybe it has become acute; the character and the ailment are the same,” Ibrahim said.

He further argued that the defence had not presented medical documentation from LUTH establishing that the hospital could not manage Kazeem’s condition.

“They said he was admitted, treated and discharged. We urge Your Lordship to dismiss this application,” he said.

While acknowledging that bail was at the court’s discretion, Ibrahim described Kazeem as a flight risk and urged the judge to impose stringent conditions if the application was granted.

Responding, Etudo urged the court to grant bail on liberal terms, insisting that his client’s condition warranted his release.

“The condition of the first defendant speaks for itself. We have heard what the prosecution said. We urge this court to grant this application on liberal terms,” he said.

He assured the court that Kazeem would attend subsequent proceedings if released, adding that his international passport was already in the custody of the authorities.

After hearing the arguments, Justice Kakaki adjourned ruling on the bail application to October 28, 2026.

Kazeem is standing trial alongside Boniface Freeman Ochoche Sule and Ikechukwu Ekugo Patriarch on a 22-count charge involving allegations of conspiring to export 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine to the United Kingdom and money laundering.

The defendants have pleaded not guilty to the charges.

World.title: Sokoto Residents Challenge ADC Candidate Dan’iya to Present Devt Blueprint
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Concerned residents of Sokoto State have challenged the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, to move beyond criticism of Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto’s administration and unveil a clear and achievable development agenda ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

In a statement jointly signed by Comrade Ibrahim Umar Kware, Comrade Aminu Hali Tambuwal and Comrade Bello Arzika Dandange, on behalf of the group, the residents said the people of the state deserve more than political attacks from those seeking their mandate.

According to the group, the 2027 election should be defined by competing ideas, credible alternatives and concrete solutions to the challenges facing the state, rather than a campaign built solely on fault-finding and condemnation of government policies.

The residents observed that since his emergence as the ADC governorship candidate, Dan’iya has consistently criticised the policies and programmes of the present administration without presenting a comprehensive policy document detailing what he would do differently.

“Enough of criticism. Sokoto people want to know what you intend to do for them. What is your development agenda and how do you intend to deliver on your promises? It is not enough to criticise the government without providing workable alternatives,” the statement said.

They argued that aspiring to govern a state of over five million people requires thorough preparation, clear vision and a sound understanding of public administration, including realistic funding strategies, implementation timelines and measurable performance indicators.

The group further urged Dan’iya to reflect on his tenure as Deputy Governor under former Governor Aminu Waziri Tambuwal and share the lessons learnt, cautioning him against what they described as the shortcomings of his political mentor whom they accused of assuming office without adequate preparation.

While emphasising the need for accountability on the part of the incumbent administration, the residents acknowledged Governor Ahmed Aliyu’s interventions in security logistics, road construction and rehabilitation, housing and primary healthcare revitalisation as efforts that merit objective assessment.

They noted that the provision of operational vehicles, motorcycles and other security equipment to security agencies has enhanced response capacity in parts of the state, even as they admitted that insecurity remains a challenge requiring sustained action.

According to the concerned residents, while the present government must be judged on its performance, the opposition has an equal responsibility to demonstrate superior capacity and offer better alternatives rather than expecting voters to be swayed by criticism alone.

They therefore challenged the ADC candidate to publicly present his specific plans for strengthening security in vulnerable communities, supporting farmers and small businesses, tackling youth unemployment, attracting private investment and improving service delivery across the 23 local government areas of the state, stressing that Sokoto needs a prepared leader with a clear plan.

World.title: Prof Gregory Ikechukwu Ibe: The Visionary Who Left a Crater
World.content:
By Eniola Olakunri

The nation lost a treasure on October 18, 2026, when the news broke that Professor Gregory Ikechukwu Ibebhad translated.

It was one shattering piece of news this writer never expected to receive. Not at this time.

It has been a few days since his passing, yet it still feels surreal. One finds it difficult to pull oneself out of that vortex of confusion, disbelief and sheer astonishment. A most disturbing reality that the mind continues to struggle to comprehend.

Proffy, my moniker for him, was a highly spirited, larger-than-life personality: popular, engaging, warm and, quite simply, a no-dull-moment kind of man who related effortlessly with virtually everyone.

We were introduced by a mutual friend in 2018, and we took to each other like fish to water. From that moment, a beautiful friendship blossomed, and we remained almost inseparable until his translation.

In 2019, without telling him, I wrote a piece about this extraordinary man. I will share substantial snippets from that piece here because, in retrospect, they provide a fascinating window into the life of a man who was truly a legend in every sense of the word.

Please read on.

THE POWER OF A VISION: THE GREGORY IBE STORY

Originally written on November 3, 2019

He took the wooden spoon Life had thrust into his mouth and ran with it.

To him, it was a spoon. It was his to do with as he wished. It did not bother him that his spoon was different, that his circumstances were dire, or that Providence appeared to have been visiting the next town when he was born.

He ran with his vision; he ran with a determination so spectacular that he turned what should have been a disability into a launch pad for success.

His spoon changed to gold!

Meet Professor Gregory Ikechukwu Charles Ibe, OFR.

EARLY YEARS

Born on December 10, 1963, in Kaduna to a policeman father, Cyril Elesim Ibe,nand petty-trader mother, Ugoeze Margaret Ibe, young Iyke, as he was fondly called by friends and loved ones, seemed destined for a life of consequence.

Although born in Kaduna, Iyke missed the opportunity to learn Hausa, one of Nigeria’s major languages, because the family moved back East when he was barely a year and a half old.

However, having spent a considerable part of his adult life in the North, he would later acquire the ability to hold a decent conversation in the widely spoken language.

From the outset, he understood that he had to develop the grit necessary to change the circumstances surrounding his birth.

His father spent a considerable part of his life as a policeman.

This was long before His Royal Highness mounted the stool of his forebears. As a policeman, the then Prince Cyril Ibe’s salary could not provide the comforts that a growing household of nine children and a wife required.

Iyke, being the first child, understood early that he had to grow up quickly. He took on odd jobs here and there to augment the family’s finances.

Today, Providence had taken Professor Ibe on its wings. His circumstances had changed dramatically, and he had recorded one spectacular success after another in several fields of human endeavour.

He was a husband and father of six children : an orthopaedic surgeon, a cardiologist, a finance expert, a lawyer, an accountant and his youngest son, who was nursing an ambition to become a pilot.

A firm believer in Henry Ford’s famous philosophy – Whether you think you can or think you can’t, you are right” – Ibe definitely thought he could.

And that is why he became a living testimony to how a vision can birth and drive success.

SCHOOLING AND APPRENTICESHIP

By the time the family moved back to the East in 1965, young Iyke knew that all he had were the goals he had set for himself and the blank canvas of life.

While schooling, he apprenticed at various times in surveying, carpentry, tailoring and local electrical works. He also joined his mother, Ugoeze, in making confectioneries, candles and petroleum jelly for sale.

In the midst of all this, Ibe continued to forge ahead academically. He understood that education provided the plank for bridging the divide between poverty on one hand and a secure future on the other.

He went on to acquire a Bachelor of Science degree in Marketing from Enugu State University of Science and Technology, followed by a Master’s degree in Health Care Management and a Ph.D. in Management from California Coast University, Santa Ana, California.

WORK LIFE: PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTORS

Ibe’s work experience cut across both the private and public sectors.

He began his career with International Generics and Industrial Construction (Nigeria) Limited in 1985 as an Accountant II and rapidly rose through the ranks. Within six years, he had become Deputy Manager, Coordinator, Northern States Projects and Deputy Area Manager, Eastern Nigeria.

His work ethic and the strong sense of values acquired from an early age became defining characteristics of his professional life.

Among the projects he handled were the Federal Ministry of External Affairs Complex, renovation of the Old Federal Secretariat Complex (both in Abuja), Imo Airport, Imo Specialist Hospital, Anambra State University of Technology satellite campuses in Enugu, Nnewi and Nkwelle, and Oba Airport, among others.

His desire to broaden his experience took him to Berkeley Pharmaceutical Limited, headquartered in London, where he was responsible for marketing and distribution of pharmaceutical products across the South-East and South-South.

In 1992, Dizengoff (West Africa) Nigeria Limited, an Israeli company, came calling. Although he was enjoying his work at Berkeley Pharmaceuticals, he could not resist the challenge and responsibilities that came with the new opportunity.

He was appointed Divisional Coordinator/Marketing Manager, responsible for market development in West Africa. In that capacity, he handled air-cooling projects for Yobe State Television, Abuja Sheraton Hotel and Towers, Kano grain silos, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation and telecommunications projects for NICON Hilton Hotels, now Transcorp Hilton, Abuja.

By 1996, Ibe was headhunted by ITE (Nigeria) Limited, a subsidiary of Globe International Holding S.A. of Switzerland, and appointed Deputy General Manager.

There, he was responsible for the marketing of educational and scientific laboratory equipment and the development and marketing of communications, education, scientific and security equipment.

He handled these assignments with gusto and an abiding sense of responsibility. But he had begun to feel the pull of entrepreneurship.

His experience at ITE had opened his eyes to the enormous challenges confronting Nigeria’s educational sector, and he felt compelled to do something about them.

THE ENTREPRENEURIAL JOURNEY

In 1999, Ibe and other foreign partners founded Skill “G” Nigeria Limited, a company established to bridge the yawning gaps between Nigeria’s educational sector and the rest of the world, particularly in technical and vocational education, science and technology.

The company took off with remarkable speed and, within a few years, became a major player in the West African educational sector.

Across Nigeria, Skill “G” traversed the length and breadth of the country, delivering vocational and technical centres, skill acquisition centres, micro-science and mathematics laboratories for primary and secondary schools, and education resource centres.

Other companies followed, including Hamitle Holding Inc., Hamitle Engineering Nigeria Limited, Hamitle Consult Nigeria Limited and HHI Nigeria Limited, with interests spanning civil engineering, construction, telecommunications and consultancy.

At various points, Ibe was called upon by the Federal, State and Local Governments, as well as international bodies, to deploy the depth of knowledge and experience he had accumulated for the benefit of the nation and humanity.

He became a lecturer at Abia State University, Uturu, and Tansian University, Anambra State, while also serving as a consultant to the Federal Government on civil service and education reforms.

His contributions to national development included participation in several committees and initiatives covering maritime education, national science parks, entrepreneurial education, science and technology laboratory development, exports, waivers and concessions, among others.

His industry was such that he was entrusted with the oversight of 12 United Nations agencies between 2000 and 2007 on behalf of the Federal Government of Nigeria.

With such an impressive portfolio of service and accomplishment, it was hardly surprising that the Federal Government honoured him with the Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR) in 2013.

THE VISIONARY BEHIND GREGORY UNIVERSITY

For years, the entrepreneur had nurtured the idea of bringing his private-sector, business and public-sector experiences to bear on Nigeria’s educational system.

He found his answer in the establishment of a university. But not just another university.

He wanted an institution that would be distinctive.

He understood the challenges: stringent regulatory requirements, finance, land, infrastructure, power, human resources and the countless logistical hurdles involved in establishing a university in Nigeria.

But Gregory Ibe was never one to run from challenges.

Where others saw hurdles, he saw ladders.

In 2012, he founded Gregory University, Uturu (GUU) in Abia State.

The University’s vision centred on becoming a world-renowned institution recognised for the quality of its academic and research programmes, as well as its professional, practical and entrepreneurial capacity development.

One of the University’s distinctive features was its emphasis on entrepreneurship. Second-year students, irrespective of their disciplines, were exposed to entrepreneurship and its practical applications,equipping them with skills with which they could begin building businesses even before graduation.

And Professor Ibe, the Founder and Chancellor, took a personal interest in this.

He would have it no other way.

His concern was straightforward: Nigeria was producing thousands upon thousands of graduates who left university with certificates but without sufficient practical skills to create opportunities for themselves.

His response was to infuse entrepreneurship into the curriculum.

The results were evident.

GUU graduates were pursuing further academic accomplishments, securing employment and, importantly, becoming entrepreneurs themselves.

Therein lay the power of a vision.

His vision was never merely about building an institution. It was about building people.

FAITH AND PHILANTHROPY

Professor Ibe was a devout Catholic whose Christian faith informed his worldview and approach to life.

He believed strongly in the power of faith, good upbringing, integrity and responsible citizenship. He believed that children should be encouraged to discover and develop their God-given talents.

He was equally passionate about giving.

His philanthropy was not restricted to individuals or even his immediate community. His constituency was Nigeria.

Over the years, through the Gregory Iyke Foundation, he supported scholarships, education, healthcare, youth development, infrastructure, sports and community projects.

Among the initiatives attributed to him were scholarships for students of medicine and pharmacy, support for student pilots, donations of computers and laboratory equipment, road construction, healthcare for senior citizens, youth empowerment, sports development, cultural initiatives and support for educational institutions.

The list was extensive.

And typically, he did not make a spectacle of his giving.

For Gregory Ibe, philanthropy was not a performance. It was a responsibility.

AND THEN CAME INNOV8

When I wrote the original piece on November 3, 2019, Professor Ibe read it and liked it immensely.

But he asked me to hold off publishing it.

His reason?

There were still other ventures in the pipeline that needed to become part of the fuller story.

He was right.

Less than a year later, with his characteristic irrepressible energy, Professor Ibe, alongside his long-time partner, founded Innov8 Hub, a not-for-profit organisation established as a moving force in innovation, creativity, entrepreneurship, capacity building and venture creation, with a mandate focused on socio-economic growth and human capital development in Nigeria and beyond.

And what followed was another remarkable chapter in the Gregory Ibe story.

In just six years, Innov8 Hub recorded achievements that would have been impressive even for an organisation with a much longer history.

It supported, mentored and provided technical guidance to more than 250 entrepreneurs and 800 researchers.

It successfully developed more than 120 products and prototypes and incubated 25 promising startups, helping them move towards commercially viable businesses. Among them were Vectar Energy, a clean-tech venture, and EpochZero, an AI-driven health diagnostics venture.

The organisation also attracted significant international recognition.

It became a Gold Recipient of the Academic–Industry Partnership Award* under the Education and Research Leadership category and was inducted into the Global Hall of Fame.

It was shortlisted for the prestigious QS Reimagine Education Awards for its Eco Lab Environmental Education Outreach initiative.

And at the Africa Startup Ecosystem Builders Summit, Innov8 was selected as one of the Top Five finalists for Innovation Hub Champion of the Year from 1,786 nominations across 52 African countries.

This was the man I proudly called Proffy.

A man who seemingly never ran out of ideas.

A man who saw possibilities where others saw problems.

A man who kept moving.

THE LEGACY

The nation has lost a visionary par excellence; a kinetic entrepreneur; an outstanding academic; a passionate philanthropist of uncommon hue; a genuine Christian; a devoted family man; and a friend who could comfortably move between the highest echelons of society and the ordinary man on the street.

Of course, there are dimensions of this remarkable human being that time and space will not permit me to fully chronicle.

But I believe the reader has, through these recollections, caught a glimpse of the extraordinary man Professor Gregory Ikechukwu Ibe – Enyi Abia – was.

When I wrote in 2019 that it would not be surprising if one day a title such as “Enyi Nigeria” was created specifically for him, I was, perhaps unknowingly, only beginning to appreciate the breadth of the man.

Professor Ibe did not merely live a life.

He built.

He nurtured.

He mentored.

He inspired.

He gave.

He educated.

He created.

He transformed.

And then, on October 18, 2026, he translated.

We often say that certain people leave a vacuum when they depart this world.

But a vacuum can, eventually, be filled.

Professor Ibe has left something far greater.

He has left a crater.

A gaping, monumental crater created by a life of uncommon energy, vision, service, enterprise, generosity and friendship.

And that crater, I dare say, can never be refilled.

May Almighty God grant his soul eternal rest and grant his beloved family, the Gregory University and Innov8 families, the countless people working across the businesses he created, his colleagues and associates, and the many others whose lives he touched, the fortitude to bear this monumental loss.

Adieu, Proffy.

You ran with the wooden spoon Life handed you.

You turned it to gold.

And you left the world richer for having passed through it.

May your gentle soul rest in perfect peace.

*Eniola Olakunri

CEO, Write Affairs

Abuja

World.title: Energia Chairman Laments Funding Hurdle For Local Oil Producers
World.content:
*Says operators pay double for same loan abroad

Peter Uzoho

Chairman of Energia Limited, Mr George Osahon, has decried the huge disparity in financing costs for indigenous upstream oil and gas operators, saying Nigerian banks charge nearly double what their overseas counterparts charge for the same facility, stalling investment and production growth.

Osahon stated this during a panel session at the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists (NAPE) Pre-Conference Workshop in Lagos, themed “Navigating Nigeria’s Upstream Future: Exploration and Development Approaches vs Energy Security Demand.”

Energia Limited is a Nigerian-owned exploration and production company and operator of Petroleum Mining Lease (PML) 23, formerly Ebendo/Obodeti Marginal Field in (OML) 56, where it holds 55/45 per cent working interest in joint venture with Oando Production and Development Company.

Responding to questions on financing challenges and why indigenous operators are not ramping up production as much, Osahon said operators face a structural dichotomy that punishes local firms.

He cited his company’s experience where a Nigerian bank offered a facility at 14.5 per cent plus manager’s fees and other charges, while the overseas arm of the same bank with same name offered 8.95 per cent for equivalent risk.

“The funny thing about this is what I call the dichotomy in the way some of this things work. We have a bank in Nigeria, Nigerian bank. And they tell you that their interest is 14.5 per cent. And there’s really not much you can do about that. In addition to the 14.5 per cent, they will ask manager’s fees and all of that. You go to the oversea equivalent of the same bank, same name, same everything. You come back with 8.95 per cent,” Osahon said.

He explained that while overseas terms are less tough, the banks limit exposure due to country risk, offering for instance $8 million when a company seeks $20 million to avoid default linked to operating environment.

In Nigeria, he said, high rates combined with unrestricted lending push operators into non-performing loans (NPLs) and delayed payments to service providers, not because operators do not want to pay.

Osahon said early local content practice also slowed service sector growth, as some operators awarded jobs to local contractors but paid equivalent value to overseas contractors, undermining real capacity development.

He however said it would be unfair to label Nigerian service providers as incompetent, recalling that the Petroleum Technology Association of Nigeria (PETAN) members single-handedly developed OML 79 efficiently before the industry downturn dispersed the team.

On production ramp-up, the Energia Chairman said ramping up is not about rolling up sleeves, but hinges on finance, clear subsurface understanding, technology and competencies.

He disclosed that a former staff who moved to Brazil told him his team now uses Artificial Intelligence to the point where after AI works, a mathematician must validate before drilling proceeds, while another company uses AI to identify and high-grade prospects before testing.

“We haven’t got there yet,” he said, noting that without such tools, drilling outcomes remain uncertain and failure makes recovery harder.

He added that ramp-up is easier with large assets with multiple compartments where water or gas injection can quickly add barrels, but more challenging for independents with limited assets.

Energia, he said, has built reputation for operational excellence, safety and sustainable development, delivering reliable energy while creating value for host communities, but requires aligned financing, technology adoption and competency development to accelerate growth in line with national energy security aspirations.

World.title: UBA Commences Comtempt Proceedings Against WEMPCO Directors over Alleged Disobidence of Court Order
World.content:
The Federal High Court, presided over by Honourable Justice Aluko, has granted an application by United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc for substituted service of Form 49 on directors of Wempco named as alleged contemnors in the case of UBA v. Wempco.

The application forms part of proceedings seeking to determine whether the named individuals disobeyed an order of the court and whether they should be committed to prison for contempt.

The directors named as alleged contemnors are Lewis Shui Ngor Tung, Phillip Shui Chei Tung, M.A. Ola Yusuf, Tung Lawrence Blake, Aali Aare Hadji Tokunbo, Paul Shui Po Tung, Tung Robert, C.L. Ip and Taiwo Alli.

In advancing the application, counsel to UBA argued that service of Form 49 on the alleged contemnors was necessary to enable them to appear before the court and show cause why an order of committal should not be made against them.

He also argued that the Directors of Wempco and some members of staff took illegal steps in an attempt to disobey the Order of Court.

The court’s decision to grant substituted service provides a procedural step towards bringing the notice to the attention of the individuals concerned in accordance with the court’s directions.

Form 49 is a notice requiring an alleged contemnor to show cause why an order of committal to prison should not be made against them for alleged disobedience of a court order.

The Federal High Court had earlier made an Order of Mareva Injunction and appointed a Receiver/Manager over some of the Assets of Wempco following the indebtedness of Wempco to UBA in the sum of N61,445,695,993.76 (Sixty One Billion FourHundred and Forty-Five Million Six Hundred and Ninety Five Thousand, Nine Hundred and Ninety Three Naira, Seventy Six Kobo).

World.title: FG Targets March 2027 for Completion of 132/33kV Substation in Katsina
World.content:
• Unveils 132/33kV power transformers

The Federal Government has fixed March 2027 for the completion of a new 132/33kV transmission substation in Mashi Local Government Area of Katsina State, as part of efforts to strengthen electricity supply and boost economic activities across the state.

The Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, disclosed this on Friday during the groundbreaking ceremony for the project in Garo, Mashi LGA, noting that compensation for affected properties had been fully paid before the commencement of construction.

The project, being executed through the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), comprises 2x60MVA transformers, providing a combined transmission capacity of 120MVA, equivalent to 96 megawatts.

The minister also unveiled 2×60MVA, 132/33kV power transformers in Kankia Local Government Area of the state, as part of efforts to strengthen electricity infrastructure in the state.

He also inspected the 2x100MVA, 132/33kV GIS transmission substation project at Katsina 330/132/33kV substation alongside Governor Dikko Umaru Radda and other top federal and state governments officials.

Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony in Garo, Tegbe said the Mashi substation would enhance the transmission network’s capacity to deliver available electricity to Katsina and its environs upon completion.

“The Federal Government, through the Transmission Company of Nigeria, is providing this new 2×60MVA, 132/33kV transmission substation.

“On completion, it will provide 120MVA of transmission capacity, equivalent to 96 megawatts. This will strengthen the network’s ability to deliver available electricity within Katsina and its environs and support productive activity and household welfare,” he said.

Tegbe urged TCN, the contractor and supervising engineers to ensure strict adherence to the March 2027 completion deadline, while maintaining high standards of workmanship and safety throughout the construction process.

He stressed that every phase of the project, including equipment manufacturing, civil works, installation and testing, must comply with the required technical standards to prevent defects and ensure the facility’s long-term reliability.

The minister described the substation as part of the Federal Government’s commitment to providing critical infrastructure to support enterprise, employment generation and economic prosperity.

He commended President Bola Tinubu for supporting investments in the power sector, adding that dependable infrastructure was essential to achieving the country’s economic development objectives.

He called on residents of Mashi to cooperate with the construction team, protect the facility and report suspicious activities around the project site to safeguard the infrastructure and facilitate its timely completion.

He urged all institutions involved to ensure that the groundbreaking ceremony translated into measurable progress, while keeping the host community informed throughout the construction and inauguration process.

In his remarks, Governor Radda commended President Tinubu for approving three transmission substation projects in the state to strengthen electricity transmission and supply to the growing population.

Radda described the projects as significant investments in the state’s economic development and expressed appreciation to the president for extending critical infrastructure to the state.

He said the Federal Government’s intervention demonstrated its commitment to improving electricity infrastructure and supporting economic growth.

World.title: Scottland FC crash out of CAF Champions League after Petro defeat
World.content:
Zimbabwean champions Scottland FC have been eliminated from the CAF Champions League after suffering a 3-0 defeat to Angola’s Petro de Luanda in the second leg of their tie.

Scottland went into the return leg with a 2-0 advantage after winning the first leg in Harare last weekend.

However, they were unable to protect their lead as Petro turned the tie around to advance at the Zimbabwean champions’ expense.



The 3-0 defeat means Scottland lost the tie 3-2 on aggregate, bringing their continental campaign to an end.

Scottland fail to hold on to first-leg advantage

Scottland had given themselves an opportunity to progress after securing a narrow victory on home soil in the first leg.

That result left the Zimbabwean side needing to avoid defeat by more than one goal in the return fixture to keep their hopes of advancing alive.



However, Petro proved too strong in the second leg, scoring three unanswered goals to overturn the deficit and secure their place in the next round.

For Scottland, the result represents a disappointing end to their bid to make progress in Africa’s premier club competition.

Petro de Luanda advance at Scottland’s expense

Petro de Luanda are among Angola’s established football clubs and have experience competing in continental competitions.



Their victory over Scottland underlines the challenge Zimbabwean clubs face when competing against some of the continent’s more experienced sides.

Scottland will now turn their attention to domestic football after their Champions League journey came to an abrupt end.

The defeat also means Zimbabwe’s defending champions will have to reflect on their continental campaign, particularly after entering the second leg with an advantage.



Further details about the match, including the goal scorers and the timing of Petro’s goals, can be added once confirmed by official match reports.

World.title: Muizenberg beachfront project: St James Walkway, parking area now open [video]
World.content:
The project is on track with the bulk of the work to be completed by the builders' break in December. Image: CoCT

Muizenberg beachgoers have more reason to celebrate, with the opening of the upgraded St James Walkway access and western parking area.

The latest milestone brings the Muizenberg beachfront revamp closer to completion ahead of the festive season.

Visitors can now access the western side of the beach from Surfer’s Corner. The City says the project remains on track, with most of the work expected to be completed by mid-December.



Muizenberg beachfront parking area reopens

The newly-paved parking area is located on the western side of the beachfront, next to the railway line. It features new kerbing made with recycled plastic, benches and provisions for streetlights.

Universal-access parking and pedestrian walkways have also been incorporated into the upgrade. The streetlights will be switched on once the project is complete.

“The festive season is around the corner and I’m sure locals and visitors to the Muizenberg beachfront will be super excited to hear that we are now in the final phase of the upgrade project,” said Eddie Andrews, Cape Town’s Deputy Mayor, on Friday.

“Earlier this morning, we celebrated a massive milestone with the opening of the beach access to the St James Walkway at Surfer’s Corner.”

Alderman Eddie Andrews and local ward councillor Izabel Sherry. Image: CoCT

What remains in the beachfront upgrade?

The refurbishments in Muizenberg began in February 2025 and is now more than 84% complete. The project includes replacing ageing seawalls and upgrading public amenities.



Work still under way includes construction of the new central ablution facility and improvements to the Shark Spotters and Adaptive Surfing buildings.

The remaining sections of the old seawall are also being removed. Meanwhile, construction continues on the stepped revetment, pergola, planters and seating areas.

Work has also started on the playground. About 85% of the precast steps and promenade units have been installed, providing coastal protection and beach access at different levels.

Andrews thanked residents, businesses and regular beach visitors for their patience during construction.

“There has been a lot of noise, movement, and machinery on site, and this work is having an impact on beach access in particular,” added Andrews, who is also the City’s Mayco Member for Spatial Planning.

“This is a mammoth project, but we are nearly there and are as excited to see the upgrades and improvements concluded.”

World.title: CAF Confed Cup: Kaizer Chiefs starting XI for Red Arrows clash
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs host Red Arrows in the second leg of the CAF Confederation Cup at Moses Mabhida Stadium on Friday.

Kick-off is at 18:00.

Amakhosi need to win by a two-goal margin to advance to the group stage of the CAF Confederation Cup.

Should Fernando da Cruz’s men succeed in their mission to beat Red Arrows on the night, they would make the group stage for the second season in a row.

World.title: Eskom announces a 9-hour power outage in parts of Gauteng on Sunday
World.content:
Silhouette of power lines and pole against a vibrant sunset sky. Image: Pexels

Eskom has announced a nine-hour power outage in parts of Soweto this weekend.

The power utility says the outage is due to emergency maintenance on its distribution network.

Areas affected by the POwer outage

The interruption will affect customers in Old Dobsonville Extensions 2, 4 and 5.



Eskom will cut the power on Sunday, 25 October, from 9:00 to 18:00.

According to Eskom, the power outage is necessary to carry out essential maintenance on its distribution power lines.

The notice was issued by Eskom’s Gauteng Communication and Stakeholder Management team.



Safety warning for residents

Eskom is urging affected customers to treat all electrical appliances as live at all times during the power outage.

This means residents should not assume appliances are safe to handle simply because the power is off, as electricity could be restored at any time.

The power utility thanked customers for their cooperation and apologised for any inconvenience the maintenance may cause.



Eskom also cautioned that the planned maintenance may not go ahead as communicated if circumstances beyond its control arise.

Customers who need assistance or want to report problems can reach Eskom through several channels:

Download the self-help MyEskom Customer app

WhatsApp Eskom on 0860 037 566

Dial the USSD code *120*3756#

Check bill-related enquiries online at csonline.eskom.co.za, Monday to Friday, from 8:00 to 16:00

Call the Eskom Contact Centre on 08600 37566 for supply-related enquiries, available 24 hours a day

Residents in the affected areas are encouraged to plan for the outage by charging devices and preparing meals before 9:00 on Sunday.

World.title: LIVE | Orlando Pirates vs African Stars – CAF Champions League
World.content:
Orlando Pirates will look to complete the job against Namibia’s African Stars when the sides meet at Orlando Amstel Arena on Friday. Image: Orlando Pirates website

Orlando Pirates will look to complete the job against Namibia’s African Stars when the sides meet at Orlando Amstel Arena on Friday, 23 October with a place in the CAF Champions League group stage at stake.

The Buccaneers head into the second leg with a slender advantage after Tshepang Moremi scored in the 75th minute to secure a 1-0 victory in the first leg in Gaborone.

LIVE | Kaizer Chiefs vs Red Arrows – CAF Confederation Cup



The result puts the Soweto giants in a strong position, but they will need another disciplined performance to secure progression to the next stage of the continental competition.

Kick-off is scheduled for 20:00, with Orlando Pirates hoping to make home advantage count in the decisive encounter.

ORLANDO Pirates hold the advantage

The two sides have developed a history of tight encounters, with Friday’s fixture marking their fourth meeting.

Their three previous matches have produced just two goals, both scored by Orlando Pirates. The Buccaneers also edged their 2018/19 CAF Champions League preliminary-round tie 1-0 on aggregate.

Justin Shonga scored in the away leg after the first meeting in Soweto ended goalless.

That history suggests another closely contested encounter could be on the cards, particularly with African Stars needing to overturn the first-leg deficit.



Orlando Pirates will advance with a win or a draw. If African Stars win by one goal, the aggregate score will be level and the tie will go to a penalty shootout. A victory by two or more goals would send the Namibian side through.

Defensive discipline could prove decisive

Orlando Pirates will take confidence from their defensive record at Orlando Amstel Arena, where they have conceded just twice this season.

Durban City scored against them in the MTN8, while La Cure Waves also found the net in the previous round of the CAF Champions League.

Maintaining that defensive solidity will be important against an African Stars side that showed its ability to frustrate Orlando Pirates for much of the opening leg.

The visitors held firm for 75 minutes in Gaborone before Moremi found the breakthrough. They will need another organised display in Johannesburg, alongside a greater attacking threat, if they are to keep their continental campaign alive.

African Stars have already shown they can recover from a difficult position. In the previous round, they overturned a 3-1 first-leg defeat to Gabonese side AS Mangasport by winning the return match 2-0.

Goals from Lawrence Doaseb and Liam April levelled the aggregate score and helped the Namibian side progress on away goals.

That comeback offers a reminder that Orlando Pirates cannot afford to underestimate their opponents.

Buccaneers aiming to finish the job

Orlando Pirates have also demonstrated their ability to respond under pressure in this season’s competition.

After drawing 0-0 away to La Cure Waves, they returned home to claim a 3-1 victory and secure their place in the current round.

They will now aim to build on their first-leg advantage and avoid giving African Stars an opportunity to force their way back into the tie.

The Buccaneers must balance protecting their lead with the need to remain a threat going forward. African Stars, meanwhile, will have to find a way past a defence that has been difficult to breach at home.

With so little separating the teams, patience, defensive organisation and clinical finishing could determine which side advances.

Orlando Pirates vs African Stars: TV and tickets

The second-leg encounter will take place at Orlando Amstel Arena on Friday.

Kick-off: 20:00

20:00 TV: SuperSport PSL and SABC 2

SuperSport PSL and SABC 2 Tickets: Available online through OpenTickets

Live updates will also be available across Orlando Pirates’ social media platforms.

The Buccaneers have secured the first-leg advantage. They now need to turn it into progression and move one step closer to the CAF Champions League group stage.

Will Orlando Pirates get the job done tonight?

World.title: LIVE | Kaizer Chiefs vs Red Arrows – CAF Confederation Cup
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz is confident that Amakhosi have the quality and desire to overturn the 1-0 first-leg deficit against Red Arrows of Zambia. Image: Kaizer Chiefs website

Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz and his skipper Inacio Miguel are both confident that Amakhosi have the quality and desire to overturn the 1-0 first-leg deficit against Red Arrows of Zambia when the teams clash in the second leg at Moses Mabhida stadium in Durban on Friday, with a berth in the Group stage of the 2026/27 CAF Confederation Cup on the line.

Explainer | What Kaizer Chiefs need to do to reach CAF group stage

‘Very good team’

The French coach said, “We faced a very good team, as I mentioned before the first leg. It was a tough game in Zambia. Unfortunately, we conceded one goal from a set piece near the end so now our only objective is to qualify for the group stage.”



Miguel concurred, pointing out, “As the coach said, we were aware of the quality of this Red Arrows team. I don’t think we did as badly as people think. We conceded from a set piece, which is part of the game, but in general play I think we managed them quite well, only to lose concentration at one corner, which was costly. Still, nothing is lost yet, and we have already proved this season that we are capable of turning the tie around.”

Addressing the concession of the decisive goal from a set piece, Miguel added, “As a defender and captain, leadership and organisation is key and it is my responsibility if we concede from a corner. It is something that we constantly work to improve on and minimise our mistakes.”

‘Practiced all aspects of the game’

Da Cruz also mentioned when questioned whether they had paid particular attention to set pieces in training, “We have practiced all aspects of the game during the week, including set pieces, particularly on concentration and aggression.”



With hints of doubt being raised in some quarters of the media and fanbase, Da Cruz acknowledged his awareness of what it means to coach Kaizer Chiefs.

“From the day I took this job, I knew the pressure was very high and I put pressure on myself every day because I demand high standards of myself,” he revealed.

“We try, step by step, to improve our level to what we expect and what the fans expect. I am completely focused on the team because what is most important is to make the fans happy.”



Fans can be disappointed

He continued, “I understand that fans can be disappointed but it is always important to analyse the context; we have some important players out injured. It’s not an excuse, but it’s a fact and that should be kept in mind. We need our supporters behind us to push us and, on our side, to stay focused on our job, the football.”

Miguel reiterated the crucial role played by the fans follow and support the team, creating a motivating atmosphere that drives the players on.

“Sometimes a team goes through a difficult phase. Our supporters are our 12th man and we need them, especially tomorrow, to come to the game,” he said.



“I think we need to stick together from the first whistle to the last and we will give everything to do the job on the field. We are truly grateful to our fans for their loyalty and support, and we will fight to get the victory.”

Widespread attention

In reference to the ‘robust conversation’ between Reeve Frosler and Renaldo Leaner after the final whistle in Ndola last weekend that drew fairly widespread attention on social media, Da Cruz said, “There was no problem. It is common in football, especially when passion is strong that these things happen, but we didn’t need to speak to the players because there was no issue.”

Concluding with the approach for the encounter, Da Cruz offered, “It is imperative for us to score the first goal and afterwards, depending on the game situation, we will think about the second goal. However, it all hinges on getting the first goal.”



Tickets for the second leg clash are available through Computicket, as well as at Shoprite and Checkers outlets nationwide for R80.

Suite tickets are available for R1 699 and R2 899, and can be purchased through the MMS via email MMS.Hospitality@durban.gov.za or phone at 031 322 3115.

The fixture is scheduled for Friday, 23 October, at the Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban, with kick-off at 18:00.



Will Kaizer Chiefs do enough to progress to the CAF Confederation Cup group stage?

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs congratulate club legend Doctor Khumalo on SAFA job
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have congratulated club legend Doctor Khumalo following his appointment as vice-chairperson of the SAFA Technical Committee. Image: Kaizer Chiefs website

Kaizer Chiefs have congratulated club legend Doctor Khumalo following his appointment as vice-chairperson of the South African Football Association’s (SAFA) Technical Committee.

The former Amakhosi midfielder will serve under chairperson Jack Maluleke after his appointment was confirmed at a meeting of SAFA’s National Executive Committee in Sandton, Johannesburg, last Sunday.

‘Happy to serve on the committee’

SAFA president Danny Jordaan confirmed that Doctor Khumalo had accepted the role, saying he was happy to serve on the committee.



Khumalo visited the club’s Naturena headquarters on Wednesday, where he spent time with chairman Dr Kaizer Motaung and interacted with the first-team coaching staff and players.

Speaking about his new responsibilities, Khumalo expressed gratitude for the opportunity to contribute his experience to South African football.

“I am grateful to have been added to the SAFA committee and I am hoping to add value via my experience. Thanks to the Chiefs Chairman for hosting me and imparting his wisdom as I take on this new role,” Khumalo said.

Motaung also congratulated Doctor Khumalo, highlighting the knowledge and experience he brings to the football structures.

“Doctor is very knowledgeable in the game. He will take all that he has developed in a career spanning over many years as a player and coach with him to the SAFA structures. We wish him well and are hoping to have a longer session with him in the next couple of weeks,” Motaung said.

A lasting legacy at Kaizer Chiefs

Khumalo remains one of the most celebrated figures in Kaizer Chiefs’ history, having spent more than 15 years with the club.



During his time at Naturena, he made over 400 appearances and won 21 titles, establishing himself as a key figure in the club’s history.

His achievements also extended to the international stage. Khumalo made his Bafana Bafana debut in 1992, scoring against Cameroon in a 1-0 victory, before playing an important role in South Africa’s 1996 Africa Cup of Nations triumph.

His appointment to SAFA’s Technical Committee offers another opportunity for the former midfielder to put his football experience to use.

World.title: Beyond Game Day | Temba Bavuma Silences His Critics — But Who Is Failing SA Sport? | 23 October 2026
World.content:
South African Athletes Keep Delivering. The System Behind Them Must Do Better.

South African sport has a remarkable ability to produce moments of national unity. When the Proteas compete, the Springboks win or an athlete succeeds on the international stage, divisions briefly give way to a shared sense of achievement. But

those celebrations can obscure a more uncomfortable question: are South Africa's sporting structures doing enough to sustain the success they celebrate?

The distinction matters because elite performance is the visible end of a much longer journey. Behind an international medal, a Test century or a World Cup victory lie years of coaching, competitive opportunities, access to facilities and financial support. When that system works, talent has room to develop. When it fails, athletes are often left to compensate through extraordinary individual effort.

Success Should Not Excuse Poor Administration

There is a temptation to regard winning as proof that a country's sporting system is healthy. Yet exceptional athletes can succeed despite institutional weaknesses, not necessarily because those institutions have enabled them.

South Africa's sporting achievements are particularly striking against the country's economic and social challenges. That should inspire admiration for those who compete at the highest level. It should also sharpen public scrutiny of the organisations responsible for developing the next generation.

In a discussion on Beyond Game Day, Vata Ngobeni argues that South Africa is "punching way above its weight". It is an observation that captures both national pride and the danger of complacency. If outstanding performances are possible under difficult circumstances, what might be achieved with stronger and more consistent support?

The governance questions raised around Athletics South Africa illustrate why administrative matters cannot be dismissed as internal politics. Rules, elections, compliance and accountability may seem remote from competition, but instability in a federation can affect athletes' preparation, access to events and confidence in the institutions representing them.

The Funding Question Is Bigger Than One Event

Major sporting events attract attention, visitors and commercial opportunities. They can have legitimate value. But public spending decisions should be judged against clear objectives and measurable outcomes, especially when development programmes and sporting bodies are also competing for limited resources.

A high-profile tournament and a grassroots development programme do not serve identical purposes. One may offer immediate visibility; the other may create opportunities that would otherwise never exist. Good sports policy recognises both while being transparent about what taxpayers are funding and how success will be measured.

That means asking whether spending reaches athletes, coaches and communities beyond the event itself. Promises of wider benefits should not be treated as substitutes for evidence that those benefits have materialised.

Who Is Accountable When the System Fails?

Reforming sport is more complicated than replacing a federation president or demanding ministerial intervention. Many sporting bodies operate under international rules designed to protect their independence from political interference. This creates a difficult balance: the public has a legitimate interest in how sport is governed, but direct government control may carry consequences for international participation.

The answer cannot be to abandon accountability. Instead, sporting organisations need credible internal governance, transparent decision-making and mechanisms that allow members to challenge ineffective leadership. Government, meanwhile, has responsibilities as a funder, policymaker and guardian of the public interest.

The central test is not whether administrators can point to the latest sporting triumph. It is whether they are creating conditions in which success becomes more

accessible, more sustainable and less dependent on exceptional individuals overcoming avoidable obstacles.

South Africa has no shortage of sporting talent or passion. Its challenge is to ensure that the institutions entrusted with both are worthy of the people they serve.
