This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How Presto Reached Liquidation

Presto’s operator, Franquicias y Concesiones S.A.S., known as Frayco, entered insolvency under Law 1116 in July 2023. In April 2026 the Superintendency of Companies confirmed a creditor deal backed by 81.39% of creditors.

That deal covered debts of about COP 31,000 million (US$9.7 million) over six years. It failed, and on 30 September Frayco itself asked for liquidation, citing lost going-concern status and weak cash flow.

On 13 October the Superintendency ordered judicial liquidation and named Mónica Macías as liquidator. It reported assets of about COP 46,943 million (US$14.7 million), according to Infobae and El Espectador.

Six days later it allowed the restaurants and plant to stay open so the business could be sold as a working unit. Nutresa’s purchase came three days after that.

What Nutresa Gets in the Presto Unit

Nutresa is buying a productive economic unit, a route that lets a buyer keep outlets without the debts and lawsuits, Infobae reports. Infobae says Presto had 180 outlets before the insolvency process began.

The unit has 114 outlets, 86 open and 28 closed, plus a plant, centres in 29 cities and a Bogotá logistics hub. The court file listed 599 employees when the liquidator asked to keep operations running.

From January to September 2026 the unit earned EBITDA of COP 1,994 million (about US$0.6 million). Its 51 profitable outlets earned COP 5,464 million, while the other 63 lost COP 3,469 million.

Over the 12 months to September, EBITDA was COP 6,800 million (about US$2.1 million), La República reports from the court file. EBITDA is earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation.

Presto’s 2025 revenue was COP 108,629 million (US$34.1 million), against about COP 139,077 million (US$43.7 million) before the pandemic. For context, see Nutresa’s first-half results, its Tío Rico ice cream purchase and the Grupo Nutresa company page.

Colombia’s Burger Market After Presto

In 2025 El Corral led Colombian burger chains with revenue of COP 791,204 million (US$248.5 million) and 292 outlets. McDonald’s was second with COP 759,836 million (US$238.6 million) and 284 outlets.

Burger King had COP 139,740 million (US$43.9 million) from 40 outlets, and Presto ranked fourth. La República counts 156 registered Presto outlets, more than the 114 in the unit.

El Corral and Presto together booked COP 899,833 million (US$282.6 million) in 2025. That is about COP 140,000 million (US$44 million) above McDonald’s, the next-largest rival.

Portafolio lists five other recent Nutresa deals: Tío Rico, Universal Sweet Industries, Empaques Industriales de Colombia, Inversionista Alcora and the Mimo’s business. The Tío Rico and Universal Sweet Industries deals are conditional on closing; more is in the Colombia section.

What It Means for US Readers

McDonald’s and Burger King, both US brands, rank second and third by revenue in Colombia’s burger market. A larger Nutresa chain would face them with more outlets and a shared supply base.

Papa John’s, a US pizza brand, is already in Nutresa’s restaurant unit. Nothing in the reports names any US investment or financing in the Presto deal.

What Is Not Known

The price and the closing date were not disclosed, and Nutresa’s own filing with the financial regulator could not be opened. The account here rests on Nutresa’s statement as published by Colombian outlets.

It is unclear whether the competition regulator, the SIC, will review the deal. Infobae says the SIC had not said, and it approved Nutresa’s 2014 El Corral purchase without conditions.

Job numbers differ. President Abelardo de la Espriella said on X that 700 jobs are saved, while the court file showed 599 employees.

What Comes Next

Nutresa says it will define the relaunch plan in the coming weeks and keep the restaurants open. Infobae says closing is subject to the usual conditions for such deals.

Watch for the price, the regulator’s stance and which of the 28 closed outlets, if any, reopen. None of these has been announced.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Grupo Nutresa buy from Presto?

On 22 October 2026 it signed a contract for the Presto brand and its productive unit. That covers outlets, a plant and production centres, and no price was disclosed.

Why was Presto in liquidation?

Its operator Frayco failed to meet a creditor deal and asked for liquidation on 30 September. The Superintendency of Companies ordered it on 13 October.

Will Presto restaurants stay open?

Nutresa says the restaurants will keep operating normally while it prepares a relaunch. Presto will run as an independent brand.

How many Presto outlets does the deal cover?

Court-file figures cite 114 outlets, 86 open and 28 closed, while news reports count 156 registered locations. The sources do not reconcile the two numbers.

Does the deal need regulatory approval?

That is not known. Infobae says the competition regulator had not said whether it will review the purchase.

Sources: Blu Radio, 22 October 2026; La República, 22 October 2026; Infobae, 23 October 2026; El Espectador, 23 October 2026; Portafolio, 23 October 2026 (all citing the Nutresa statement and the Frayco liquidation file); open.er-api.com exchange rates, 23 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026).

World.title: South Africa Election Body Fights Fake News
World.content:
Johannesburg's inner city at dusk, seen from the Carlton Centre, pictured in June 2015. Photo: Andrew Moore / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

Published Friday, 23 October, 12:27 p.m. ET (6:27 p.m. Johannesburg) · Source: Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC), South African Government

South Africa’s Electoral Commission (the IEC, the independent body that runs elections) has partnered with Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa to fight false election content. Reports on the partnership appeared on 20 and 21 October, about two weeks before voting on Wednesday, 4 November 2026.

It is part of our coverage in the South Africa local elections 2026 updates. The vote chooses municipal councils, including Johannesburg, Durban and Nelson Mandela Bay.

Key Facts What: The IEC partnered with Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa against election falsehoods.

The IEC partnered with Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa against election falsehoods. When: Voting is Wednesday, 4 November 2026; special voting is 2 and 3 November.

Voting is Wednesday, 4 November 2026; special voting is 2 and 3 November. Special votes: 2,655,067 applications approved by 14 October, up 131% from 2021.

2,655,067 applications approved by 14 October, up 131% from 2021. Ballots: A court ruling forced 6.6 million extra ballots; printing should end by 30 October.

A court ruling forced 6.6 million extra ballots; printing should end by 30 October. Prediction markets: Polymarket: Helen Zille 54.0% for Johannesburg mayor, as of 12:27 p.m. ET, 23 October.

In plain English The IEC is South Africa’s independent election referee. Real411 is its public site and app where people can report misleading election posts.

Tech Platforms Join the IEC Effort

The commission has named its Real411 platform as the place for the public to report misleading election content. Complaints can be filed in all 11 official languages through the website or the mobile app.

The IEC also gazetted an Election Code of Conduct Countering Disinformation on 4 September 2026. Reports do not say how many posts or accounts have been removed, investigated or referred for prosecution.

File photo: Sandton, Johannesburg’s business district, seen across the city’s suburbs.

Election Readiness in Numbers

The IEC reported 2,655,067 approved special-vote applications by 14 October, up 131% from 1,147,759 at the comparable 2021 election. Special voting takes place on 2 and 3 November.

The IEC had printed more than 66% of about 79 million ballot papers by 14 October. A Constitutional Court ruling that reinstated 181 ANC candidates then forced it to print 6.6 million extra ballots, and Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo expects printing to finish by 30 October.

The IEC is preparing 23,696 voting stations. Voters can only vote at the station where they are registered.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, traders put Helen Zille at 54.0% to be Johannesburg’s next mayor, ahead of David Makhura at 12.6%, Frank Chikane at 8.4% and Herman Mashaba at 7.1%. About US$133,000 had been traded across the event’s markets as of 12:27 p.m. ET on 23 October.

Prices are bets, not polls. They reflect who traders expect to win the mayor’s office, not a party’s vote share.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Polls and Positions

Analyst Melanie Verwoerd said the Democratic Alliance (DA), the party that runs Cape Town, appeared well placed to keep the city. She warned that other big councils could end up in coalition talks.

Deputy Chief Electoral Officer Masego Sheburi said the IEC had finished its voting-district review and was finalising venue leases. The IEC’s call to voters is “Get up. Show up. VOTE.”

What It Means for US Readers

Johannesburg is South Africa’s largest city, so who runs its council matters for water and power services. Verwoerd’s warning means coalition talks could follow the vote.

US readers will know the debate over how platforms police election falsehoods. How well the IEC’s channels work will only be clear once complaint figures are published.

What Is Not Known

The number of complaints, platform removals and referrals to police has not been disclosed. It is also unclear whether the extra ballots will be ready by the 30 October target.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is South Africa's local government election?

Voting day is Wednesday, 4 November 2026, with special voting on 2 and 3 November. Voters can only vote at the station where they are registered.

What is the IEC doing about election misinformation?

It has partnered with Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa. The public can report misleading content on the Real411 platform in all 11 official languages.

How many people applied for special votes?

The IEC approved 2,655,067 special-vote applications by 14 October. That is 131% more than the 1,147,759 approved for the 2021 election.

Who do prediction markets favour in Johannesburg?

Polymarket traders gave Helen Zille 54.0% for mayor on 23 October. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move quickly.

Sources: IEC · South African Government · South African Government · The Citizen · EWN · Polymarket

World.title: Mexico City Day of the Dead Seen at US$664M
World.content:
Candles on the graves of San Andrés Mixquic's cemetery, seen from the roof of the San Andrés Apóstol church, pictured on 2 November 2009. Photo: Thelmadatter / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

Published Friday, 23 October, 12:27 p.m. ET (10:27 a.m. Mexico City) · Source: Coparmex Ciudad de México, La Jornada

It lands ten days before the capital’s parade and adds to our Day of the Dead 2026 updates. Day of the Dead is Mexico’s 1 and 2 November holiday honouring the dead with home altars, flowers and special bread.

Key Facts What: Mexico City employers forecast 12.4 billion pesos (about US$664 million) from Day of the Dead.

World.title: Tunisia Geopolitics Explained 2026
World.content:
TUNISIA · GEOPOLITICS

Key Facts — What is happening President Kais Saied, who won a second term on Sunday, 6 October 2024 with 90.69% of the vote, is balancing a trade system tied to Europe against growing links with China, Algeria, Turkey and the Gulf in October 2026.

— Why it matters Europe took 70.2% of Tunisian exports in the first nine months of 2026, yet no IMF loan approval has been found, so loans, migration controls and energy supplies give outside powers leverage in Tunis.

— The numbers Tunisia ran a trade deficit of 21.0 billion dinars (about US$7.0 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, and China supplied 12.6% of imports, Italy 11.8% and Algeria 7.1%.

— Who is who Saied holds executive power, Prime Minister Sarra Zaafrani Zenzri heads the government, Foreign Minister Mohamed Ali Nafti leads diplomacy, and Brahim Bouderbala presides over the parliament in Tunis.

— What to watch Watch the next joint commission with Algeria, any partnership deal with China, the new electoral law before parliament, and whether Tunis ever reopens talks with the IMF.

— What it means for you US goods exports to Tunisia were US$589.6 million in 2025 and imports US$1.01 billion, so tariffs, olive oil prices and military training ties are the main points of contact for US readers.

Europe is the market, Washington the training partner and Beijing the supplier, while Algiers and the Gulf offer a cushion. Here is what each power wants from Tunis in October 2026.

Tunisia geopolitics in October 2026 is a balancing act between Europe, which buys 70.2% of exports, and a widening circle of partners. President Kais Saied rejects outside conditions, yet the country still depends on European markets, imported energy and Chinese goods.

This guide sets out what each outside power wants, from loans and military training to phosphates and trade. Every figure carries its date.

More coverage sits on the Rio Times Tunisia page. Conversions use 2.9987 dinars and 0.8915 euros per US$1, the open.er-api.com rate of 23 October 2026 (00:02 UTC).

Who Holds Power in Tunis

Kais Saied won the presidential election of Sunday, 6 October 2024 with 2,438,954 votes, or 90.69%. The electoral commission ISIE announced the final result on Friday, 11 October 2024.

Saied has ruled in a strong presidential system since he suspended parliament on Sunday, 25 July 2021. Critics say he has narrowed political space since then.

The Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy, a Washington research group, wrote in July 2026 that some Western ties had grown strained. It added that Tunis has sought partners beyond its traditional allies.

Sarra Zaafrani Zenzri, appointed head of government in March 2025, chaired government meetings on 8 October 2026, the prime minister’s office shows. Brahim Bouderbala, president of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People, chaired its bureau on Friday, 16 October 2026.

Mohamed Ali Nafti is Foreign Minister, and Khaled Shili is Defence Minister. Both appeared in official reports in July and August 2026.

For the domestic picture, read the Rio Times Tunisia explained guide. This pillar focuses on what outsiders want.

Tunisia Geopolitics at a Glance

The list below summarises each relationship using only what the sources checked can confirm. Details and dates follow in the sections after it.

European Union and Italy: 70.2% of exports, EU grants, the ELMED power link to Italy and migration cooperation.

70.2% of exports, EU grants, the ELMED power link to Italy and migration cooperation. United States: goods trade, the African Lion exercise, defence talks, and no Section 301 tariff surcharge on Tunisian goods.

goods trade, the African Lion exercise, defence talks, and no Section 301 tariff surcharge on Tunisian goods. China: 12.6% of imports, a temporary zero duty offer, a bridge, a cancer centre and partnership talks.

12.6% of imports, a temporary zero duty offer, a bridge, a cancer centre and partnership talks. Russia: the 70th anniversary of ties in July 2026, and imports from Russia down 54%.

the 70th anniversary of ties in July 2026, and imports from Russia down 54%. Turkey and India: Turkish imports up 6.7%, and an Indian phosphate and fertiliser joint venture.

Turkish imports up 6.7%, and an Indian phosphate and fertiliser joint venture. Gulf states: exports to Saudi Arabia up 52.1%, Saudi Fund talks, and no confirmed Qatar or UAE deal.

exports to Saudi Arabia up 52.1%, Saudi Fund talks, and no confirmed Qatar or UAE deal. Algeria and Libya: a roadmap with Algiers in July 2026 and a border corridor plan with Tripoli.

a roadmap with Algiers in July 2026 and a border corridor plan with Tripoli. BRICS: no membership or application confirmed.

The European Union and Italy, the Anchor Market

The European Union took 35.4 billion dinars (about US$11.8 billion) of Tunisian goods from January to September 2026, or 70.2% of exports. The National Statistics Institute, INS, says that compares with 32.6 billion dinars a year earlier.

France took 22.7% of exports, Italy 16.6%, Germany 14.0% and Spain 5.3%. Imports from the EU were 32.0 billion dinars (about US$10.7 billion), or 44.8% of the total.

Italy supplied 11.8% of Tunisian imports, second only to China, ahead of France at 11.4% and Germany at 7.9%. Imports from France and Italy rose 18.1% and 18.6%.

The EU says it has mobilised over 600 million euros (about US$673 million) in grants since its 2023 partnership with Tunisia. Commissioner Dubravka Šuica made the statement in Tunis in October 2025.

The European Commission’s June 2023 package listed up to 900 million euros (about US$1.01 billion) of loans tied to an IMF programme. It listed 150 million euros (about US$168 million) of 2023 aid and 105 million euros (about US$118 million) for migration.

The memorandum signed in Tunis on Sunday, 16 July 2023 names only a 307 million euro (about US$344 million) ELMED grant. It states no other amounts.

The EU says departures from Tunisia fell 80% in 2024 against 2023. It says they fell a further 86% in 2025 against the same period of 2024.

The EU also announced a 12 million euro (about US$13.5 million) European Investment Bank grant to STEG, the state power utility. It backs ELMED, a planned power cable to Italy meant to allow green electricity exports to Europe by 2040.

The EU calls itself Tunisia’s largest investor and trade partner and links European firms to over 400,000 jobs. The statement also noted the 30th anniversary of the EU Tunisia Association Agreement.

The record points to what Brussels and Rome want: fewer boat departures, stable energy links and open markets. For the Mediterranean setting, see the guide to Tunisia and its neighbours in North Africa.

The United States, Trade and Training

US Census Bureau data show US goods exports to Tunisia of US$589.6 million in 2025 and imports of US$1.01 billion. That left a US deficit of US$424.4 million.

From January to August 2026 US exports were US$407.0 million and imports US$850.9 million. The US deficit for those eight months was US$444.0 million.

The US Trade Representative opened Section 301 forced labour investigations into 60 economies in March 2026. Tunisia was not among them, while Algeria, Egypt, Libya and Morocco were.

USTR set Section 301 tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on those economies from Friday, 24 July 2026, as Section 122 tariffs expired. Tunisia is absent from the final action, so no Section 301 surcharge applies to it.

The outlet Managers wrote on 29 July 2026 that Tunisian goods pay the regular tariff, with no percentage given. Before the Supreme Court tariff ruling, Tunisie Numérique wrote on 2 March 2026, duties on Tunisian goods were about 25%.

The US Army says the African Lion exercise opened on Monday, 13 April 2026 at El Aouina Air Base. Tunisia was hosting for the tenth straight year, with about 560 military personnel taking part there.

On Wednesday, 22 July 2026 Defence Minister Shili met General Dagvin Anderson, commander of US Africa Command, in Tunis. Shili asked for deeper defence technology transfer and strategic and intelligence cooperation, La Presse reported.

A Tunisian American Joint Military Commission was due to meet in the United States in early September 2026, Business News wrote. Whether it met, and what it agreed, was not confirmed.

On Thursday, 22 October 2026 Shili met Laura Gross of the US Defense Threat Reduction Agency in Tunis. They discussed border surveillance, counterterrorism and counter-drone systems, Business News reported.

China, Cheap Imports and Big Projects

China was the largest single source of Tunisian imports from January to September 2026, at 12.6% of the total. That is about 9.0 billion dinars (about US$3.0 billion), and imports from China rose 7.5%.

From January to April 2026 Tunisia’s deficit with China was about 3.77 billion dinars (about US$1.26 billion), roughly half the total deficit. Business News reported the INS figure on 12 May 2026.

Ambassador Wan Li said on 8 May 2026 that China cut duties to zero for 53 African countries on 1 May. For Tunisia, he called it a temporary two year measure.

He said China proposes an early harvest trade deal first and a wider partnership agreement later. Tunisia, he added, would keep the right to exclude sensitive Chinese products.

Wan Li said a Chinese company is building the Bizerte bridge, financed by the European Investment Bank and the African Development Bank. He also cited a planned cancer centre in Gabès and a Chinese built solar plant.

He added that China agreed in principle to finance the El Menzah Olympic stadium rebuild. Sinoma Cement planned a US$20 million investment in 2026, he said.

Saied visited China in 2024, the ambassador said, including the Huawei and BYD sites in Shenzhen. Huawei is involved in Tunisia’s 5G network, he added.

La Presse reported on 18 May 2026 that China is financing the Gabès cancer centre, with works due by end June. The estimated budget is 40 million dinars (about US$13.3 million), and no report of a groundbreaking was found.

La Presse reported on 8 October 2026 that Economy Minister Samir Abdelhafidh and Wan Li urged a joint investment working group. The sources checked give no signed value for the partnership talks, and the ambassador’s claims are his own.

Russia, Turkey and India

Foreign Minister Nafti and Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov exchanged messages on Saturday, 11 July 2026 for the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations. They cited cooperation in agriculture, the economy, science and culture.

Imports from Russia fell 54% from January to September 2026, INS says. The sources checked give no Russian loan, base or trade value.

Imports from Turkey rose 6.7% in the same nine months. Tunisia’s deficit with Turkey was about 1.08 billion dinars (about US$360 million) from January to April 2026.

India’s ambassador Devyani Uttam Khobragade spoke at the Republic Day event in Tunis on Monday, 26 January 2026. Industry Minister Fatma Thabet Chbiboub welcomed recent agreements to raise capital in STIP, the Tunisian Indian Phosphate and Fertilizer Company.

The capital increase is meant to raise phosphoric acid output and phosphate exports to India. Imports from India rose 3.2% from January to September 2026.

The Gulf, the Maghreb Neighbours and the UN

Tunisian exports to Saudi Arabia rose 52.1% from January to September 2026, and to Egypt 78.6%, INS says. Exports to Libya were flat, up 0.03%.

Sultan Al Murshid, head of the Saudi Fund for Development, met Economy Minister Samir Abdelhafidh in Riyadh in October 2025. The fund said it would study new Tunisian projects, and a joint commission was planned for late December 2025.

No Saudi, Qatari or Emirati loan, deposit or investment figure for 2026 was confirmed in the sources checked. Tunis took part in the BRICS summit in Johannesburg in August 2023, but no membership application was confirmed.

Nafti met Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune in Algiers on Wednesday, 8 July 2026. The two sides signed minutes and adopted a roadmap for the 24th Grand Joint Commission, to be held in Algeria.

Algeria supplied 7.1% of Tunisian imports, but Tunisian exports to Algeria fell 11%. Tunisia’s deficit with Algeria was about 1.57 billion dinars (about US$520 million) from January to April 2026.

Tunisia’s foreign minister visited Tripoli on 10 and 11 April 2026 and met Libyan Government of National Unity head Abdelhamid Dbeibah. Tunisia plans a Ras Jedir border corridor to Africa’s interior, with commissioning envisaged for 2029.

No source checked gave Tunisia’s vote on the Ukraine resolution of Monday, 24 February 2025, which passed 93 to 18. On Gaza, Webdo reported that Tunisia abstained on the truce text of Friday, 27 October 2023.

The same outlet wrote that Tunisia voted for the ceasefire resolution of Tuesday, 12 December 2023. It also wrote that Tunisia did not take part in the 12 September 2025 vote on a two state declaration.

Phosphates, Loans and the IMF Standoff

Phosphate and derivative exports fell 16.5% from January to September 2026, INS says. India is investing in a phosphate and fertiliser joint venture with Tunisia.

Olive oil exports rose to 4.01 billion dinars (about US$1.34 billion) from 2.92 billion (about US$0.97 billion). Energy imports rose 32%, and the energy deficit reached 10.5 billion dinars (about US$3.5 billion).

The IMF reached a staff level agreement with Tunisia on Saturday, 15 October 2022 for about US$1.9 billion over 48 months. Its release said the deal needed approval from the IMF Executive Board.

On Thursday, 6 April 2023 Saied said in Monastir that he refused “the diktats imposed from abroad”. No board approval was found in the sources checked, and the Rio Times report on the standoff covers the debt picture.

The central bank put net foreign currency assets on 22 October 2026 at 24.1 billion dinars (about US$8.0 billion). That equals 93 days of imports, and the figure is provisional; an earlier Rio Times report counted 92 days.

The IFC, the World Bank Group’s private sector arm, projects at least US$300 million of investment in Tunisia this year. Read the report on the IFC target for details.

What It Means for US Readers

US goods exports to Tunisia were US$589.6 million in 2025, and imports from Tunisia US$1.01 billion, Census data show. Tunisia supplied about 24.5% of US olive oil needs in 2024 to 2025, Tunisie Numérique wrote.

Investors can watch three signals: any IMF talks, a China trade deal and the US tariff position on Tunisian goods. Each could change costs for firms that source from or sell in Tunisia.

Visitors and expats can start with the Tunisia explained guide. The report on Tunisia holding its key rate at 7% covers prices.

What Is Not Known

USTR names no Tunisia rate since 24 July 2026, and the duty on each product line was not checked. Whether the Joint Military Commission met in September 2026 is unknown.

Tunisia’s vote on the Ukraine resolution of 24 February 2025 could not be confirmed, as UN records were not reachable. The Gaza votes of 2023 rest on Webdo, and the reason for Tunisia’s absence in September 2025 is not public.

Whether China and Tunisia have signed an early harvest or partnership deal is not known, nor whether the Gabès groundbreaking took place. The ambassador’s claims were not checked against Chinese or Tunisian government texts.

No new 2026 EU loan was confirmed, and how much of the 2023 package was paid out was not checked. No IMF board approval, Qatari or Emirati deal, Turkish loan or BRICS application was found.

Algeria’s gas supply to Tunisia and any Algerian deposit were not verified against primary data. Tunisia’s Gaza votes after 2023 were not checked.

No prediction market on Tunisian foreign policy was found on 23 October 2026, so none is shown. Polymarket lists only a closed 2024 election market and football matches.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who runs Tunisia in 2026?

President Kais Saied holds executive power after winning 90.69% of the vote on 6 October 2024. Sarra Zaafrani Zenzri heads the government.

Who is Tunisia’s biggest trading partner?

The European Union took 70.2% of Tunisian exports from January to September 2026. China was the largest single source of imports at 12.6%, ahead of Italy at 11.8%.

Does Tunisia have an IMF programme?

A staff level agreement for about US$1.9 billion was reached on 15 October 2022 and needed board approval. No board approval was found in the sources checked.

Does the United States have a base in Tunisia?

No US base was found in the sources checked. The US Army says the African Lion exercise opened at El Aouina Air Base on 13 April 2026.

Is Tunisia a member of BRICS?

No source checked shows Tunisia as a BRICS member or applicant. Tunis took part in the BRICS summit in Johannesburg in August 2023.

What does the European Union want from Tunisia?

The EU says it has mobilised over 600 million euros (about US$673 million) in grants since 2023. It says departures from Tunisia fell 80% in 2024, and energy links and trade are other priorities.

Sources: INS Tunisia (foreign trade, September 2026); US Census Bureau (trade with Tunisia); USTR (Section 301 investigations, March 2026); USTR (final action, 23 July 2026); Central Bank of Tunisia (indicators, 22 October 2026); European Commission (EU Tunisia partnership package, June 2023); European Commission (memorandum of understanding, 16 July 2023); EU External Action Service (Commissioner Suica in Tunis, October 2025); IMF (staff level agreement, 15 October 2022); Prime Minister’s office, Tunisia (October 2026); Assembly of the Representatives of the People (16 October 2026); USTR (press release, 23 July 2026); EY Tax News (Section 122 expiry, 24 July 2026); Managers (US duties and olive oil, 29 July 2026); US Army (African Lion 2026, 15 April 2026); UN press (General Assembly, 24 February 2025); La Presse (ISIE final results, 12 October 2024); La Presse (Chinese ambassador Wan Li, 8 May 2026); La Presse via AllAfrica (AFRICOM visit, July 2026); Business News (military commission, 24 July 2026); Business News (Shili and DTRA, 23 October 2026); La Presse (Gabès cancer centre, 18 May 2026); La Presse (Tunisia China working group, 8 October 2026); La Presse via AllAfrica (Nafti and Lavrov, 11 July 2026); Business News (Nafti in Algiers, 8 July 2026); Business News (trade deficits, 12 May 2026); La Presse via AllAfrica (Libya and Ras Jedir, 14 April 2026); L’Economiste Maghrebin (India, 27 January 2026); La Presse (Saudi Fund, 29 October 2025); Tunisie Numerique (US tariffs, 2 March 2026); Webdo (Gaza vote, 27 October 2023); Webdo (Gaza ceasefire vote, December 2023); Tunisie Numérique (Ukraine vote totals, February 2025); Kapitalis (BRICS summit, 23 August 2023); Webdo (UN declaration, September 2025); Kapitalis (Saied on the IMF, 6 April 2023); Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy (9 July 2026); open.er-api.com (exchange rates, 23 October 2026) (all accessed 22 and 23 October 2026).

World.title: Namibia Geopolitics Explained 2026
World.content:
NAMIBIA · GEOPOLITICS

Key Facts — What is happening President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, in office since 21 March 2025, is courting Washington, Beijing, Brussels, New Delhi and Abu Dhabi at once while keeping the non-alignment that Namibia’s constitution requires.

— Why it matters Namibia is a leading uranium producer, an emerging offshore oil province and the owner of a deep-water Atlantic port, so every major power wants a foothold, and its choices shape mineral and energy supply chains.

— The numbers In March 2026 China took 32.0% of Namibia’s exports and South Africa 23.4%, uranium was 26.7% of exports, and in May 2026 Namibia ran a US$133 million (NAD 2.2 billion) deficit with the United States.

— Who is who Nandi-Ndaitwah leads the ruling SWAPO party, Selma Ashipala-Musavyi is minister of international relations and trade, and US ambassador John Giordano is leading an American push on energy and critical minerals.

— What to watch Watch the 31 December 2026 end of the current US duty-free AGOA window, TotalEnergies’ delayed Venus oil investment decision, the reviewed Germany genocide declaration promised to parliament, and follow-up to nine China agreements.

— What it means for you US firms can bid for Namibian mining, energy and port work as Washington promotes American capital, but US duty-free access for Namibian farm, fish and manufactured exports lapses at year end unless Congress acts again.

Washington pitches capital, Beijing holds majority stakes in two uranium mines and Brussels funds hydrogen, while Windhoek stays non-aligned. Here is what each power wants in October 2026.

Namibia geopolitics in October 2026 is a balancing act between Washington, Beijing, Brussels and a growing list of other suitors. The southern African country sells uranium, gold, fish and diamonds, and hopes to add oil.

President Nandi-Ndaitwah visited China in July 2026, hosted India’s prime minister in July 2025 and addressed the UN in September 2025. This guide sets out what each outside power wants, from minerals and ports to votes at the United Nations.

More coverage sits on the Rio Times Namibia page. Conversions use NAD 16.50 per US$1, the open.er-api.com rate of 23 October 2026 (00:02 UTC).

Who Holds Power in Windhoek

SWAPO, the South West Africa People’s Organisation, has governed since independence in 1990. Its leader Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah won in November 2024 with about 58% and was sworn in on Friday, 21 March 2025.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

SWAPO holds 51 of the 96 elected seats in the National Assembly, down from 63 before the 2024 vote. The Independent Patriots for Change, a newer opposition party, holds 20 seats.

Selma Ashipala-Musavyi is minister of international relations and trade, and she co-chaired the 16 March 2026 talks with Russia. Elijah Ngurare was prime minister on 16 September 2026, when he hosted a solidarity dinner for Cuba.

Article 96 of the constitution commits the state to a policy of non-alignment, as a commentary in The Namibian notes. That principle helps explain why Windhoek takes meetings and money from rival powers at the same time.

Namibia Geopolitics at a Glance

The list below summarises each relationship using only what the sources checked can confirm. Details and dates follow in the sections after it.

United States: an AGOA duty-free trade window to 31 December 2026, a visa bond pilot, and an ambassador pitching energy and critical minerals.

an AGOA duty-free trade window to 31 December 2026, a visa bond pilot, and an ambassador pitching energy and critical minerals. China: the biggest single export market, majority stakes in two uranium mines, and nine agreements signed in July 2026.

the biggest single export market, majority stakes in two uranium mines, and nine agreements signed in July 2026. European Union and Germany: a green hydrogen and raw materials partnership, EUR 1.3 billion mobilised, and an unfinished genocide settlement with Berlin.

a green hydrogen and raw materials partnership, EUR 1.3 billion mobilised, and an unfinished genocide settlement with Berlin. Russia: an intergovernmental commission that met on 16 March 2026, with a draft customs agreement ready for signing and mining instruments outstanding.

an intergovernmental commission that met on 16 March 2026, with a draft customs agreement ready for signing and mining instruments outstanding. India: a state visit in July 2025, a digital payments licence, defence training and trade of US$568.4 million in 2024-25.

a state visit in July 2025, a digital payments licence, defence training and trade of US$568.4 million in 2024-25. UAE and Qatar: an Emirati offer to explore a trade pact, and Qatari energy interest, including QatarEnergy’s stake in the Venus oil project.

an Emirati offer to explore a trade pact, and Qatari energy interest, including QatarEnergy’s stake in the Venus oil project. Angola and South Africa: Namibia’s closest trade and energy neighbours, with an Angolan refinery stake offered to Namibia on 19 October 2026.

Namibia’s closest trade and energy neighbours, with an Angolan refinery stake offered to Namibia on 19 October 2026. Turkey and BRICS: no confirmed Turkish or BRICS agreement for Namibia in the sources checked.

The United States, Minerals and Trade

Ambassador John Giordano pitched the United States on Tuesday, 4 August 2026 as Namibia’s long-term mining and energy partner. He called Namibia the world’s third largest uranium producer and pointed to rare earths and the Orange Basin oil province.

Giordano warned against partners that rely on state backed finance and opaque contracts, calling such a partner a strategic liability. He named no country, so the target of that remark is a matter of inference.

On Wednesday, 21 October 2026 the embassy described his roadshow through Washington, New York, Philadelphia, Singapore, Johannesburg and Cape Town. In New York he joined the president at a US-Namibia Presidential Roundtable on investment, infrastructure and trade.

Trade currently favours American exporters. Namibia ran a May 2026 deficit of US$133 million (NAD 2.2 billion) with the United States, second only to South Africa.

The African Growth and Opportunity Act, or AGOA, is a US law that gives eligible African goods duty-free entry. President Trump signed its reauthorisation on 3 February 2026, running to 31 December 2026 and retroactive to 30 September 2025.

Namibia’s trade ministry says agriculture, fisheries and manufactured goods regain preferential access under it. The US House had passed a three-year extension to 2028 on 12 January 2026, but the signed law runs only to 2026.

Since 1 January 2026, US business and tourist visa applicants from Namibia can face bonds of US$5,000, US$10,000 or US$15,000. The US embassy says the bond is refundable and 38 countries are in the pilot.

Namibia is not among the 60 economies in the US Section 301 tariff notice of 23 July 2026. That notice replaced a global duty that expired on 24 July and sets no Namibian rate.

No primary source states the rate now paid on Namibian goods, so it remains unconfirmed. The Rio Times report on Namibia’s uranium exports covers the wider trade picture.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

China, the Biggest Customer

China took 32.0% of Namibia’s exports in March 2026, ahead of South Africa at 23.4%, the Namibia Statistics Agency reported. Uranium was 26.7% of exports that month, followed by gold at 16.1% and fish at 10.9%.

In May 2026 Namibia’s largest trade surplus was with China, at US$91 million (NAD 1.5 billion). China also supplied 12.9% of imports in March 2026, second to South Africa at 34.5%.

China’s biggest stake is in uranium. Swakop Uranium, which runs the Husab mine, is 90% owned by Taurus Minerals and 10% by Namibia’s state-owned Epangelo Mining.

Taurus is owned by China General Nuclear Power Group, a Chinese state company, and the China-Africa Development Fund. Husab shipped its first uranium oxide in December 2016, according to Swakop Uranium.

China National Uranium Corporation, part of China National Nuclear Corporation, bought Rio Tinto’s 68.62% of the Rössing mine in 2019. The Namibian Competition Commission approved that deal with conditions on local jobs.

Chinese Ambassador Zhao Weiping said in May 2026 that Husab, valued at about US$5 billion, is China’s largest single African investment. He added that China is open to helping Namibia if it decides to build a nuclear power plant.

President Nandi-Ndaitwah made a state visit to China from 6 to 11 July 2026 and met President Xi Jinping. The presidency listed nine agreements on Sunday, 12 July, including green minerals, vocational training and a table grape export protocol.

Other items covered an economic partnership framework, hospital pairing, a satellite ground station study and a smart city feasibility study. No monetary value was reported for any of them.

The Chinese ambassador said China has applied zero tariffs to all tariff lines for 53 African countries since 1 May 2026. He also said about 200 Namibian business people travelled with the president, the largest such delegation to date.

The European Union and Germany

The European Union signed a strategic partnership with Namibia on green hydrogen and raw materials in 2022, its Windhoek delegation says. In May 2026 EU Commissioner Roswall announced an extension of that partnership to 2030, the Republikein reported.

On 18 September 2025 the EU said it had mobilised EUR 1.3 billion (US$1.46 billion) in loans and grants for Namibia. This comes under Global Gateway, its overseas investment programme, which aims to unlock over EUR 20 billion (US$22 billion) of private money.

One result is Cleanergy Solutions Namibia, a green hydrogen plant at Walvis Bay run by Belgium’s CMB.Tech and Namibia’s Ohlthaver & List Group. A pilot green iron plant, HyIron, was inaugurated on 11 April 2025.

Germany carries a separate history: in 2021 it recognised the 1904 to 1908 killings of Ovaherero and Nama people as genocide. It offered EUR 1.1 billion (US$1.2 billion) over 30 years as development aid.

Lawmakers and descendants of the victims criticised that joint declaration, and in March 2025 the president said talks had to resume. On 8 April 2026 she said the reviewed text was within reach and headed soon for parliament, to conclude before year end.

The Rio Times regional guide explains how Windhoek frames these ties inside Southern Africa. The Rio Times report on Namibian oil and hydrogen sets out the oil and hydrogen bets that Brussels and Berlin are backing.

Russia, India and the Gulf

Russia and Namibia held the 11th session of their intergovernmental commission in Windhoek on Monday, 16 March 2026. Several draft agreements, including one on customs cooperation, were finalised and ready for signing, the trade minister said.

A geology working group met on 26 February 2026, and a fertiliser plant was discussed, with no agreement reported. The Soviet Union backed Namibia’s liberation struggle, which commentators cite when explaining the warmth of ties.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a state visit on 9 July 2025 and received Namibia’s highest civilian award. Namibia joined the Global Biofuels Alliance and became an observer at the International Big Cat Alliance.

India’s trade with Namibia was US$568.4 million in 2024-25, its foreign ministry says. An Indian Air Force team has trained Namibian helicopter pilots since 1996, and the Bank of Namibia licensed India’s UPI payments system.

On 17 February 2026 the UAE’s foreign trade minister said his country was ready to explore a free trade agreement. He also named an investment protection pact and a double taxation deal, and put non-oil trade at about US$260 million in 2025.

Namibia’s exports to the UAE include diamonds, scrap metal, frozen fish and grapes, according to the forum report. Qatar’s energy minister met the president on 20 November 2025 to discuss energy and environmental cooperation.

No Turkish or BRICS agreement for Namibia was confirmed in the sources checked as of 23 October 2026. BRICS is the bloc of emerging economies led by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

Neighbours, Oil and Walvis Bay

South Africa remains the closest economic partner, taking 23.4% of exports and supplying 34.5% of imports in March 2026. Africa accounted for almost half of Namibia’s total trade in May 2026, the Namibia Statistics Agency data show.

The main African export markets that month were South Africa, Zambia, Botswana, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zimbabwe. Petroleum oils were the largest import line in March 2026, at 16.3% of imports.

Venus, TotalEnergies’ 2022 discovery, is estimated at 700 million to 800 million barrels, and partners include Impact, NAMCOR and QatarEnergy. TotalEnergies said in August 2026 it is technically ready but awaits a fiscal agreement with the government.

Chief Executive Patrick Pouyanné hinted on 28 September 2026 that a decision could come in October. No decision had been announced in the sources checked as of 23 October 2026.

President João Lourenço of Angola said on Monday, 19 October 2026 he had invited Namibia to join the Lobito refinery’s shareholders. Lusa reported that the plant, under construction in Benguela province, is designed to process 200,000 barrels a day.

Walvis Bay draws almost every suitor, from Emirati investors pitched on its container terminal to European hydrogen backers. Read the Rio Times report on the Angolan refinery offer for the border and port picture.

Votes, Principles and Palestine

Namibia abstained on the 2 March 2022 UN General Assembly resolution on aggression against Ukraine, the UN voting record shows. The resolution passed with 141 votes for, 5 against and 35 abstentions.

A commentary in The Namibian cites non-alignment, trade with both East and West, and liberation-era Soviet support. Namibia’s votes since 2022 were not reviewed for this guide.

In her first UN General Assembly speech on 24 September 2025, the president urged action on Gaza and called it genocide. She said failure to act could become the moral failure that defines this era.

On 16 September 2026 she called for lifting the US economic blockade of Cuba at a solidarity dinner in Windhoek. She credited Cuban forces with helping bring about the UN plan, Resolution 435, that led to Namibian independence.

She added that Cuban doctors have served in Namibian hospitals for more than three decades. These stances sit beside Windhoek’s courtship of American capital, giving US policymakers an independent partner, not a bloc ally.

What It Means for US Readers

US companies can compete for Namibian mining, energy, port and hydrogen work, and the embassy is actively promoting American capital. Contracts and values from the October roadshow were not published, so treat it as promotion, not deals.

US importers of Namibian farm, fish and manufactured goods should note that AGOA duty-free access runs to 31 December 2026. Any further extension depends on Congress and was not confirmed in the sources checked.

Namibian travellers and business partners face US visa bonds of up to US$15,000 under a pilot that began on 1 January 2026. US firms hosting Namibian visitors should expect added cost and paperwork for them.

Nothing here is investment advice, and no company or share is recommended. Readers who follow uranium, oil or hydrogen should check company filings, which are the primary source for project decisions.

What Is Not Known

US tariff rate: Namibia is absent from the 23 July 2026 Section 301 notice, but the rate now paid is unconfirmed, and the 15% threat the trade minister cited in March was not shown to apply.

Namibia is absent from the 23 July 2026 Section 301 notice, but the rate now paid is unconfirmed, and the 15% threat the trade minister cited in March was not shown to apply. AGOA after 2026: whether Congress will extend the programme beyond 31 December 2026 is not confirmed.

whether Congress will extend the programme beyond 31 December 2026 is not confirmed. China deals: no values were published for the nine July 2026 agreements, and the terms of the green minerals agreement are not public.

no values were published for the nine July 2026 agreements, and the terms of the green minerals agreement are not public. EU partnership to 2030: the Republikein report was paywalled and the Commission text was read only second-hand, so amounts and legal steps are not confirmed.

the Republikein report was paywalled and the Commission text was read only second-hand, so amounts and legal steps are not confirmed. Germany: the text of the reviewed joint declaration and the date for tabling it in parliament are not public.

the text of the reviewed joint declaration and the date for tabling it in parliament are not public. Venus oil: no final investment decision by TotalEnergies had been announced in the sources checked as of 23 October 2026, and the fiscal terms are not public.

no final investment decision by TotalEnergies had been announced in the sources checked as of 23 October 2026, and the fiscal terms are not public. Angola refinery: the terms of the Lobito stake and Namibia’s answer were not available, and the offer rests on one Lusa report.

the terms of the Lobito stake and Namibia’s answer were not available, and the offer rests on one Lusa report. Turkey, BRICS, Taiwan: no 2026 agreement or status change was confirmed in the sources checked.

no 2026 agreement or status change was confirmed in the sources checked. UN votes: Namibia’s votes since March 2022 on Ukraine, Gaza and other resolutions were not reviewed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the president of Namibia in 2026?

Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah of SWAPO was sworn in on Friday, 21 March 2025. She is the country’s first woman president.

Is Namibia aligned with China or the United States?

Neither, formally, because Article 96 of the constitution commits Namibia to non-alignment. In 2026 it signed nine agreements with China and courted American investors at the same time.

What does China own in Namibia?

Chinese state-linked investors hold 90% of Swakop Uranium, which runs the Husab mine, with Epangelo Mining holding 10%. A Chinese state company also bought 68.62% of the Rössing uranium mine in 2019.

What does the United States want from Namibia?

Ambassador John Giordano pitched Washington on 4 August 2026 as a long-term partner in mining and energy. He cited uranium, rare earths and the Orange Basin oil province.

Is Namibia a member of BRICS?

No source checked shows Namibia as a BRICS member or partner country as of 23 October 2026. The status is listed as unconfirmed.

What is happening with Germany and the genocide talks?

On 8 April 2026 the president said a reviewed joint declaration was within reach and would soon go to parliament. She wants it concluded before the end of 2026.

What is AGOA and why does it matter to Namibia?

AGOA is a US law giving eligible African goods duty-free entry, including Namibian fish and manufactured goods. President Trump signed its reauthorisation through 31 December 2026 on 3 February 2026.

World.title: Who Runs Mozambique’s Economy, the Key Players in 2026
World.content:
MOZAMBIQUE · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening Mozambique’s economy grew 1.7% in the second quarter of 2026, the central bank held its policy rate at 9.25% on Wednesday, 30 September 2026, and a new IMF programme is still under negotiation.

— Why it matters Public debt stood at 91.4% of GDP at the end of 2025 and the aluminium smelter Mozal has been idle since 15 March 2026, so gas projects carry the hopes for growth.

— The numbers Inflation was 6.31% in September 2026, nominal GDP was about US$24.4 billion in 2025, gross reserves were US$4.24 billion at the end of 2025, and the Port of Maputo handled 32 million tonnes in 2025.

— Who is who President Daniel Chapo leads, Finance Minister Carla Louveira runs the budget and IMF talks, Felisberto Navalha became central bank governor on 2 September 2026, and TotalEnergies operates the Mozambique LNG project.

— What to watch Watch for a second IMF mission in November 2026, ExxonMobil’s investment decision on Rovuma LNG expected in 2026, and a firm bid or withdrawal on Kenmare by 17 November 2026.

— What it means for you US investors reach Mozambique mainly through ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies and the listed miner Kenmare, while US travellers and importers deal with a metical near MT 63.7 per US$1 as of 23 October 2026.

Gas, power, mines and a few banks decide Mozambique’s money, and the people who run them are changing. Here is who holds the levers in October 2026.

The Mozambique economy in October 2026 is run by President Daniel Chapo’s government, a new central bank governor and a few firms. Growth is weak, debt is high and the next boom depends on liquefied natural gas (LNG).

This guide names who controls the money, from TotalEnergies and ExxonMobil to Hidroelétrica de Cahora Bassa and the banks. Every figure carries its date.

More coverage sits on the Rio Times Mozambique page. The wider picture is in Mozambique explained and Mozambique geopolitics explained.

Conversions use MT 63.72 per US$1 and EUR 0.8915 per US$1, the open.er-api.com rates of 23 October 2026 (00:02 UTC). Amounts are rounded.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “South Africa prints 6.6M extra ballots, vote Nov 4” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

The Mozambique Economy in Numbers

Mozambique’s economy is small, indebted and dependent on a few exports. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) put nominal GDP at about US$24.4 billion for 2025.

The IMF estimates real growth of 0.5% in 2025 and projects 1.9% for 2026 if policies stay unchanged. The central bank, the Banco de Moçambique, reported 1.7% growth in the second quarter of 2026.

In the first quarter of 2026 output grew only 0.1% including LNG and 1.1% without it. The central bank published those figures after its meeting on Wednesday, 29 July 2026.

Annual inflation slowed to 6.31% in September 2026, the central bank said on Friday, 9 October 2026. The Rio Times covered the release in its inflation report.

The IMF classes public debt as unsustainable, at 91.4% of GDP at the end of 2025. It projects 94.6% for 2026, with external public debt at 61.2% of GDP in 2025.

Gross reserves were US$4.24 billion at the end of 2025, about 6.5 months of imports excluding megaproject goods, the IMF says. It projects a 2026 budget deficit of 6.3% of GDP against a government target of 0.3%.

No IMF programme is agreed, but Finance Minister Carla Louveira called a ten day mission an important step on 21 September. A second mission is due in November.

The Government and Central Bank at the Controls

Daniel Chapo took office as president in January 2025 and sets economic policy with the finance and economy ministries. Carla Louveira is finance minister, and Basílio Muhate heads the separate economy ministry.

Felisberto Navalha was sworn in as central bank governor on Wednesday, 2 September 2026. He replaced Rogério Zandamela, whose mandate ended on 31 August 2026.

The bank’s Monetary Policy Committee kept its MIMO policy rate at 9.25% on Wednesday, 30 September 2026. It cited climate shocks and Middle East and European tensions that could lift fuel and food prices.

It also said it will change the reserve requirement regime from the next maintenance period. A May 2026 rise in that ratio had already reduced liquidity in meticais, the bank said on 29 July.

Domestic public debt, excluding loans and overdue liabilities, was MT 538.3 billion (about US$8.4 billion) in June 2026. It rose MT 63.7 billion (about US$1.0 billion) from December 2025.

Commercial banks bought US$4.24 billion of foreign exchange in the first half of 2026. The fuel sector took 50% of the foreign exchange sold to the largest buyers.

The sovereign wealth fund, the Fundo Soberano de Moçambique, held US$117.5 million on 8 April 2026. The central bank invests it abroad while the government keeps overall responsibility.

Decree 56/2026 of 17 September approved the rules for a Development Bank of Mozambique, created by Law 17/2026. The central bank also extended its exceptional regime for converting export earnings by Notice 7/GBM/2026 of 1 October.

Gas: TotalEnergies, Eni and ExxonMobil

Gas is the biggest bet on the Mozambique economy. Three projects in the Rovuma Basin, off the northern coast, sit at different stages.

Mozambique LNG, in Area 1, is operated by TotalEnergies with 26.5%. Mitsui holds 20%, the state firm ENH 15%, PTTEP 8.5%, and ONGC Videsh, Beas Rovuma and BPRL Ventures 10% each.

TotalEnergies lifted its force majeure on 7 November 2025 and announced a full restart on Thursday, 29 January 2026. It targets first LNG in 2029, while the IMF assumes output from 2030; see the Rio Times report on the TotalEnergies restart.

The company says the project is 40% complete, with over 4,000 workers mobilised and more than 3,000 of them Mozambican. It expects contracts for Mozambican firms to exceed US$4 billion.

ExxonMobil’s Rovuma LNG, in Area 4, is planned as 18.6 million tonnes a year from 12 modular trains. No final investment decision has been taken, and startup is targeted for 2031.

Eni operates the Coral Sul floating LNG plant, in production since the fourth quarter of 2022. It took a final investment decision on a twin unit, Coral Norte, on Thursday, 2 October 2025.

Coral Norte is rated at 3.55 million tonnes a year, with first LNG due in the second quarter of 2028. Eni holds 50%, CNPC 20%, and KOGAS, ENH and XRG 10% each, the Journal of Petroleum Technology reported.

Natural gas was Mozambique’s top export in the first quarter of 2026, at US$467.4 million. Aluminium earned US$417.2 million and coal US$410.3 million, out of US$1.85 billion in total exports, Millennium bim reported from central bank data.

Estêvão Pale is minister of Mineral Resources and Energy and spoke at a minerals conference in Nacala on Monday, 19 October 2026. ENH, the state hydrocarbons company, is led by chairman Rudêncio Morais.

ENH is planning a gas project costing about US$250 million around Beira and Inhassoro, Reuters reported on 19 October 2026. It would link floating import terminals by a 140 km pipeline to the ROMPCO line to South Africa.

Sasol, the South African company that operates the Pande and Temane fields, said it was too early to speculate. Those fields are expected to run down within a few years.

Aluminium and Power: Mozal and Cahora Bassa

Mozal, the aluminium smelter near Maputo, went into care and maintenance on Sunday, 15 March 2026. South32 owns 63.7%, South Africa’s Industrial Development Corporation 32.4% and the Mozambican state 3.9%.

The smelter needs about 950 MW of constant power, supplied under an agreement that expired in March. South32 said it could not secure sufficient and affordable power beyond that month.

South32 booked US$117 million of extraordinary charges for the shutdown. Mozal directly and indirectly employed more than 4,000 people and made 355,000 tonnes of aluminium in the year to June 2025.

Hidroelétrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB) runs the Cahora Bassa dam on the Zambezi river. The state firm Companhia Elétrica do Zambeze holds 85%, Portugal’s REN 7.5% and Mozambican investors 4%.

HCB earned a net profit of €95.5 million (about US$107 million) on revenue of €293.2 million (about US$329 million) in 2025. Output fell 30% to 10,921 GWh in what it called one of the most severe droughts in decades.

The company paid about €255.7 million (about US$287 million) in taxes, fees and dividends to the state, Lusa reported. Shareholders approved the accounts on Thursday, 30 April 2026, and Tomás Matola chairs the board.

Coal, Mineral Sands and the New Mining Law

Coal remains a core export, though gas has overtaken it. In November 2025 the government forecast over 22 million tonnes for 2026, of which 9.3 million is coking coal.

Vulcan, an Indian company, owns the Moatize mines in Tete province, bought from Brazil’s Vale in April 2022 for over US$270 million. The Nacala Logistics Corridor railway went with them.

Kenmare Resources runs the Moma mine in northern Mozambique, which it says supplies about 6% of the world’s titanium feedstocks. Third quarter 2026 ilmenite output was 233,600 tonnes, up 12% from a year earlier.

Kenmare cut its 2026 ilmenite guidance to 710,000 to 750,000 tonnes, from about 800,000, citing commissioning problems at a new plant. Managing Director Tom Hickey leads the company.

Kenmare also received a non binding possible cash offer from International Resources Holdings (IRH). IRH must announce a firm bid or walk away by 5 pm GMT on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.

Parliament approved a revised mining law by consensus on Friday, 8 May 2026. The law firm King & Spalding says President Chapo signed it on 3 June, setting a non-dilutable state stake of at least 15%.

Local firms get priority for mining supplies and services, and 10% of mining revenue goes to a community fund. For the debate on the size of the state share, see the Rio Times report on a 20% state stake.

Banks, Telecoms and the Stock Exchange

Millennium bim is one of three systemically important banks, with BCI and Standard Bank, on the central bank’s 2026 list. BCP África owns 66.69% of it and the Mozambican state 17.12%.

Its 2025 net profit fell 93.92% to MT 201 million (about US$3.2 million), after impairments tied to sovereign debt. Total assets were MT 200.9 billion (about US$3.15 billion), and it served 2.28 million clients.

Net loans were MT 49.3 billion (about US$774 million) and client resources MT 160.9 billion (about US$2.5 billion). Moisés Jorge chairs the board and Rui Manuel Pereira Pedro leads the executive committee.

Moza Banco, Absa Bank Mozambique and the state Banco Nacional de Investimento won capital market awards for 2025. The Maputo stock exchange, the BVM, topped MT 200 billion (about US$3.1 billion) in value, Minister Louveira said on 25 March 2026.

Vodacom Moçambique, the local arm of South Africa’s Vodacom, had 11.6 million customers on 31 March 2026. Its billing was MT 20.36 billion (about US$320 million), down 1.5% in the year.

Ports, Rail and Export Markets

The Port of Maputo handled 32 million tonnes in 2025, up 3.4%, TimesLIVE reported on 13 January 2026. The operator, Maputo Port Development Company (MPDC), handled 15.2 million tonnes itself, a record.

Grindrod holds 24.7% of MPDC, whose chief executive is Osório Lucas. The port’s main concession has been extended to 2058, the report said.

Rail carried 11.7 million tonnes through the port, up 17%. The Nacala railway, sold with the Moatize mines to Vulcan, serves coal exports.

India bought 18.2% of Mozambican exports in the first quarter of 2025, mainly gas, coal and cashew nuts, Forbes África Lusófona reported. South Africa took 13.4%, South Korea 11.9%, and China bought gas, titanium minerals and heavy sands.

What It Means for US Readers

US exposure to the Mozambique economy runs through energy and mining. ExxonMobil is developing Rovuma LNG, and its investment decision is expected in 2026.

TotalEnergies’ Mozambique LNG and Eni’s Coral projects will sell into world LNG markets from 2028 and 2029 on company schedules. Delays would push back that supply.

Kenmare is the most direct listed play on Mozambican minerals, and its possible takeover has a firm deadline of 17 November 2026. Investors should read the company’s own announcements.

A US traveller or importer deals with meticais at about MT 63.7 per US$1 on 23 October 2026. A new IMF programme would show whether lenders think the debt is manageable.

What Is Not Known

The size and date of ExxonMobil’s investment decision on Rovuma LNG are not confirmed, and the sources read give no dollar cost. TotalEnergies’ January 2026 release also states no total cost for Mozambique LNG.

Whether Mozal restarts is unknown; BusinessDay reported in July that South32 seeks a buyer and the IDC weighs options. The size of any new IMF loan and its conditions are not public.

The official gazette text of the new mining law was not read. The 15% state stake rests on a law firm summary and Miningmx, and parliamentary materials suggest it may rise.

The owners and holdings of Mozambique’s private business families could not be confirmed from primary sources, so none are named. Details of the state power utility EDM and the rail and port company CFM were also not confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who runs the Mozambique economy?

President Daniel Chapo’s government, with Finance Minister Carla Louveira and central bank governor Felisberto Navalha, sets policy. Gas operators such as TotalEnergies, Eni and ExxonMobil, plus HCB, Kenmare and the banks, hold the main assets.

What is Mozambique’s main export?

Natural gas was the top export in the first quarter of 2026, at US$467.4 million. Aluminium followed at US$417.2 million, though Mozal closed on 15 March 2026.

What is the central bank’s interest rate?

The MIMO policy rate was 9.25% after the Monetary Policy Committee met on Wednesday, 30 September 2026. Annual inflation was 6.31% in September 2026.

Is Mozal still operating?

No, it is not operating. The aluminium smelter near Maputo moved to care and maintenance on 15 March 2026 after talks on power supply failed.

When will Mozambique LNG start?

TotalEnergies targets first LNG in 2029 and says the project was 40% complete in January 2026. The IMF assumes production from 2030.

Does Mozambique have an IMF programme?

No new programme was agreed as of October 2026. A second IMF mission is due in November 2026 to discuss conditions.

World.title: Cameroon Culture, the Key Figures to Know in 2026
World.content:
CAMEROON · CULTURE

Key Facts — What is happening Cameroon culture is carried abroad by saxophonist Manu Dibango, striker Samuel Eto’o, fighter Francis Ngannou and novelist Imbolo Mbue, while the Ecrans Noirs film festival prepares its first edition without its founder.

— Why it matters Cameroon had 29.9 million people in 2025, three UNESCO cultural listings from 2023 to 2025, and a diaspora that sells its music, books, film and sport far beyond Central Africa.

— The numbers The population was 29,879,337 in 2025, the culture ministry asked parliament for 10.4 billion CFA francs for 2026 (about US$17.8 million), and Cameroon has won five Africa Cup of Nations titles.

— Who is who Pierre Ismaël Bidoung Mkpatt is Minister of Arts and Culture, Samuel Eto’o heads the football federation FECAFOOT, and Bassek Ba Kobhio, who died on 12 May 2026, founded Ecrans Noirs.

— What to watch Ecrans Noirs holds its 30th edition in Yaoundé from 21 to 28 November 2026 with a tribute to its founder, and the Ngondo water rites close with the sacred canoe departure on the first Sunday of December, 6 December 2026.

— What it means for you US readers already meet Cameroon through NBA forward Pascal Siakam, UFC title winner Francis Ngannou, the PEN/Faulkner winning novel Behold the Dreamers and the 1972 hit Soul Makossa, all easy entry points.

From Manu Dibango’s Soul Makossa to Eto’o’s football federation, Cameroon exports talent. Here are the figures and festivals that define it in October 2026.

Cameroon culture reaches the world through a few famous voices, from saxophonist Manu Dibango to striker Samuel Eto’o. This guide names the key figures, works and festivals to know in October 2026.

Cameroon had 29,879,337 people in 2025, the World Bank says, and its culture speaks in French, English and many local languages. Its artists work at home, in Europe and in the United States.

More coverage sits on the Rio Times Cameroon page, with the Cameroon politics guide and the guide to Cameroon’s economy. Amounts in CFA francs use 584.82 per US$1, the open.er-api.com rate of 23 October 2026.

Cameroon Culture at a Glance

Cameroon culture is shaped by hundreds of communities, a French and English colonial legacy, and a state that funds the arts modestly. The Ministry of Arts and Culture presented a proposed 2026 budget of 10.4 billion CFA francs (about US$17.8 million) to parliament.

Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Minister Pierre Ismaël Bidoung Mkpatt told parliament’s finance committee the money would fund cultural infrastructure, creative industries and heritage listings. Cameroon Tribune, the state daily, reported the hearing on 1 December 2025.

UNESCO recognised three Cameroonian cultural listings in three years. The Nguon rituals of the Bamoun joined its intangible heritage list in 2023, then the Ngondo traditions of the Sawa in 2024.

The Diy-Gid-Biy landscape joined the World Heritage List in 2025, with 16 dry-stone structures probably built from the 12th to 17th centuries. The Mafa people still use the ruins for ritual and sacrifice, UNESCO says.

The list below is a quick map of the figures covered in this guide. Each one is dated and checked against an official, institutional or regional source.

Music: Manu Dibango, Richard Bona, Charlotte Dipanda.

Books: Mongo Beti, Calixthe Beyala, Léonora Miano, Imbolo Mbue.

Film: Bassek Ba Kobhio, Jean-Marie Teno, Jean-Pierre Bekolo.

Art: Pascale Marthine Tayou, Barthélémy Toguo, Marilyn Douala Manga Bell.

Sport: Roger Milla, Samuel Eto’o, Francis Ngannou, Pascal Siakam.

Heritage: the Ngondo rites, the Nguon rituals, the Bamoun kings, Diy-Gid-Biy.

Music, From Soul Makossa to Concert Halls

Manu Dibango, the Cameroonian saxophonist, released Soul Makossa in 1972, and New York DJs turned it into a world hit. He died of Covid-19 on 24 March 2020 in the Paris region, aged 86.

The track began as the B-side of a single built around a Cameroon football anthem for the Africa Cup of Nations. Makossa is the Cameroonian dance style behind the title.

Richard Bona was born on 28 October 1967 in Minta, in Haute-Sanaga, and began as an instrumentalist in Paris and New York. His album Tiki was nominated for a Grammy Award in 2005, Music In Africa records.

Bona won a Victoires du jazz award in 2004 and the Sacem Grand prix jazz in 2012. Both honours came from France, where many Cameroonian musicians first found large audiences.

Charlotte Dipanda, who draws on makossa and African soul, was due to sing at Brussels’s Cirque Royal on Saturday, 16 May 2026. The diaspora outlet Camer.be says no Cameroonian artist had been booked in that hall before.
