Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

Traditional dance is also part of community celebration, as in this performance in Kob, in the North-West. The dancers’ shirts read Mukonge Dance.

Foreign concert halls therefore matter as much as home stages for many Cameroonian artists. A sold-out room in Brussels or a Grammy nomination counts as proof of reach.

Writers Who Carried Cameroon Abroad

Alexandre Biyidi, who wrote as Mongo Beti, published Ville cruelle in 1954 and The Poor Christ of Bomba in 1956. The pen name means roughly child of the Beti, and he died in 2001, aged 69.

Calixthe Beyala, raised in Douala, took the Académie française’s Grand Prix du roman in 1996 for Les Honneurs perdus. The prize drew controversy because of plagiarism allegations against the book.

Léonora Miano, born in Douala in 1973, has lived in France since 1991. Her novel Contours du jour qui vient won the Prix Goncourt des lycéens in 2006.

Imbolo Mbue was born in Limbe and came to the United States to study, earning degrees at Rutgers and Columbia. Her debut novel Behold the Dreamers won the PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction, worth US$15,000, in 2017.

Mbue writes in English, which links Cameroon’s literature directly to US readers. Beyala and Miano write in French, and their prizes come from French institutions.

Together the four show the double pull of Cameroon’s literary life. Home audiences read in two languages, while the biggest awards and sales often come from Paris and New York.

Film, Television and the Ecrans Noirs Festival

Bassek Ba Kobhio, the filmmaker who founded the Ecrans Noirs festival in Yaoundé in 1997, died on 12 May 2026 at 69. His films include Sango Malo and Le Silence de la forêt (2003).

Ecrans Noirs held its 29th edition from 20 to 27 September 2025, with Brazil as guest of honour, focusing on Afro-descendant cinema. The theme was how to distribute African films on and beyond the continent.

The 30th edition runs from 21 to 28 November 2026 at Yaoundé’s conference centre, Cameroon Tribune says, honouring Ba Kobhio. It is the first edition without its founder.

Jean-Marie Teno directed the 1992 documentary Afrique, je te plumerai, which looks at Cameroon thirty years after independence. It links colonial writing to later corruption and protest against one-party rule.

Jean-Pierre Bekolo, born in Yaoundé in 1966, made the 1992 satire Quartier Mozart, which mixes sorcery and city life. It won prizes at festivals in Cannes, Locarno and Montreal.

Bekolo’s Aristotle’s Plot (1996) was Africa’s entry in a British Film Institute series for cinema’s centenary. His later features include Les Saignantes (2005) and Miraculous Weapons (2017).

The state broadcaster CRTV was created by a law of 17 December 1987, is government owned and broadcasts in French and English. On 27 April 2026 the culture minister promised a new method to secure dedicated state funding for the film sector.

Painters, Sculptors and Art Spaces

Pascale Marthine Tayou, born in 1966 in Nkongsamba, lives and works in Ghent and Yaoundé. He showed at Documenta 11 in Kassel in 2002 and at the Venice Biennale in 2005 and 2009.

His solo shows include the Serpentine Sackler Gallery in London in 2015 and the Bass Museum in Miami in 2017. His sculptures and installations often follow a single person moving through a global village.

Barthélémy Toguo, born in 1967, lives between Paris and Bandjoun in western Cameroon. There he founded Bandjoun Station, an art centre with residencies, a permanent collection, a library and coffee plantations.

Bandjoun lies about 3 kilometres from Bafoussam, roughly 300 kilometres from both Douala and Yaoundé. Its residencies last four to eight weeks and take three or four artists a year.

In Douala, doual’art is a contemporary art centre founded in 1991 and led by Princess Marilyn Douala Manga Bell. Its public art triennial, the Salon Urbain de Douala, began in 2007 and has presented more than 80 works and events.

Football, Boxing Rings and Basketball Courts

Cameroon has won the Africa Cup of Nations five times, in 1984, 1988, 2000, 2002 and 2017, the continental body says. At the 2025 tournament the Indomitable Lions lost 2-0 to Morocco in the quarter-final in Rabat on Friday, 9 January 2026.

Cameroon did not play at the 2026 World Cup. DR Congo won the African playoff semi-final 1-0 in November 2025 with a 90th-minute goal by captain Chancel Mbemba.

Roger Milla scored against Russia at the 1994 World Cup aged 42 years and 39 days. The Olympic Channel calls him the oldest goalscorer in men’s World Cup history.

Samuel Eto’o retired as a player in 2019 and won the FECAFOOT presidency on 11 December 2021 with 43 of 74 votes. He was re-elected on 29 November 2025 as the only approved candidate, despite a sports ministry order to suspend the vote.

The federation says Eto’o is Cameroon’s all-time leading scorer and the record scorer at the Africa Cup of Nations. His second term runs four years, so football politics will stay tied to his name until late 2029.

Francis Ngannou, born in Batié, won the UFC heavyweight title on 27 March 2021 at UFC 260 by knocking out Stipe Miocic. He defended it at UFC 270 on 22 January 2022 against Ciryl Gane.

Pascal Siakam won the 2019 NBA championship with the Toronto Raptors and played the 2025 NBA Finals for the Indiana Pacers. He is among the most visible Cameroonian athletes in US sport.

Festivals, Kings and Living Heritage

UNESCO inscribed the Ngondo water oracle traditions of the Sawa people in 2024. The festival runs each year from September to the first Sunday of December.

On that final Sunday a sacred canoe leaves the Wouri River bank, and a priest dives to bring back the oracles’ message. The message is read in a sacred hut and passed to district chiefs.

Cameroon Tribune says the next Ngondo is planned for 5 to 6 December 2026 in Douala, under the theme awakening. UNESCO’s first-Sunday rule puts the canoe departure on Sunday, 6 December, after a caravan with wrestling, a crafts fair and a pageant.

The Bamoun people of Foumban hold the Nguon rituals, also spelled Ngouon, every two years, with consultations in early December, UNESCO says. It inscribed them in 2023, but no organiser has confirmed the 2026 dates.

A museum of the Bamoun kings opened in Foumban in 2024, holding more than 10,000 objects from over 600 years of history. Exhibits include royal headdresses, manuscripts, masks and portraits of the 20 kings.

The second South West Cultural Festival opened in Buea on Friday, 27 February 2026, and ran to 1 March. Minister Bidoung Mkpatt launched it on behalf of Prime Minister Joseph Dion Ngute.

Media and the English-Speaking Regions

Cameroon Tribune is the state’s bilingual daily, and the state broadcaster CRTV runs ten regional radio stations. Both serve readers and listeners in French and English.

The North-West and South-West regions are English speaking, and the United Nations humanitarian office still records displacement and violence there. Its situation report for January to March 2026 lists more than 1,700 protection violations.

Cultural life in those regions, from schools to festivals, runs under that pressure. The Cameroon politics guide and the Cameroon geopolitics explainer explain the conflict and the politics behind it.

Cultural ties also run across borders into the Congo basin and the Gulf of Guinea. The Cameroon in Central Africa guide and the explainer on Cameroon’s role in Africa map those neighbours and trade routes.

What It Means for US Readers

US audiences already meet Cameroon through the NBA, the UFC and the bookshop. Siakam, Ngannou and Mbue’s PEN/Faulkner winning Behold the Dreamers are the most direct links.

Soul Makossa, released in 1972, remains the musical entry point, and Bona’s Grammy-nominated Tiki is a second. Streaming makes both easy to find from the United States.

Culture is a small line in the state budget, with a 2026 request of about US$17.8 million. Festivals such as Ecrans Noirs in Yaoundé and Ngondo on the Wouri River are the clearest dated entry points for visitors.

Check the US State Department’s current advisory for Cameroon before booking, because conflict affects parts of the country. Film buyers and curators should also note that Brazil was guest of honour at Ecrans Noirs in 2025.

What Is Not Known

The ministry’s 10.4 billion CFA francs (about US$17.8 million) was a proposal, and the final amount after parliament’s vote was not checked. Cameroon Tribune named Bidoung Mkpatt as culture minister on 22 October 2026.

The Ecrans Noirs website shows conflicting dates for the 30th edition, so the November dates rest on Cameroon Tribune and its header. Who will succeed Bassek Ba Kobhio as the festival’s general delegate was not found.

The full programme for Ngondo 2026 and the dates of the next Nguon rituals in Foumban were not confirmed. No official count of Cameroon’s languages or ethnic groups was found.

No verified data exists in the sources checked on the size of Cameroon’s music, film or publishing industries. No prediction market applies to this topic.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Cameroon known for culturally?

Cameroon is known for makossa music, writers such as Mongo Beti and Léonora Miano, football and festivals such as Ngondo. UNESCO listed Ngondo in 2024 and Diy-Gid-Biy in 2025.

Who are the most famous people from Cameroon?

Well known names include Manu Dibango, Samuel Eto’o, Roger Milla, Francis Ngannou, Pascal Siakam and Imbolo Mbue. Each is dated and sourced in this guide.

What is Soul Makossa?

Soul Makossa is a 1972 recording by Manu Dibango that became a world hit after New York DJs played it. Dibango died on 24 March 2020, aged 86.

Which Cameroonian traditions has UNESCO recognised?

UNESCO inscribed the Bamoun Nguon rituals in 2023, the Sawa Ngondo traditions in 2024 and the Diy-Gid-Biy landscape in 2025. All three are officially listed.

What is the Ecrans Noirs festival?

Ecrans Noirs is a film festival in Yaoundé founded in 1997 by Bassek Ba Kobhio, who died on 12 May 2026. Its 30th edition runs from 21 to 28 November 2026.

Did Cameroon qualify for the 2026 World Cup?

No. DR Congo beat Cameroon 1-0 in the African playoff semi-final in November 2025 with a 90th-minute goal. Cameroon has won the Africa Cup of Nations five times.

World.title: Bahamas Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026
World.content:
BAHAMAS · POLITICS

Key Facts — What is happening Prime Minister Philip Davis and his Progressive Liberal Party won a second term on Tuesday, 12 May 2026. They took 33 of 41 House of Assembly seats against eight for the opposition.

— Why it matters One party controls the Cabinet and the House of Assembly. Decisions on tax, security and ties with Washington therefore sit with a single government for up to five years.

— The numbers The House has 41 elected seats and the Senate has 16 appointed seats. The Cabinet has 29 members including the Prime Minister, as of October 2026.

— Who is who Dame Cynthia Pratt is Governor-General, Chester Cooper is Deputy Prime Minister, and Michael Pintard leads the opposition. Sir Ian Winder is Chief Justice, and Shanta Knowles is Police Commissioner.

— What to watch A parliamentary committee is still seeking documents on about US$700 million of borrowed money placed in the National Investment Fund. Freeport governance is open to six months of public consultation from 21 October 2026.

— What it means for you The Bahamian dollar is fixed at one to the US dollar. A 12.5% US tariff on Bahamian goods since 24 July 2026 tests ties with Washington.

Bahamas politics is a two-party Westminster system in which Prime Minister Philip Davis’s party holds 33 of 41 seats. This guide names who holds each office as of October 2026.

Bahamas politics is dominated by two parties, the governing Progressive Liberal Party (PLP) and the opposition Free National Movement (FNM). As of October 2026 the PLP holds 33 of 41 seats after its win on 12 May.

This guide names who holds each office, from the Governor-General to the head of the defence force, and how power is shared. It also lists what is not yet public.

Figures come from Bahamian government sources, the constitution and the State Department, with seat totals taken from local newspapers. The Bahamian dollar is fixed at one to the US dollar, which the open.er-api.com rate of 23 October 2026 confirms.

Daily news is in the Rio Times Bahamas section. Related guides cover Bahamas geopolitics and who runs the Bahamian economy.

This guide condensed into 3 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Free. We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

Bahamas Politics in Brief

The Bahamas is a parliamentary monarchy that became independent from the United Kingdom in 1973. King Charles III is head of state, and the Governor-General represents him.

Dame Cynthia Pratt has been Governor-General since September 2023, and she was still in office on 19 October 2026. The Prime Minister’s office says she was the first woman to serve as Deputy Prime Minister and as National Security Minister.

RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

The Governor-General dissolves Parliament on the Prime Minister’s advice under Article 66 of the constitution. The Prime Minister is the leader of the party that commands a majority in the House of Assembly.

Parliament has two chambers, and the elected House of Assembly has 41 seats after the 12 May 2026 election. Two seats, St. James and Bimini and the Berry Islands, are new since 2021.

The PLP won both new seats, Business View Caribbean said. The Senate, the upper chamber, is appointed rather than elected.

The appointed Senate has 16 members: nine on the Prime Minister’s advice and four on the Opposition Leader’s advice. The Prime Minister names the last three after consulting the Opposition Leader, to keep the Senate balanced like the House.

A Parliament lasts five years from its first sitting unless it is dissolved sooner. Regional press said Davis moved the 2026 vote up from October, citing the Atlantic hurricane season.

How the 12 May 2026 Election Was Won

Davis announced on Wednesday, 1 April 2026 that he would ask for Parliament to be dissolved on Wednesday, 8 April. The Office of the Prime Minister cited Article 66(2) of the constitution.

Voters went to the polls on Tuesday, 12 May 2026, and the PLP won 33 of 41 seats, local newspaper tallies show. The PLP won 32 seats in 2021, when the House had 39, Business View Caribbean said.

The FNM won eight seats, one more than in 2021, flipping Freetown and MICAL but losing St Barnabas. Its leader, Michael Pintard, kept his Marco City seat and called Davis to concede.

A Nassau Guardian analysis put the PLP at 71,245 votes, about 51%, and the FNM at 48,863 votes, about 35%. It put the Coalition of Independents (COI) at 17,095 votes, about 12%, with no seats.

Former prime minister Hubert Minnis lost Killarney, a seat he had held for about two decades, while running as an independent. The FNM’s deputy leader, Shanendon Cartwright, and its chairman, Duane Sands, also lost.

Davis’s remarks on being sworn in as Prime Minister are dated Thursday, 14 May 2026. The government’s Throne Speech, published on 20 May, said it was the first consecutive term for any administration since 1997.

The Government and the Cabinet

The Cabinet Office order of 21 May 2026 lists 29 members: Davis and 28 ministers. The Tribune headlined it one of the largest Cabinets in Bahamian history.

Chester Cooper is Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Science and Technology. Fred Mitchell is Foreign Minister, and Michael Halkitis is Finance Minister.

Glenys Hanna Martin is Minister of Tourism, and Dr Michael Darville runs Health and Wellness. Myles LaRoda is Minister of National Security and Leader of Government Business in the House.

Wayne Munroe, a King’s Counsel and senator, is Attorney General and Minister of Legal Affairs. Senator Jerome Fitzgerald is Minister of Economic Affairs, and Senator Barbara Cartwright runs Social Services.

Clay Sweeting oversees Works and Family Island Affairs, and Ginger Moxey is Minister for Grand Bahama. Jobeth Coleby-Davis holds Energy, Utilities and Aviation, and Mario Bowleg holds Youth and Sports.

Wayne Munroe moved from National Security to Attorney General, and Michael Halkitis was sworn in as Finance Minister, the Tribune said. Myles LaRoda now holds National Security, the post Munroe left.

The Throne Speech set the agenda, led by compulsory pre-primary school from age four and a National Digital ID. It also promised an Employment Bill 2026, an E-Verify portal for employers and a Backlog Reduction Court.

Agencies are to move onto the MyGateway portal within three years, and the Real Property Tax is to be reviewed. An Artificial Intelligence Governance Act and a National Cybersecurity Authority are also promised.

On 21 October 2026 Davis announced plans for one governance framework for all of Grand Bahama. He opened six months of public consultation on Freeport governance.

The Opposition and Parliament

The FNM is the main opposition party and governed until the 2021 election. Pintard leads it and, as Leader of the Opposition, was due to be sworn in on Monday, 18 May 2026.

On Wednesday, 13 May 2026 the FNM caucus, executive and Central Council unanimously endorsed Pintard to stay on, a Bahamian daily said. Former Deputy Prime Minister Desmond Bannister said on 14 May that he should resign.

The FNM Central Council deferred its convention to no later than October 2027, a local daily said. Pintard still led the party and the opposition in October 2026.

The COI is a newer force that won no seats but doubled its vote, from 8,388 in 2021 to 17,095 in 2026. The same analysis put turnout in the 60 percent range.

Patricia Deveaux is Speaker of the House of Assembly. Pintard said on 23 June 2026 he had asked twice for Public Accounts Committee hearings to be televised, without reply.

The committee is examining 700 million Bahamian dollars (about US$700 million) of borrowing the government says went into the National Investment Fund. Finance Minister Halkitis said on 29 May 2026 that the government acted lawfully.

Pintard has said he sees no evidence that the full US$700 million reached the fund, and he wants the transaction documents. The Tribune reported on 14 October 2026 that the committee still awaited Finance Ministry documents and had made no final findings.

Rio Times explainers on the National Investment Fund and the probe next steps give more background. Both are Rio Times pieces, so they are context, not sources for the figures.

Security Forces, Courts and Watchdogs

The Royal Bahamas Defence Force is the country’s military, and its stated mission is to defend the sovereignty of the Bahamas. Commodore Floyd Moxey commands it, and he was named in late April 2025 to succeed Commodore Raymond King.

The Royal Bahamas Police Force is led by Commissioner Shanta Knowles, appointed on 3 January 2025, its website says. No report of a successor was found, and no October 2026 statement from her was confirmed.

Myles LaRoda oversees both forces as Minister of National Security. Wayne Munroe held that job in 2025, the Tribune said.

The US Coast Guard helps Bahamian authorities with coastal defence through Operation OPBAT, a joint counter-drug effort. The US Navy operates an underwater research facility on Andros Island, the State Department says.

In late September 2026 Bahamas Ambassador to the US Wendall Jones accused DEA agents of operating without government consent. Attorney General Munroe echoed the complaint, the Caribbean National Weekly reported on 1 October 2026.

US Ambassador Herschel Walker dismissed the claim of illegal operations as “fake news”. Davis told reporters the issue is process, adding “it’s not about targeting criminals at all”.

Sir Ian Winder is Chief Justice, and he gave the opening of the legal year speech in January 2026. The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London remains the final court of appeal, the State Department says.

The Court Services Act, in force since July 2024, gave the judiciary more administrative and financial independence. The legal system follows English common law, the State Department’s 2026 investment report says.

The same report says watchdogs are still taking shape. The Independent Commission of Investigations bill passed in 2025 is not expected to be operational for several years.

The Freedom of Information Act of 2017 is only partly in force, and the Public Disclosure Commission has not published asset declarations. An Integrity Commission, campaign finance reform and a working Ombudsman are pending.

The report adds that the Bahamas has no history of politically motivated violence. It says minor incidents, such as damaged billboards, can occur before general elections.

What It Means for US Readers

Tourism and financial services make up about 85% of the Bahamian economy, the State Department says. More than 12.5 million visitors came in 2025.

A large single-party majority points to steady policy on visitors, taxes and investment through the term. Voters can still change that at the next election, due by about 2031.

A 12.5% US tariff on Bahamian goods took effect on Friday, 24 July 2026, up from 10%, the Tribune reported. It follows a Section 301 finding, and Nassau has sought an exemption for crawfish and stone crab exports.

US trade with the Bahamas is worth about US$7.3 billion a year, with a US$3.8 billion US surplus, the State Department says. The Bahamian dollar is fixed at one to the US dollar, so prices carry no exchange risk.

Davis said Nassau wants US officials to notify it about operations in the country. Drug enforcement on Bahamian soil still depends on Bahamian consent and law.

Travellers should check the State Department’s current advisory for the Bahamas before booking. Business visitors can follow the Public Accounts Committee inquiry into the National Investment Fund.

What Is Not Known

Official seat and vote totals were not found on a government site, so the seat counts rely on local newspaper tallies. Turnout and the number of registered voters were not confirmed.

Cabinet portfolios follow the 18 May 2026 announcement and the 21 May order of precedence. A 3 June 2026 gazette notice on the allocation of portfolios was not read, so some ministry names may have changed.

The result of the FNM’s post-election review and the future of Pintard as leader were not found. The party convention is due only by October 2027.

Whether the National Investment Fund transfer broke any rule is unknown, because the committee has made no final findings. The government says it acted lawfully.

The outcome of the drug-agent dispute is unknown. No report of a settlement was found, nor of any US reply beyond Ambassador Walker’s remarks.

The full list of senators, the Senate President and any October 2026 public statement by Commissioner Knowles were not verified. The next general election date is not set, and it is due by about 2031 unless Davis calls it earlier.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the prime minister of the Bahamas in 2026?

Philip Davis, leader of the Progressive Liberal Party, is Prime Minister. He won a second term in the election of 12 May 2026.

Who is the head of state of the Bahamas?

King Charles III is head of state. Dame Cynthia Pratt is his representative as Governor-General.

What are the main political parties in the Bahamas?

The Progressive Liberal Party governs with 33 of 41 seats. The Free National Movement is the opposition with eight, and the Coalition of Independents won no seats.

How is the Bahamian Parliament organised?

The House of Assembly has 41 elected members, and the Senate has 16 appointed members. The Prime Minister, the Opposition Leader and the Governor-General share the Senate appointments.

When is the next Bahamas general election?

A Parliament lasts five years from its first sitting, so the vote is due around 2031. The Prime Minister can ask for an earlier dissolution.

Who controls the police and military in the Bahamas?

Minister of National Security Myles LaRoda oversees both. Commissioner Shanta Knowles leads the police, and Commodore Floyd Moxey leads the defence force.
