World.title: Power Failure Disrupts Costa Rica’s Juan Santamaría Airport Control Tower
World.content:
A power failure temporarily knocked out critical air traffic control systems at Costa Rica’s Juan Santamaría International Airport today, raising new concerns about the reliability of equipment at the busiest airport. The electrical problem affected the control tower for nearly an hour, reportedly leaving air traffic controllers without their usual radar screens, communication systems, weather information and radio equipment. During the outage, personnel were left relying on a portable backup radio to communicate with aircraft.

The failure prompted a temporary interruption in airport operations while technicians worked to restore the equipment. However, Costa Rican authorities said the situation was resolved quickly and maintained that scheduled flights were not affected. Public Works and Transport Minister Efraím Zeledón confirmed the electrical failure and said officials initially feared the disruption could last considerably longer. Technical crews were able to restore the affected systems before that became necessary.

Costa Rica’s Civil Aviation Authority also confirmed that normal operations had resumed, including both arrivals and departures. Aeris, the company that operates Juan Santamaría International Airport, said the control tower’s systems were fully restored. Nevertheless, the company advised travelers to contact their airlines directly to confirm their flight status.

The incident raises questions about the reliability of the airport’s electrical infrastructure and whether adequate backup systems are available when critical equipment fails. Air traffic controllers depend on radar, radio communications and weather information to safely coordinate aircraft approaching, landing and departing. When those systems become unavailable, airport authorities may need to restrict operations until normal service can be restored.

Today’s incident is not the first time technical problems have disrupted Costa Rica’s main international airport. On September 12, a truck damaged fiber-optic cables near the airport, temporarily interrupting radar communications, flight-processing systems and airline check-in services. The incident forced some airlines to process passengers manually and resulted in lengthy lines and flight delays.

An even more serious electrical failure occurred last September, when problems with the radar system forced Costa Rica to close its airspace for nearly seven hours. The disruption affected operations at both Juan Santamaría and Guanacaste Airport in Liberia, delaying, diverting or canceling numerous flights.

Following that incident, authorities announced plans to improve the electrical infrastructure supporting the airport’s radar equipment. The latest failure comes as Costa Rica continues to face questions about the reliability of its aviation infrastructure, including technical problems and shortages of air traffic controllers.

Although toay’s outage was relatively brief, it highlighted how quickly a technical failure can affect the systems responsible for managing commercial air traffic. Authorities have not publicly established the precise cause of the latest electrical problem or explained whether it was related to previous infrastructure failures.

For travelers, airport operations have returned to normal. Passengers departing from or arriving at Juan Santamaría are encouraged to check directly with their airlines for the latest flight information.

World.title: National Institute of Culture and History donates $60,000 to National Garifuna Council
World.content:
National Institute of Culture and History donates $60,000 to National Garifuna Council

By Zoila Palma: Today, the National Institute of Culture and History (NICH), through the National Celebrations Commission presented a donation valued at BZD $60,000 to the National Garifuna Council.

Albert Vaughan, President of NICH, presented the donation to Alex Nolberto, President of the National Garifuna Council, ahead of Garifuna Settlement Day 2026.

NICH says that it remains committed to supporting Belize’s cultural councils and strengthening the institutions that safeguard, promote and celebrate our rich cultural heritage.

World.title: Ministry of Health, PAHO strengthen Tobacco and Alcohol prevention efforts in Belize
World.content:
Ministry of Health, PAHO strengthen Tobacco and Alcohol prevention efforts in Belize

By Zoila Palma: The Ministry of Health and Wellness, in partnership with the Pan American Health Organization/World Health Organization (PAHO/WHO) and with support from the Australian Government, is strengthening tobacco and alcohol prevention efforts across Belize through youth-focused and community-based initiatives.

Last week, the programme reached the Stann Creek and Toledo districts with activities aimed at raising awareness and promoting healthier lifestyles.

In Dangriga, the initiative hosted the Stann Creek Youth Tobacco and Alcohol Forum, bringing together young people and stakeholders to discuss the risks and consequences of tobacco and alcohol use.

The forum encouraged participants to become advocates for healthier choices among their peers. A community sensitization session followed, engaging residents and stakeholders on prevention, awareness and the importance of creating supportive environments that promote healthier living.

In Punta Gorda, the Toledo Youth Tobacco Forum provided young people with an opportunity to share their perspectives, expand their knowledge and discuss practical ways to prevent tobacco and nicotine use among their peers. The activities form part of a broader joint prevention initiative designed to empower young people, strengthen community participation and promote evidence-informed strategies to address tobacco and alcohol use.

The Ministry expressed appreciation to staff of the National Drug Abuse Control Council (NDACC) and the respective district teams for their work in coordinating and implementing the forums and community activities.

World.title: Belize participates in Central America Travel Market 2026 in Guatemala
World.content:
Belize participates in Central America Travel Market 2026 in Guatemala

By Zoila Palma: Belize participated in the Central America Travel Market (CATM) 2026, held from October 19 to 21 in Guatemala City, Guatemala, with a delegation of 20 Belizean hoteliers and tour operators.

The participation provided an opportunity to promote Belize’s tourism offerings and strengthen relationships with regional and international travel industry partners.

CATM is a major tourism trade marketplace in Central America, bringing together tourism businesses, international buyers, tour operators and travel media. The event aims to strengthen commercial partnerships, showcase the region’s diverse tourism experiences and create new business opportunities in international markets.

During the event, the Belize Tourism Board (BTB) held a productive meeting with Ventur, a travel trade partner with whom it has previously collaborated on cooperative marketing initiatives.

The BTB also met with TAG Airlines at its offices in Guatemala City to explore further collaboration and strengthen regional tourism connectivity, potentially creating additional opportunities for travellers visiting Belize and other Central American destinations.

Belize’s participation concluded with “Unwind with Belize,” a rooftop reception celebrating the country’s vibrant culture and renowned hospitality.

Guests experienced Belizean-inspired cuisine, lively local music and colourful carnival performances, offering a taste of the country’s unique cultural identity.

World.title: International News: NASA says current El Niño could rival 1997-98 event, raising concerns over Global weather impacts
World.content:
International News: NASA says current El Niño could rival 1997-98 event, raising concerns over Global weather impacts

By Zoila Palma: NASA scientists say the El Niño developing in 2026 could become even stronger than the powerful 1997-98 event, raising concerns about potential impacts on weather patterns around the world.

According to NASA, satellite observations show similarities between the current event and previous major El Niño episodes, which contributed to droughts, wildfires, crop failures, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding in various regions.

El Niño is a natural climate pattern that occurs approximately every two to seven years, bringing warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures to parts of the equatorial Pacific. The phenomenon develops when trade winds weaken, allowing warm water normally concentrated in the western Pacific to move eastward. This shift further weakens the winds and increases ocean temperatures, creating a feedback loop between the atmosphere and the ocean. However, each El Niño develops differently, meaning its effects vary by region and from one event to another.

NASA is using satellite measurements of sea surface height to compare the current El Niño with previous events.

Data collected in October 2026 show elevated sea levels and warm water extending across the eastern Pacific toward the coast of South America, a pattern resembling the 1997-98 event.

World.title: PUP mourns passing of banana trailblazer Tony Zabaneh
World.content:
PUP mourns passing of banana trailblazer Tony Zabaneh

By Zoila Palma: The People’s United Party (PUP) has expressed condolences on the passing of Former Chairman Extraordinaire and businessman Antonio “Tony” Zabaneh of Independence Village, Stann Creek District.

“Tony has transitioned: we bid farewell to a true Belizean patriot.

Tony served as the Chairman of Independence Village for many years, his last term ending in 2016. He was instrumental in the establishment of the Big Creek Port whose primary focus was the exportation of bananas. It has since become a major port for the export and importation market, namely sugar and fuel products. Tony established the Banana Growers Association where he served as the sole Chairperson from its inception in 1971. Under his Chairmanship, in 1972, the Association launched a rehabilitation plan to restore banana farms and export bananas to the United Kingdom. Tony led the Association until the time of his death,” the PUP said.

The PUP says that Zabaneh’s involvement in the Independence Community and the impact he made will live on for generations to come.

“He was an ardent sports enthusiast. A softball coach of the well-known Sagitun girls., football with the Sagitun boys and a boxing fanatic. Tony loved and focused on developing talent in the south. Many a youth made it to national stardom under his tutelage and direction,” the PUP added.

The PUP says Zabaneh was a true trailblazer.

“There was very little business enterprise into which Tony did not venture. Belize has lost a great Belizean and this country and particularly the South is better because he was here. He left Belize far better than he found it,” the party said.

May his soul rest in peace and rise in eternal glory.

World.title: International News: France prepares to deploy 70,000 police ahead of new protests
World.content:
International News: France prepares to deploy 70,000 police ahead of new protests

By Zoila Palma: France will deploy approximately 70,000 police and security personnel nationwide on Saturday as authorities prepare for another round of demonstrations following some of the country’s worst urban violence in years.

Today, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced the security measures warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media.

President Emmanuel Macron convened a meeting of his defence council with senior ministers and officials to address the crisis, AFP reports.

He was also scheduled to meet with high school student representatives whose initial protests over school conditions have expanded into a nationwide movement expressing anger over the rising cost of living. Students are demanding improvements to school infrastructure and reforms to the Parcoursup university admissions system.

The government has sought to distinguish peaceful demonstrations from the looting, arson and destruction that accompanied protests last weekend.

World.title: Belize Marketing and Development Corporation participates in 11th Binational Belize–Mexico Seminar
World.content:
Belize Marketing and Development Corporation participates in 11th Binational Belize–Mexico Seminar

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Marketing and Development Corporation (BMDC) participated in the 11th Binational Belize–Mexico Seminar, taking place October 21–23 at the University of Belize Central Campus in Belmopan.

Under the theme “Innovation: Advancing Knowledge, Innovation, and Community Partnerships for Binational Development in Belize and Mexico,” the event highlights the importance of collaboration, knowledge sharing, and innovative approaches to sustainable development.

BMDC says that it remains committed to promoting Belizean agricultural products, supporting local farmers and producers, and strengthening partnerships that contribute to economic growth and community development.

World.title: Ministry of Agriculture engages farmers in Cayo for training on thrips management in sweet pepper production
World.content:
Ministry of Agriculture engages farmers in Cayo for training on thrips management in sweet pepper production

By Zoila Palma: Ten farmers participated in the fifth training session on thrips management in sweet pepper production, conducted by the Ministry of Agriculture’s Cayo District Agriculture Department in Springfield, Cayo, on Thursday, October 22.

The training was led by Extension Officer Moises Perez and focused on biological control alternatives for thrips and other agricultural pests. As part of the session, green lacewing insects (Chrysoperla carnea) were released to help control thrips populations affecting sweet pepper crops.

Despite ongoing management efforts, thrips infestations continue to threaten crop development and production.

The Ministry noted that the pest can cause significant damage to flowers and fruits, potentially resulting in crop losses of up to 100%.

Farmers were also reminded that no single control method, whether chemical, biological or mechanical, can completely eradicate thrips because of their life cycle and ability to develop resistance to chemical treatments.

The training sessions form part of collaborative efforts involving the Ministry of Agriculture, the Climate Resilient Agriculture Project (CRESAP) and the Regional International Organization for Plant Protection and Animal Health (OIRSA).

World.title: Inclement weather forces postponement of schoolboy football games
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Several ISSA Manning Cup and daCosta Cup schoolboy football matches scheduled for Friday have been postponed because of prevailing weather conditions.

The postponements affect matches in Portland, St Thomas, Kingston and St Andrew, St Catherine and Clarendon, as organisers continue to monitor the weather situation across the island.

The decision means a halt to schoolboy football action in the affected parishes, with further updates expected as the day progresses.

Organisers are continuing to assess conditions in the other parishes to determine whether the scheduled matches can proceed.

Players, coaches, officials and supporters have been urged to prioritise their safety and avoid unnecessary risks amid the unfavourable weather.

“Please stay safe and do not take any chances that may prove unsafe,” the advisory stated.

No details have been provided regarding new dates for the postponed matches. Further announcements are expected as the weather situation develops.

— Howard Walker

World.title: Gov’t halts overseas travel for public officials until March 2027
World.content:
Jamaican passport

KINGSTON, Jamaica — The Government has imposed an immediate moratorium on official overseas travel across the public sector until March 31, 2027, as it moves to contain expenditure and redirect resources towards national recovery and reconstruction following the devastation caused by Hurricane Melissa.

The directive, outlined in a government memorandum, applies to Cabinet ministers, ministers of state, permanent secretaries, senior public officers, heads of government agencies, board members, chief executive officers and other public sector employees.

The restriction will remain in effect for the remainder of the 2026/2027 financial year, subject to limited exceptions.

According to the memorandum, the unprecedented destruction caused by Hurricane Melissa has placed significant pressure on Jamaica’s fiscal resources and public sector capacity, prompting the Government to prioritise expenditure and mobilise resources for reconstruction.

“At this critical juncture, it is imperative that the Government exercises the highest degree of fiscal discipline, prioritises expenditure and ensures that the attention and efforts of ministers and senior public officials remain firmly focused on national reconstruction, economic recovery and the effective delivery of public services,” the memorandum stated.

The travel ban extends to all ministries, departments and agencies, statutory bodies, executive agencies, public enterprises and other public sector entities.

It said the restriction applies regardless of whether the proposed travel is funded by taxpayers, the budget of a public body or an external organisation or sponsoring institution.

The Government has also directed that all previously approved overseas trips that have not yet taken place be reviewed to determine whether they comply with the new restrictions. The specific circumstances under which overseas travel may be exempted were not detailed.

The memorandum also makes clear that prior approval does not automatically exempt officials from the moratorium.

“The Government must lead by example in demonstrating prudence, restraint and an unwavering commitment to directing scarce public resources towards the country’s most urgent priorities,” the memorandum added.

World.title: Blood blunder
World.content:
A woman mistakenly transfused with blood intended for another patient with the same first and last names at University Hospital of the West Indies (UHWI) in March 2006 has won nearly twice the $4 million in general damages awarded by the Supreme Court after successfully challenging the decision in the Appeal Court.

According to the Appeal Court, instead of the $4 million awarded by the Supreme Court judge, the woman should have been awarded the sum of $7,600,000 for “pain and suffering and loss of amenities”. The judges of the appeal, after hearing arguments from attorney Denise SeniorSmith, who represented the woman, said: “The complaint that the measure of damages was either inordinately low or grossly inadequate is irresistible.”

“In short, in the judgment of this court, the award made to the appellant by the learned judge was an entirely erroneous estimate of the damages to which the appellant was entitled,” the Appeal Court stated.

According to the facts contained in the record of the court, the woman was admitted to UHWI on March 4, 2006 as an emergency admission with severe thrombocytopaenia (a medical condition defined by an abnormally low blood platelet count). She was subsequently diagnosed with immune thrombocytopaenia (ITP) — a bleeding disorder caused by low blood platelets — and was required to undergo a blood transfusion as part of UHWI’s management of the condition.

That transfusion was conducted the following day (March 5, 2006) by the UHWI’s nursing staff. According to the evidence before the court, the transfusion “resulted in a mismatch with the appellant’s blood group as she was given blood intended for another patient with the identical first and last names”.

According to the evidence, the night after being transfused with the incorrect blood group, the woman experienced what she described as “intolerable pain throughout her body, high temperature and depersonalisation (a psychiatric state where the patient does not believe he/she is real). That pain and suffering, the court was told, “continued for several days, accompanied by sleepless nights”.

Two days after the transfusion, the haematology service became aware of the nursing staff’s error. The woman was informed of the transfusion blunder during a meeting with the medical team the next day (March 8).

She was discharged as an inpatient on April 10, 2006, but remained an outpatient of the hospital and filed a claim form and particulars of claim in August 2011 seeking damages against the hospital for the negligent transfusion of the incorrect blood group by its nursing staff.

In the claim she alleged that she suffered “excruciating pain, reduction of her platelet count, and trauma, amongst other injuries”, because of that negligence.

In December 2016 the Supreme Court made an award of $3,500,000 for psychological injury along with an additional sum of $500,000 to account for the further pain and suffering that the woman experienced as a consequence of the transfusion, making the total award for general damages $4,000,000.

However, the woman disputed that decision in January 2017 appeal, contending, among other things, that the judge had erred in determining the amount of the award which was “inordinately low/or grossly inadequate” and far less than the sums submitted by her attorney.

The Appeal Court, in reviewing the case, said the overarching issue was whether the sum awarded was an entirely erroneous estimate of the damages to which she was entitled as a result of the learned judge’s failure to apply comparable cases, or otherwise act on correct principles of law.

Following an assessment of arguments from Senior-Smith, attorneys representing the hospital, and various case law, the Appeal Court, in its ruling handed down on October 16, said: “A fair and reasonable quantum of damages for the psychological injury the appellant suffered should be $7,100,000, rounded up.”

“The appellant should have been awarded the sum of $7,600,000 for pain and suffering and loss of amenities. That is just shy of twice the sum the learned judge awarded ($4,000,000),” the Appeal Court stated.

In reference to the $10-million in damages sought by Senior-Smith on the basis of a comparative case, the Appeal Court, however, maintained that the two matters were “distinguishable”, while adding that, “In the assessment of damages, the object is never to provide the injured party with a windfall, but with that sum of money which will restore that party to the position she would have been in had she not suffered the wrong that gave rise to the claim”.

The court apologised for the delay in delivering the judgment and said, “The appeal is allowed. The order for general damages is set aside. Substituted therefor is the following: general damages awarded to the appellant in the sum of $7,600,000 with interest at the rate of three per cent from August 31, 2011 to December 7, 2016.”

It further affirmed the original orders of the Supreme Court for special damages and for future medical expenses.

World.title: Six charged in alleged $110-million loan fraud
World.content:
CHUNG... the activity alleged in this matter, although sophisticated, expansive and creative, was no match for the skills of our forensic investigators

THE Financial Investigations Division (FID) is reporting that six people have been arrested and charged following a joint investigation with the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) into an alleged fraudulent loan scheme totalling approximately $110 million.

According to the FID, the loans were obtained from a prominent financial institution between January 2023 and December 2024 through applications supported by forged and fictitious documents. The agency also said that loan proceeds were then moved through bank accounts held by third parties.

The FID identified the six individuals charged as Errol Williams, 39, a business owner and accountant from St Catherine; Christine Elliot, 52, a customer service representative from St Catherine; Staisha Campbell, 24, who is unemployed and from St Catherine; Paige Dixon, 34, a labourer and farmer and Adrien Kerry-Ann Gordon, 44, a self-employed shopkeeper, both from Kingston; and Admarie Ashman, 58, who is self-employed and from the Kingston 3 area.

The FID said Williams was arrested on September 24, 2026, during an intelligence-led search operation. “He is alleged to have benefited by approximately $20 million from the scheme. He was offered bail in the sum of $1.5 million with a surety,” the FID said in a news release late Thursday evening.

Elliot and Campbell were arrested and charged on September 16, 2026, following a search operation. They are alleged to have received $1.35 million and $1.2 million, respectively in loan proceeds. Each was offered bail in the sum of $500,000 with a surety.

Dixon and Gordon were arrested on September 9, 2026, following a search operation. Each is alleged to have received $1.5 million in loan proceeds, which was withdrawn. They were offered bail in the sum of $500,000 each with a surety, while Ashman was arrested and charged on October 20, 2026, following a search operation at her home.

“All six face charges of engaging in a transaction involving criminal property under the Proceeds of Crime Act; uttering forged documents under the Forgery Act; obtaining credit by fraud under the Larceny Act; and conspiracy to defraud under common law,” the FID said.

It added that Williams is also charged with possession of criminal property.

The FID said Ashman, who remains in custody, is scheduled to appear in the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court, Criminal Division on Friday, October 23, 2026. The other five accused appeared in the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court, Criminal Division, on October 13, 2026, each represented by an attorney.

The matter was adjourned for mention on February 16, 2027 with the following bail conditions:

• A stop order has been placed on their movement;

• They have surrendered their travel documents;

• They are to report to the police twice weekly; and

• They are not to interact or interfere with witnesses.

The FID said that on December 24, 2024, the financial institution reported to the police that documentation submitted in support of loan applications made by 79 individuals, between January 2023 and December 2024, was fraudulent.

“The institution had identified irregularities in the applicants’ files and, when it tried to verify the applicants’ stated places of employment, could not locate them at the addresses provided. By then, the loans had been disbursed and were not being repaid,” the FID said.

“It is alleged that forged job letters, utility bills, and pay advices were submitted to support the loan applications. Analysis of the bank accounts of two of the accused indicated that most of the loan funds received were subsequently transferred to third-party accounts,” the FID added.

The law enforcement agency also said it is further alleged that Williams “created fictitious documents, provided bank accounts to others and instructed that loan funds be transferred to them, and obtained a fraudulent driver’s licence and birth certificate and opened bank accounts in fictitious names to facilitate the deposit of loan funds”.

The FID said that Ashman was taken into custody following a search operation conducted on October 20, 2026, by members of the Constabulary Financial Unit, assisted by personnel of the Kingston Eastern Police Division, under a warrant issued pursuant to the Financial Investigations Division Act.

“She was held on reasonable suspicion of engaging in a transaction involving criminal property, obtaining credit by fraud, uttering forged documents and conspiracy to defraud, and was subsequently charged,” the FID said.

It added that during the search, “Ashman was found in possession of two separate forms of Government-issued photo identification, a driver’s licence and an electoral identification card, which carry different dates of birth: One in her name and the other in the name ‘Cassandra Burton’. Numerous items, including banking cards, letters and other printed documents, were seized by the police, taken into custody and entered into evidence.”

Commenting on the matter, FID Chief Technical Director Dennis Chung said: “The activity alleged in this matter, although sophisticated, expansive and creative, was no match for the skills of our forensic investigators. It spanned a long period, involved many individuals, and relied on documents, accounts and identities made to look legitimate. The investigation required close collaboration and the expertise of one of our longstanding strategic partners, the JCF.

“We also want the public to understand how easy it can be for persons to get caught up in a money mule scheme such as this. A request to receive money, or to lend an account or identification, can seem harmless, but it can make a person a pawn in someone else’s criminal activity. We urge everyone to remain vigilant, to ask questions and to refuse any such request, as you will be held criminally liable.”

Arguing that financial institutions also have a critical role to play, Chung said: “We encourage them to strengthen their due diligence capabilities, both in assessing loan applications and applicants, and in vetting their own employees, whether new hires or those with long tenures. Due diligence is not a one-time exercise. It must be sustained, as it protects institutions, their customers and the wider financial system.”

The FID also reminded the public that the charges are allegations and that each of the accused is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.

World.title: It’s Timeless!
World.content:
Ricardo Smith .

What initially started as co-producing songs for some of the biggest names in the dancehall space has morphed into a various artistes rhythm project.

Jamaican label Armzhouse Records has teamed up with overseas-based Land Lawd Music for the release of the six-song project Timeless rhythm.

Maurice Linton, who alongside Everton “Rado” Minott are the driving forces behind Armzhouse Records, explained how the joint collaboration with Land Lawd Music came about.

“Our label has been somewhat of a musical mentor to Ricardo Smith of Land Lawd Music. This journey began when we collaborated on singles for different artistes, so when we decided to commence work on the Timeless rhythm, it was just to create a body of work that stood the test of time — songs that could resonate with everyone and have a longer shelf life. This was a shared vision between both entities. The aim of the collaboration was to bring our creative ideas together, develop a strong body of work, and build upon the foundation of the Timeless rhythm project. By combining our experience, creativity, and passion for music, we wanted to create something meaningful,” Linton told the Jamaica Observer’s Splash recently.

Linton added: “Our previous collaborations have done well so there is a musical chemistry between both entities. We always deliver great work, so we decided to repeat the formula.”

The Timeless rhythm features the songs God and I by I-Octane, which was included on the dancehall artiste’s 2025 album of the same name, and for which a music video has now been released.

Apologies by chart-topper Turbulence; Born Fighter by Zagga, who is best known for his #1 hit My Destination; Calling On You by Frassman Brilli; Victory by Ras Shiloh and Norris Man; and Late Night by Mr Melody.

Linton said: “After hearing the rhythm, we knew that it would be one of those rhythms that would be played many years from now. It has a longevity sound. Hence, the reason it’s called Timeless. And getting the artistes involved was quite easy. From the moment they heard it, it’s like the lyrics and melodies just started to flow out of nowhere. Every artiste on the project gravitated to it with the right energy. The rhythm truly is Timeless.”

According to Linton, the success of I-Octane’s God and I single was what prompted his team to get other artistes involved.

“The first song that we released I-Octane’s song, which is on his album, and it accumulated more than one million streams on Apple Music. And with that kind of success, we decided to open up the project to other artistes and the quality of music that we got was well-received,” he disclosed.

Smith, who says the name of his label represents his entrepreneurial mindset, and whose ultimate goal is to one day earn a Grammy Award, says he is pleased with the feedback that the project has so far received.

“I think it’s a job well done. The feedback is great, both from the artistes and listeners. With a project like this we can see it growing more in the reggae space, thanks to an incredible line-up of artistes that we worked with,” said Smith.

The video for Apologies by Turbulence has now been released.

World.title: Boys need more male teachers
World.content:
The Education Transformation Oversight Committee is arguing that the response to boys’ under-performance cannot be left to the education ministry alone, as the difficulties affecting some students were linked to circumstances both inside and outside the classroom.

AS Jamaica searches for answers to the persistent under-performance of boys in school, chairman of the Education Transformation Oversight Committee (ETOC) Dr Adrian Stokes is calling for a closer look at the gender balance among the country’s teachers, arguing that more men must be encouraged to enter the profession.

His call comes as the education ministry continues to find ways to develop preliminary measures to improve how boys learn.

Speaking during an ETOC quarterly press conference on Thursday, Stokes said the country needed to examine how it could attract more men to teaching.

“We may have to look at how much room we have to provide incentives for males to enter the teaching profession. There’s a plethora of female teachers. Sometimes when I go into a room for a meeting with anything to do with education it’s a preponderance of females. We need to have a better balance in terms of the gender mix that we have in education,” Stokes argued.

He noted that the response to boys’ under performance could not be left to the education ministry alone, as the difficulties affecting some students were linked to circumstances both inside and outside the classroom.

“For the psychosocial issues, it will have to be a joined-up approach. It’s not just the Ministry of Education. We’re talking about social work, social services, Ministry of Labour and Social Security, Ministry of National Security. It will take a holistic approach of joined-up government to really deal with the problem in the manner that it deserves,” he added.

The ministry’s preliminary approach identifies three areas for action: making classroom learning more engaging for boys, replacing punitive discipline with restorative measures, and providing support for the social and psychological challenges that may affect their education.

Stokes said the ministry had done considerable work to develop a systematic response, but stressed that the proposals were still at an early stage and had not received final approval.

He said the country needed practical measures that could be tested and improved, rather than assuming that one committee or a single intervention would solve the problem.

Acting Chief Education Officer Terry-Ann Thomas Gayle said the ministry was continuing to strengthen psychosocial support in schools, including through cluster-based guidance counsellors who serve several institutions where a counsellor is not assigned to an individual school.

She said the ministry had also incorporated a psychosocial component into its boys’ education programme and was working with teams to develop activities and support measures for male students.

Thomas Gayle said the ministry wanted to encourage more men to participate in education, including through mentoring.

“We welcome more men to really take part in education… but wherever there are males in education we’re maximising how we utilise their support in ensuring that we pull more boys into the focus. Our males in education, part of the thrust for our revisit to how we look at boys, is really to get more of our males to be mentors, and we want those boys in our schools, in our high schools specifically, and in our tertiary institutions, to volunteer to be peer mentors,” she said.

She added that the ministry intended to expand programmes already operating in some schools.

Thomas Gayle also argued that the national standards curriculum included activities designed to engage boys, particularly in subjects such as science, where practical and experimental learning can be used.

Meanwhile, minister of state in the Ministry of Education Rhoda Moy Crawford, who said boys’ education had long been one of her interests, expressed optimism that the situation could improve.

“One of the reasons why I’m very positive that all is not yet lost in terms of the education of our boys is when we look back at the top 10 PEP students, six of those students are boys… So I really know that all is not lost,” she said.

At ETOC’s previous quarterly press conference in July, Stokes warned that Jamaica had yet to find effective solutions to the long-standing gender gap in education. He cited findings from the review led by Professor Orlando Patterson, which pointed to social circumstances, abusive upbringings and cultural ideas about masculinity as factors that can discourage boys from engaging with school.

The committee has since placed the issue among its key priorities, as the ministry works to translate its preliminary ideas into practical measures.

World.title: WIGTON’S SOLAR SNAG
World.content:
WIGTON Energy has taken its concerns about delays in finalising a power purchase agreement with Jamaica Public Service Company (JPS) to the energy minister, as unresolved terms hold up financing for more than 70 megawatts of planned solar generation.

The company is aiming to break ground within six months, but told shareholders at its annual general meeting that it would not compromise their interests to get the agreement signed. The solar developments form part of a wider expansion programme under which Wigton expects to spend at least $8 billion over the next two years.

The BusinessWeek reported in October 2025 that the power purchase agreement (PPA) had been completed with JPS and submitted to the Office of Utilities Regulation, (OUR) for review. A year later, terms remain unresolved.

“We have recently met with JPS, met with the OUR and written to the minister of energy to express our concerns about how slow the process is moving. And this is not just for Wigton alone,” Wigton Energy chairman Dan Theoc told shareholders during the question-and-answer session.

“What we want to do is get that PPA executed in short order, move on to secure the financing, and then move on to construct the actual assets. And it has to happen in that order.”

Asked whether the delay effectively left the projects at a standstill, Theoc replied, “We cannot secure financing without an executed power purchase agreement.”

Wigton has leased land for the two solar developments, described at the meeting as approximately 50 megawatts and 20 megawatts. Its September interim report puts their combined capacity at 70.53 megawatts, more than the 62.7 megawatts of wind generation it currently operates.

JPS would purchase the electricity under a proposed 20-year agreement, but the terms must first be acceptable to Wigton and the lenders expected to finance construction.

Chief Executive Officer Gary Barrow acknowledged the difficulty during his presentation, saying negotiations had taken longer than anticipated.

“There are a few problematic provisions that we are working through, as we have to be sure that we represent the best interests of you, our shareholders,” Barrow said.

“And we will not expedite and compromise, notwithstanding we are aiming to break ground within the next six months.”

The provisions in dispute were not identified at the meeting. Theoc said the negotiations involve Wigton and JPS, with the OUR also participating.

“What we’re experiencing is a difficulty in finalising that PPA, which may or may not be related to the fact that JPS itself is going through a very dynamic time,” shareholders were told.

Wigton said it understood that the other successful bidder in the procurement round was similarly awaiting an agreement that would allow it to proceed with financing.

The company approaches the planned expansion with $3.26 billion in cash and cash equivalents at September 30, after fully repaying its Bond A obligation during the month. Total liabilities were down 23.7 per cent from a year earlier to $3.03 billion, while shareholders’ equity stood at $5.81 billion.

Management pointed to the investment programme when shareholders questioned the cash being held by the business.

“I see a future where in the next two to three years we will have doubled the size of the company and spent more than $8 billion in capital expenditure,” shareholders were told.

“So before the questions come about why are we sitting down on this $3 billion of cash, let me let you know right now that we plan to spend about $8 billion in the next two years. So we need that cash to help us grow the business.”

Wigton is also negotiating terms for its remaining Bond B, which has a principal balance of approximately $1.9 billion. Management said those discussions were advanced. The obligation falls due within the next 12 months, according to the September report.

Debt repayments have already reduced the cost of borrowing. Finance expenses fell 47.2 per cent to $81.2 million for the six months ended September, helping to cushion higher operating costs and a fall in other income.

The existing wind business is producing more electricity, although the improvement has not yet translated into higher profit across the full half-year.

Production rose 16.6 per cent to 94.7 million kilowatt-hours, supported by favourable wind conditions and spending on plant maintenance and repairs. Electricity sales increased 13.6 per cent to $1.51 billion.

Net profit, however, declined 11.5 per cent to $313.6 million from $354.5 million. Other income fell to $71.3 million from $210.1 million, largely because of lower insurance proceeds and foreign exchange gains. Repairs following the hurricanes of 2024 and 2025 also contributed to higher costs, while administrative spending increased as Wigton invested in staff and technology.

The July-to-September quarter showed an improvement. Net profit rose 51.8 per cent to $144.6 million, with electricity sales up 42.6 per cent to $726.5 million.

The expansion plans extend beyond the solar developments awaiting the JPS agreement. Wigton is in advanced negotiations for a solar project with a major Jamaican industrial company, part of its effort to build a business supplying commercial and industrial customers.

Management did not identify the prospective client or disclose the size of that individual project, but said the wider pipeline included 10 megawatts of capacity it could execute over the next two to three years.

Wigton is also pursuing business elsewhere in the Caribbean, with its September report confirming that it has been shortlisted to participate in upcoming regional requests for proposals. The company did not identify the markets or disclose the potential size of those projects.

Barrow said the regional expansion would involve strategic partners as Wigton broadens its energy portfolio and reduces its dependence on a single market.

“Our ultimate ambition is definitive and unwavering. Wigton will become the largest renewable energy powerhouse in the Caribbean,” he told shareholders.

World.title: Nearly all coral reefs risk collapse in 50 years, IUCN warns
World.content:
This picture taken on October 5, 2026, shows healthy coral growing in the waters of the Naidiri Marine Biodiversity Park, a marine protected area located about 52 kilometres from Nadi. Almost all shallow-water coral reefs around the world are at “extremely high risk” of disappearing by 2075 due to climate change, the International Union for Conservation of Nature warned on October 22, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

YEREVAN, Armenia (AFP) — Nearly all of the world’s shallow-water coral reefs face an extremely high risk of collapse by 2075 due to climate change, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) warned Thursday.

In the first global assessment of its kind, the world authority on threatened wildlife classified 96 per cent of the planet’s coral reef systems as “critically endangered” — its highest risk category.

Corals are heat sensitive and particularly vulnerable to human-driven climate change, which is warming the world’s oceans and increasing the frequency and intensity of damaging bleaching events.

“The future threat of climate change is looming and severe, and that poses a very high risk to the survival of these ecosystems,” said Mishal Gudka, scientific lead of the IUCN Red List of Coral Reef Ecosystems assessment.

The emergence this year of a “super” El Nino, the natural warming phenomenon, also presents a risk to corals, Gudka said at a news conference at the UN’s COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia.

The IUCN presented its findings at COP17, where governments are under pressure to make progress on a landmark pact to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030.

For its assessment, the IUCN used the “middle-of-the-road” scenario from the UN’s panel of climate experts that projects global temperatures rising 2.7C above pre-industrial levels by 2100.

The world is on track for 2.6C warming this century under current global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions, the United Nations warned Wednesday.

“Heat stress from climate change is the single most consistent threat driving coral reef decline worldwide,” the IUCN said in a statement.

Overfishing is also hurting corals as certain herbivores and predators help control algae and maintain an ecological balance, the organisation said.

The overexploitation of parrotfish and other groupers threatens 63 per cent of coral reef ecosystems.

Coastal development, pollution, tourism and more frequent storms are among other threats.

World.title: Ukraine and Russia each exchange 270 prisoners of war
World.content:
Moscow’s defense ministry also confirmed the exchange in a statement, saying Friday that the 270 exchanged Russian prisoners were in Belarus.

A prisoner exchange deal was brokered by U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration in May. The process is expected to involve 2,000 prisoners of war in total, Zelenskyy said at the time. The latest wave of exchanges took place soon after the end of another round of negotiations in Oslo and St. Petersburg.

“We express our gratitude to the United States of America and the United Arab Emirates, and in particular, we thank everyone who contributed to the release of Stephen Hubbard — a 74-year-old English teacher from Izium who was unlawfully convicted and subjected to torture by the Russians,” Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War said in a statement.

Most of the military personnel handed over to Ukraine had been detained since 2022, authorities said. Some had even been captured in 2018 and 2020, during the war in Donbas.

World.title: French prosecutors open hate crime probe after deadly drive-by shooting
World.content:
Earlier in the day, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on X that at least one person had been killed and four others injured in a shooting in Trappes, a suburb west of Paris with a lower socioeconomic status and a large Muslim community. A 12-year-old was among those injured, the mayor of nearby town La Verrière told reporters.

“The main focus will obviously be on identifying the perpetrator’s motives — what drove him to attempt to carry out a massacre … to target our communities,” Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh said on French broadcaster BFM.

“Our thoughts are with the victims, their families, and all the residents of Yvelines. During this terrible ordeal, the nation stands with them,” President Emmanuel Macron said on social media.

Marine Le Pen, the front-running far-right candidate for next year’s presidential election slammed the killing as “a barbaric act whose motives must be determined, and of which those responsible must be severely punished.”

“Racism kills,” Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the leading left-wing candidate for next year’s election. “In the face of this heinous crime, all human beings are reminded that they are alike as they see themselves united in horror and outrage.”

Center-right candidate Edouard Philippe said “terrorism must be fought relentlessly, with absolute determination” and that “the investigation will have to determine the motives of the perpetrator of this despicable act.”

This is a developing story.

World.title: EU prosecutor probes EPP over consultant contracts
World.content:
It covered only the initial €110,000 payments, leaving the EPP to pay roughly €350,000 itself, according to Germany’s Süddeutsche Zeitung, Dutch investigative outlet Follow the Money and Greece’s Inside Story.

The consultants were hired to work on the party’s communications ahead of the election campaign. However, former EPP employees told reporters at the outlets that their fees were disproportionate to the work they delivered. The consultants disputed that assessment and said they had subsequently reimbursed part of the money.

The EPPO neither confirmed nor denied the investigation, saying it could not comment in case it jeopardized any ongoing proceedings or their outcome.

A spokesperson for the EPP said: “We have not been formally notified regarding this matter. The EPP fully respects the independence and mandate of the relevant authorities and remains committed to providing them complete transparency and full cooperation, should it be requested.”

World.title: Drone hits another ship in Black Sea near Romania, killing at least 1 sailor
World.content:
The incident is the latest in a string of drone attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Dan told POLITICO last week that Russia’s intention was clearly to weaken Romania’s support for Ukraine in the war but vowed not to back down.

NATO allies met Tuesday to discuss the threat to Black Sea shipping and Dan said Romania would receive “additional capabilities” to help defend the area.

“Evidently, this is an incident within the broader process of escalation that Russia is pursuing in the context of its war in Ukraine,” the Romanian president said.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she was “deeply alarmed” by “yet another Russian escalation in the Black Sea.” The ship was carrying Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew, she said.

“These reckless attacks target innocent lives and openly defy international law. My thoughts are with the family and loved ones of the sailor that was killed. And with the families of the three crew members still missing.”

Over the last month, drones have hit several cargo ships and chemical tankers close to Romania and Bulgaria — both NATO members — killing more than 20 people in total.

Reuters reported that the ships hit by drones in recent weeks had been near or heading towards the Sulina Canal, linking the Danube River and the Black Sea. This has become a key export route for Ukrainian grain and food oil after Russia attacked Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports.

This article was updated.

World.title: Top ICC official urges EU to act ‘as soon as possible’ on US sanctions
World.content:
That has agonized senior figures in The Hague. Zavala Giler said the Commission's "lack of clarity" left private companies and NGOs in the dark over whether they should comply with sanctions decided by Washington — and what risks they face if they don't.

Zavala Giler's call to the Commission adds to pressure from EU lawmakers for a swift response after the Oct. 9 announcement. Kallas told the European Parliament on Tuesday that Brussels would use the next few months "to open dialogue" on the issue. The new sanctions are set to take effect in April next year.

"What I would hope is that the space for dialogue is not interpreted as a space for waiting to protect the court," Zavala Giler said, who spoke from his glass office on the eve of a visit to the Court’s headquarters by the EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

Damocles sword

Anticipating sweeping sanctions, the Court spent six months abandoning U.S. tech providers and moving to an open-source software environment, and 20 months to make its financial transactions dollar-proof. That move has been a huge undertaking for Zavala Giler's team, he said.

The Court initially deepened its reliance on U.S. technology after it was hit by a massive cyber attack in 2023, but what seemed a solution at that time became a problem in the face of sanctions. Even though the current regime includes a carveout for telecommunications, there is no guarantee it will remain the case.

"It becomes a sort of Damocles sword on top of our head that could be revoked at any time," Zavala Giler said. "I cannot count on U.S. tech companies anymore."

World.title: Feijóo vows conservative overhaul if he wins Spain’s Nov. 29 election
World.content:
“I cannot rule out doing what the Spanish people tell me,” Feijóo said, acknowledging the polls which currently indicate the PP would need Vox’s support to secure a parliamentary majority. “If they tell me to provide stability with [Vox], I will do so.”

If such a partnership is needed, Vox is expected to demand a deputy prime minister post and at least one ministry, as it has in regional coalitions with the PP. POLITICO’s Madrid Playbook this week reported on speculation that the far-right party could be given the agriculture portfolio, but Feijóo said he had held no formal talks on allocating ministries.

During the interview, the conservative leader vowed to revise Spain’s abortion law, which was amended in 2023 to allow minors over 16 to terminate pregnancies without parental consent. Feijóo said he was keen to involve legal guardians in the decision, arguing that “many 16-year-old girls who have their parents’ support will not want to have an abortion.”

It’s unclear whether that measure would satisfy Vox, which has sought to completely repeal the current abortion law and rejects abortion as a legal right.

The PP leader also pledged to restrict access to euthanasia, which Spain legalized in 2021 for adults with serious, incurable illnesses or severe, chronic and disabling conditions under strict safeguards. “Spain must become the country where it is easiest to sustain life,” he said.

Feijóo also promised to scrap the standalone Equality Ministry as part of a broader effort to reduce the size of government. He insisted the move did not undermine his commitment to feminism. “I grew up in a house with more women than men. How could I think that a woman doesn’t have the same rights as a man?” he said.

Feijóo declined to explicitly commit to further increase the minimum wage, which has risen eight times under Sánchez, from €735 a month in 2018 to €1,221 today. His goal, he said, was to raise “the average wage, so that people’s purchasing power improves.”

World.title: Starlink still restricted for Ukraine despite Trump saying Musk lifted speed limits
World.content:
Ukrainian drone units started testing speed limits from Thursday evening, shortly after Trump told reporters that Musk had restored Starlink. While some tests recorded speeds of up to 200 km/h over the Black Sea and noted an improvement, the drones still rapidly lost signal once flying above the 160 km/h speed limit.

“So, the key point is: We accelerate above 180 km/h, fly for a couple of minutes, the connection drops. It falls to 140–150 km/h and then is re-established — but the situation is better,” a drone pilot from Ukraine’s top drone unit known as Magyar’s Birds told POLITICO. “So it works better, but with constant connection interruptions,” the pilot, whose call sign is Leon, said.

The speed limit on Starshield, Starlink’s service designed for military purposes, stalled key operations and partially disabled crucial drone interceptors against Russian Shaheds attack drones.

Musk said that the U.S. government controlled Starshield, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the administration could not direct SpaceX or Musk regarding restrictions or slowdowns of Starlink services in Ukraine as it is a private company.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy argued the Starlink restriction was a planned operation to specifically restrict Starshield’s operating speed over Ukraine. The Ukrainian government said that it was not told why that had happened for days. However, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Trump had called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions.

“I don’t want to say. That’s a very interesting situation. My relationship with Elon is very good. I don’t want to comment on it, whether I called, or someone else called … The bottom line: he put it back,” Trump told reporters on Thursday evening.

World.title: Die Suche nach dem Super-Sozi
World.content:
In der SPD brodelt es gewaltig an der Basis und in der Fraktion. Ex-Arbeitsminister Hubertus Heil bringt sich als neuer Parteivorsitzender in Stellung und sägt am Stuhl von Lars Klingbeil. Maximilian Heimerzheim analysiert, wer als weibliche Doppelspitze infrage kommt und warum Manuela Schwesig noch zögert.

Im 200-Sekunden-Interview fordert der SPD-Bundestagsabgeordnete Ralf Stegner eine personelle Neuaufstellung seiner Partei. Der Parteilinke erklärt, warum die Sozialdemokraten dringend wieder als breite Volkspartei auftreten müssen, um den Absturz bei künftigen Wahlen zu verhindern.

Auf dem CSU-Parteitag inszeniert sich der bayerische Ministerpräsident Markus Söder als unangefochtener Herrscher. Doch Landtagspräsidentin Ilse Aigner bleibt eine interne Gefahr. Nikolaus Doll beleuchtet, warum das taktische Rennen um das Amt des Bundespräsidenten über Söders politische Zukunft entscheidet.

Das Berlin Playbook als Podcast gibt es jeden Morgen ab 5 Uhr. Rixa Fürsen, Maximilian Stascheit und das POLITICO-Team liefern Politik zum Hören – kompakt, international, hintergründig.
