World.title: Negotiations Continue Between Zagreb Airport and Wizz Air
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Negotiations are continuing between Zagreb Airport and Wizz Air, with the popular airline citing cost issues being the primary remaining obstacle.

During September, 455,530 passengers passed through the airport, while the growth rate for the first nine months of the year fell to just 1.1 percent. As is somewhat seasonally appropriate, the capital’s airport recorded its third consecutive monthly drop in passenger numbers; in September traffic fell by 3.3 percent, continuing the slowdown that began back in July. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that during that month, 455,530 passengers passed through the airport, while the growth rate for the first nine months of the year shrank to only 1.1 percent. The latest figures come at a time when Croatia Airlines is reducing capacity during the process of renewing its fleet.

new routes and a new incentive scheme

Passenger numbers at the airport are expected to fall again in October, followed by a gradual recovery in November, while December, according to estimates, should remain at last year’s levels, reports Ex-Yu Aviation News. Zagreb Airport has attracted four new routes this year, including those to Warsaw (Modlin), Tel Aviv and Beijing (via Bucharest). By comparison, six new routes were introduced in 2025 and ten back in 2024. During 2026, the airport also lost four routes, three of which were operated by Croatia Airlines. Several factors have influenced the slowdown in growth: rising fuel prices, which make airlines more cautious about launching new routes; the stall in the expansion of Croatia Airlines’ network; and the increase in almost all basic airport charges and fees at Zagreb Airport.

Zagreb Airport is trying to return to stronger growth and has launched a new incentive scheme for which airlines can apply until the 31st of December. This new model significantly lowers the threshold for obtaining incentives compared with the previous system – in which the wildly popular Ryanair was the only beneficiary, and carriers were required to achieve at least 35,000 passengers per year. This change is expected to make the system more accessible, especially for smaller markets and airlines considering routes with lower passenger volumes. Another key difference concerns the duration and flexibility of the programme.

ongoing negotiations with wizz air

The previous model was designed for a five-year period, while the new one is limited to four years but introduces mechanisms that reward better results in the initial phase. Carriers that exceed the figure of 100,000 or 150,000 passengers in the first five years of operations can secure the continuation of incentives without the obligation to meet annual thresholds. As part of its new growth incentive model, Zagreb Airport is excluding certain destinations from the list of eligible ones, as they are considered either sufficiently developed or strategically less important within this programme.

Despite interest in Zagreb, Wizz Air announced this summer that costs associated with the airport remain the main obstacle to establishing a base in Croatia’s capital. Nevertheless, they have not ruled out the possibility of introducing flights to Zagreb and confirmed that negotiations are ongoing. Zagreb Airport ended last year with a record of almost 4.7 million passengers, an increase of 9.2 percent compared with 2024. Based on currently reported capacities on scheduled routes, Zagreb Airport is expected to record an overall capacity increase of 1.8 percent in November.

This is mainly contributed by Ryanair, which will offer just over 17,000 additional seats, as well as the new Air China route and capacity increases by Austrian Airlines, KLM and Air Serbia. For December, stagnation is currently forecast, with around 100 fewer seats than in the same month last year. Capacity reductions at Croatia Airlines, Lufthansa and Qatar Airways are the main factors negatively affecting growth during the last month of the year.

World.title: Hajduk Beats Thun 1-0 to End 32-Year Wait for European Away Win
World.content:
Hajduk made it two wins from two in the Conference League league phase on Thursday night, beating Thun 1-0 in Switzerland. Dalisson scored the only goal in the 17th minute. Gonzalo Garcia’s side dominated the first half but had to withstand heavy pressure after the break, in a match that featured remarkable misses at both ends.

The result ended a long wait. Hajduk’s last away win in the group or league phase of a European competition came on September 28, 1994, when Aljoša Asanović’s 88th-minute goal earned a 1-0 win over Steaua in Bucharest in the Champions League. Following their 2-1 win over Ajax in the opening round, Hajduk now have a maximum of six points from two matches.

Lineups

Thun (4-4-2): Steffen; Fehr, Bürki, Bamert, Mambwa; Reichmuth, Roth, Kait, Maier; Labeau, Dursun

Hajduk (4-2-3-1): Silić; Acapandié, Hadžikadunić, Marešić, Hrgović; Del Moral, Fayad; Bamba, Dalisson, Šotiček; Šego

Match report

Hajduk set the tone from the start. Bamba went down under a challenge from Mambwa in the Thun box in the 2nd minute without getting a decision, and needed treatment on his ankle. A minute later, Šego tested Steffen, who saved comfortably.

Hrgović broke superbly down the left in the 10th minute, but his pass for Šego was cut out. By the 13th minute, Hajduk had two-thirds of the possession and were pressing Thun high up the pitch, and four minutes later that pressure paid off. Nico Maier gave the ball away in midfield, and Dalisson carried it to the edge of the box. His first shot was blocked, but the ball came straight back to him, and the Brazilian flicked it into the net with the outside of his boot for 1-0.

Thun should have equalized in the 24th minute. Brighton Labeau got away from Acapandié and fired low inside the box, but Silić saved, and Furkan Dursun dragged the rebound wide from 16 meters. Mambwa blazed over from more than 20 meters in the 30th minute.

Thun saw more of the ball after falling behind, but Hajduk’s pressing kept them from settling, and the chances kept coming for them. Šotiček’s effort from around 20 meters in the 33rd minute was heading just inside the post until Steffen tipped it behind. From the resulting corner, Hrgović was free on the left of the box, but he fired well over. Fayad then shot straight at Steffen from 17 meters, and in the 37th minute Bamba struck the post directly from a corner.

Hrgović blocked a Fehr shot in the 44th minute. Two minutes were added, and Hajduk went in 1-0 up at the half, a lead that could easily have been bigger.

Neither side made changes at the break, but the balance shifted quickly. Del Moral was booked in the 47th minute for stopping a Mambwa run, and Thun began to push Hajduk back. Fehr curled wide of the right post from the edge of the box in the 54th minute. Labeau’s turn and shot was blocked two minutes later, and Roth was booked for pulling back Dalisson to stop a counter. Reichmuth then shot straight at Silić in the 58th minute.

Marešić was booked in the 64th minute. A minute later, Del Moral headed a Fehr free kick clear just ahead of Bürki, and Labeau sent a shot over from around ten meters after a corner.

Hajduk had a golden chance to double their lead in the 68th minute, when Olivier Mambwa shoved Bamba in the box, and Gillett pointed to the spot. Šego stepped up but struck a weak penalty down the middle, an easy save for Steffen.

Melnjak then replaced Šotiček for Hajduk. Reichmuth was booked in the 73rd minute for a foul on Del Moral.

Then came the miss of the night. In the 75th minute, Labeau broke down the right and squared the ball to Noah Christoffersson, who somehow put it wide of an empty net from close range.

García brought on Livaja and Dendoncker for Šego and Del Moral in the 78th minute, while Thun replaced Labeau and Roth with Braschi and Derbaci, and later Reichmuth with Lengen. Martin and Van Hoorenbeeck replaced Bamba and Fayad in the 84th minute. Livaja won a free kick two minutes later and then headed wide from the resulting cross.

Four minutes of stoppage time were added, and Hajduk nearly sealed it on the break in the 92nd minute, when Dalisson tried to lob from distance and hit the crossbar. Hajduk held on for a 1-0 win and a significant step towards the knockout phase of the Conference League.

World.title: Austrian Airlines is Scrapping Zagreb-Vienna Route After 40 Years
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Austrian Airlines is scrapping its direct Zagreb-Vienna route after 40 years, leaving the question of who will take on the Zagreb-Vienna route open.

Austrian Airlines will discontinue its long-standing route between Vienna and Zagreb next year. Index reports that the last flight between the two capitals is planned for the 10th of January 2027, and the Star Alliance member has confirmed that it will not reinstate the route even during the summer season of 2027.

“We can confirm that our flights between Vienna and Zagreb will, unfortunately, not continue during the summer season,” Austrian Airlines spokesperson Andrea Hansal told EX-YU Aviation News. With this, the carrier will leave Zagreb after more than four decades of operation. It introduced flights to the Croatian capital in the mid-1980s and interrupted services during the war and the COVID-19 pandemic.

the number of flights has already allegedly been reduced by austrian airlines

In recent years, Austrian Airlines has significantly reduced the number of flights operating on the Vienna–Zagreb route. The carrier previously operated up to 12 flights a week, but during the summer season of 2026 it reduced them to one daily flight. This represented a 37.5 percent reduction in the number of flights and a 27 percent reduction in available seat capacity compared with the previous year. The reduction in the number of flights during the winter began as early as the end of 2024, when the company thinned out departures and introduced smaller turboprop aircraft. At the same time, Croatia Airlines, also a Star Alliance member, expanded its offer on this route. During the summer of 2026 it doubled the number of flights to Vienna, to a total of ten per week.

Croatia Airlines will continue flying between Zagreb and Vienna during the upcoming winter season, which starts this Sunday, and will retain two daily flights, as it did last winter.

zagreb airport continues to expand its destination network and bring in new airlines

Austrian Airlines, on the other hand, will continue to operate daily flights until the route is discontinued in January. Many of them will be operated by aircraft of the company Air Dolomiti, which Austrian Airlines uses under a wet-lease agreement. All of this is happening at a time when Zagreb International Airport is trying to attract new carriers and expand its destination network. The airport is participating in the Routes World conference currently being held in Frankfurt. Zagreb Airport is represented there by President of the Management Board and CEO Huseyin Bahadır Bedir and Head of Route Development Yavuz Aytis.

World.title: NEC Stun Dinamo 4-2 at Maksimir in the Europa League
World.content:
Dinamo suffered their first European defeat of the season on Thursday night, losing 4-2 at Maksimir to NEC Nijmegen in the third round of the Europa League league phase. Dion Drena Beljo scored twice for the home side, but NEC captain Tjaronn Chery struck two of his own, with Clement Bischoff and Bryan Linssen also on target.

Dinamo went in as clear favorites. NEC arrived in Zagreb having gone two months without a win, and the stakes for the home side were high: according to Football Meets Data, a win would have given Dinamo roughly an 80 percent chance of a top-24 finish, while defeat would drop those odds below 50 per cent.

Lineups

Dinamo: Kotarski; Galešić, Domínguez, McKenna, Perez Vinlof; Stojković, Mišić, Ivanušec; Almena, Beljo, Hoxha

NEC: Crettaz; Storm, Schuurs, Fonville; Geiger, Nejašmić, Lebreton, Kaplan; Chery, Linssen, Bischoff

Match report

Dinamo had the better of the opening exchanges. Beljo forced the first save from Gonzalo Crettaz in the 3rd minute with a shot on his weaker right foot. Five minutes later, Schuurs cleared a Galešić cross just ahead of Stojković. Ivanušec went down in the box in the 17th minute, but the referee waved play on.

The home side went closest in the 20th minute. Almena slipped Stojković into space, and he lifted the ball over Crettaz, only for Kaplan to hook it off the line. Two minutes later, NEC produced their best effort to that point, as Lebreton’s long-range strike came back off the crossbar. Beljo was booked in the 24th minute.

Against the run of play, NEC went ahead in the 25th minute. Tobias Storm raced down the right and crossed for Bischoff at the far post, who took a touch, beat Galešić and scored.

Dinamo equalized in the 33rd minute. Stojković sent Perez Vinlof away on the left, and his cross to the far post was met by Beljo, who rose highest between two defenders to head in for 1-1. Ivanušec thought he had put Dinamo ahead two minutes later, but his goal was ruled offside. In the 37th minute, Stojković laid the ball off in a quick move for Beljo to finish from around ten meters and make it 2-1.

Lebreton was booked in the 44th minute for bringing down Beljo, and NEC equalized right on half-time. Bischoff broke down the left and delivered a difficult cross that Linssen met with a diving header for 2-2.

Neither side made changes at the break, and it was NEC who took control. By the 52nd minute, Dinamo were pinned inside their own final third, and two minutes later, the visitors went back in front. Darko Nejašmić played the ball forward to Linssen, who found Chery in the middle. The NEC captain applied just enough of a touch to beat Kotarski for 3-2.

Rodríguez replaced Almena in the 58th minute and quickly became Dinamo’s main outlet down the right. Stojković lobbed Crettaz on the counter in the 62nd minute but missed the target. Ivanušec went down in the box again two minutes later without reward, and Crettaz parried another Stojković effort in the 65th. Mario Kovačević turned to Oršić and Valinčić in the 67th minute, replacing Galešić and Hoxha.

NEC rode their luck in the 72nd minute. Rodríguez beat three players and set up Mišić, whose fierce shot from distance was saved by Crettaz, who then stopped Oršić’s follow-up. Three minutes later, Rodríguez cut inside and teed up Beljo, who could not convert from close range. Goda came on for Perez Vinlof in the 76th minute, with Monteiro replacing Geiger for NEC.

Chery settled it in the 80th minute, collecting a loose ball on the edge of the box and firing into the top corner for his second of the night. Crettaz denied Rodríguez after a counter in the 83rd minute and then saved an excellent Oršić free kick two minutes later, and NEC saw out four minutes of stoppage time to complete the win.

It was a first defeat in Europe this season for Dinamo and a first Europa League win for NEC. Dinamo travel to Sunderland on November 5 for their next league-phase match.

World.title: Croatian Government Gives 15,000 Unlicensed Apartments 4 More Years
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – The Croatian Government has given in on certain aspects of the Hospitality Activity Act, providing 15,000 unlicensed apartments 4 more years to operate.

The Croatian Government has now accepted the final proposal of the Hospitality Activity Act, which extends the validity of temporary decisions for around 15,000 landlords by an additional four years, the Ministry of Tourism and Sport announced. Index reports that these temporary decisions – on the basis of which apartments and rooms operate in buildings that do not have all the necessary papers, an occupancy permit, or are still waiting for the completion of the legalisation process – were due to expire at the end of this year. If the law had remained unchanged, thousands of landlords would have had to lock up, but with the new legislative proposal the Government has moved the deadline all the way to the 31st of December 2030.

protecting the livelihoods of family landlords

Tourism and Sport Minister Tonči Glavina said that this protects the livelihood of family landlords and ensures the continuity of their business so that they have enough time to legalise their properties and obtain permanent permits. “This is an important measure, especially when we take into account that at the end of 2024 around 15,000 landlords were operating on the basis of temporary decisions,” Glavina stated.

unique registration numbers as of 2027

In addition to extending the permits for legalisation, the law also brings novelties aimed at combating unregistered rentals. A unique registration number is being introduced for accommodation units advertised via online platforms such as Booking and Airbnb, but this provision will not enter into force immediately – only from the 1st of May 2027 so that the market has time to adapt. The state plans to establish direct data exchange with the platforms, which means that properties without a valid registration number would no longer be allowed to be advertised online. At the same time, county bodies are obliged to submit accurate data on the number of resolved cases and temporary decisions to the Ministry once a year, by the 30th of June.

higher penalties and closer inspections

The new legal framework also provides for higher misdemeanour fines for violations of the regulations, expanded powers for tourism and tax inspectors, and the digitisation of administrative procedures through the eTurizam system. Another novelty is that the rental of rooms and apartments in family houses will in future also be able to be registered through a craft or a limited liability company (d.o.o.), and not only in the status of a private landlord as has been the case until now. The bill has been sent to the parliamentary procedure for a second reading.

World.title: €3,000 Parking Fine Arrives a Year After Dubrovnik Trip – Poles Outraged
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – A €3,000 parking fine arrived at the addresses of tourists following their Dubrovnik trip an entire year later, and it’s safe to say they’re not happy…

Fines that some former visitors to Dubrovnik “earned” by parking their cars around the historic city centre are arriving months after they return from their holidays, and the case has attracted plenty of attention in the Polish media. Morski reports that one of the fined tourists contacted Croatia’s well known media outlet Index, claiming that because of two entries into the restricted zone he received two fines of €1,500 each, meaning the total sum amounted to €3,000.

“I’m writing to you on my own behalf and on behalf of many Polish tourists who, instead of returning with nice memories from a holiday in Croatia, specifically Dubrovnik, came back deeply disappointed by the greed and inhumane rules that apply in that city,” he wrote.

The Polish tourist claims that the fines reached him more than one year after his trip to Croatia. “Personally I received two separate fines of €1,500 each. In addition, the law firms hired by the city authorities don’t even reply to e-mails and it’s extremely difficult to communicate with them,” he stated. According to him, the problem has caused a lot of dissatisfaction among Polish tourists, and television stations and internet portals are reporting on it.

In addition, this particular Polish tourist complained that traffic signs warning about the entry restriction are in place, but he considers that it is nowhere near clear enough to tourists what they must do in order to be allowed to enter the zone by car, and that the fines are disproportionate to the offence. On the 2nd of June 2025, the City of Dubrovnik introduced a special traffic regime zone around the historic centre in order to reduce traffic congestion and protect the area that has been exposed to a large number of vehicles for years.

The City of Dubrovnik otherwise prescribed fines of €260 for natural persons, €660 for craftspersons and persons performing independent activities, and a significantly higher €1,320 for legal entities. The responsible person in a legal entity can be fined an additional €260.

World.title: Estonian employers get right to test employees' sobriety
World.content:
Amendments to the Occupational Health and Safety Act that take effect on October 26 will give employers the right to test employees for intoxication.

However, according to the Labor Inspectorate, this does not mean that every workday can now begin with a breathalyzer test. Under the new rules, employers may test employees for intoxication if there are reasonable grounds for suspicion. For example, suspicions may arise if an employee behaves unusually, slurs their speech or displays other signs of possible intoxication.

An exception applies to workplaces where working while intoxicated could have particularly serious consequences. If an employee's duties involve operating potentially hazardous equipment or they work in an environment involving such hazards, the employer may conduct intoxication tests even without reasonable suspicion. This could apply, for example, to bus and truck drivers, operators of dangerous machinery and construction workers.

The aim of the amendment is to prevent workplace accidents and protect employees, their colleagues and others.

Employers cannot conduct intoxication tests at their own discretion. Before conducting tests, they must establish written procedures and inform all employees of them. These procedures must clearly specify how testing will be conducted, what constitutes a positive result, the potential consequences of such a result and what happens if an employee refuses to be tested. Employees' rights must also be protected and they must have the opportunity to challenge test results.

Employers may retain intoxication test data for up to three years from the date of testing.

The Labor Inspectorate emphasizes that the purpose of intoxication testing must be to ensure workplace safety, not to subject employees to unjustified checks.

World.title: Prosecutors doubt sex offender ID photos in checks would help protect kids
World.content:
The Prosecutor's Office backs stronger background checks for people working with children but questions whether adding sex offenders' ID photos would really improve safety.

The Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs has submitted a bill of amendments to the Child Protection Act and the Criminal Records Database Act for review, aiming to simplify background checks on people working with children and strengthen safeguards against child sexual abuse (CSA).

Under the proposed changes, employers could automatically check employees' records monthly instead of manually at least once a year as currently required. The Social Insurance Board (SKA) would also be notified if an employee is barred from working with children.

The ministry also wants background checks to display the ID photos of people barred from working with children due to sexual offenses involving physical contact with minors.

The Prosecutor's Office, however, questions whether including the photos would really help keep kids safer. The ministry argues ID photos could help catch people who use false personal identification codes to evade checks, but prosecutors consider this unlikely.

They also note that the ministry's own explanatory memo acknowledges public sex offender registries have not been shown to reduce reoffending.

Prosecutors want more treatment, support for offenders

The Prosecutor's Office supports the overall goal of the proposal but says preventing CSA requires more investment in mental health services, counseling, treatment and specialist training.

Providing offenders with the necessary treatment and therapy is key to reducing repeat offenses, the office said, however Estonia lacks sufficient treatment options and social programs for both incarcerated offenders and convicted offenders living in the community.

Prosecutors acknowledge that the proposed changes would not worsen the status quo, but question how much more protection they would offer children.

SKA's child helpline, available in Estonian, Russian, and English, is open 24/7 at 116 111.

Callers, including kids, parents, teachers or other community members, can seek advice, support or report a child in danger.

In case of emergency, call 112.

World.title: Proposal. New national roadmap requires Estonian Convention on the Future
World.content:
Estonia needs a new mechanism for making long-term strategic decisions that brings together experts, politicians and citizens while remaining above day-to-day party politics, Erik Terk, Mati Heidmets and Marju Lauristin write.

The world finds itself in rough seas where many of the old rules and assumptions no longer apply. The power struggle between major powers and the redistribution of positions in the global market are dangerously rocking the boats of small countries, but they may also open up new windows of opportunity.

We must place Estonia within the broader picture of a changing world to ensure both our resilience against threats and our capacity for development. We need both the ability to adapt quickly and the capacity to make strategic changes that require sustained action over a longer period.

Unfortunately, we are witnessing trends in the opposite direction.

For example, efforts to reform the energy, education and healthcare systems are becoming bogged down in a deadlock of conflicting initiatives. Strengthening defense capabilities, ensuring the sustainability of the Estonian language and culture and achieving economic success all require a long-term vision, consistent action and shared determination.

Without these, development becomes erratic. Today we rush in one direction, tomorrow in another. Eventually, we may even lose sight of what kind of society we want to be once we have somehow managed to struggle through the waves of crises.

Successful governance of Estonia requires a different mechanism for shaping the future than the current practice of short-term political agreements can provide.

While firmly defending the values of democratic governance, we must acknowledge that the traditional forms of representative democracy inherited from the last century have become trapped in partisan conflicts that prevent them from effectively managing today's rapid and complex changes.

Building resilience for the future requires a broader societal platform that would both strengthen the intellectual capacity for planning long-term development and help ensure the quality and consistent implementation of strategic decisions that shape the country's future, regardless of the turbulence of day-to-day political confrontations.

To achieve this, we must find a way to bring together all the knowledge and goodwill available in Estonia when preparing decisions that will shape long-term development. This means involving as many leading researchers from different fields as possible, experts with significant international experience, political leaders from different party backgrounds, experienced and critically minded entrepreneurs and specialists who stay out of party politics and active ordinary citizens with extensive practical experience.

Borrowing the name of the Convention on the Future of Europe, which met some years ago, we have called our proposed mechanism the Estonian Convention on the Future. It would be a body that convenes periodically to review and refine the country's course of development and examine possible solutions to emerging issues of central importance.

The convention would not relieve elected representatives of their responsibility for political choices. Rather, it would serve as an additional or supporting mechanism for parliament, providing a stronger scientific and societal foundation for policymaking. As a body that we could reasonably expect to act in Estonia's overall interests, it would operate at some distance from day-to-day political life and competition between parties.

The convention would not make final decisions. Its task would be to carry out essential preparatory work for strategic choices, bringing together knowledge, experience and different perspectives from across society, examining alternatives and formulating possible options and proposals. Ideally, the convention could develop a comprehensive vision of development that takes into account the key dimensions of Estonia's future: social well-being, economic competitiveness, national security, environmental protection, demographic sustainability and the vitality of Estonian-language cultural life.

The central principle behind the convention's structure would be to bring together two distinct levels of participation: experts and the public.

On one side would be what we might call a chamber of experts, to which Estonia's knowledge-based umbrella organizations, such as universities, the Estonian Academy of Sciences and professional associations, would delegate representatives. All political parties represented in parliament would also be able to appoint representatives. The chamber of experts would operate through a series of sessions held over a designated period.

On the other side, the convention would include a chamber operating as a citizens' assembly, giving citizens interested in solving problems the opportunity to contribute their ideas and proposals to the formulation of strategic decisions through an online discussion platform.

The online citizens' assembly could be formed through both voluntary registration by individuals wishing to participate, with the necessary personal information provided and the application of representative sampling principles.

Both chambers of the convention would need to be supported by a team of specialists responsible for organizing expert sessions, managing the online citizens' assembly platform and ensuring the flow of information between the two levels.

Artificial intelligence could be used to quickly summarize and compare expert opinions and citizens' proposals, formulate recommendations based on them and put those recommendations to a vote. It could also be used to analyze background materials and datasets relating to the issues under discussion and visualize possible solutions.

In this way, the convention could become a genuine forum for collective deliberation, helping to build societal consensus on strategic issues important to Estonia's future. It would also enable both lawmakers and the government to base their plans for reforms with long-term consequences on a diverse range of thoroughly examined, publicly debated and interconnected perspectives.

World.title: Expert: Estonian party ratings could shift as election campaigning ramps up
World.content:
The Center Party and Social Democrats topped Emor's October poll as long-time leader Isamaa slipped, with voters' party loyalties still far from firm, said expert Aivar Voog.

Voog, a polling expert at Emor, told ERR on Friday that party ratings had remained largely unchanged over the last year, but shifted more sharply in recent months as parties ramp up campaigning ahead of the March 2027 Riigikogu elections.

He noted that new members may also be influencing support.

Isamaa had long led the rankings, but its supporters' loyalty was never particularly firm, Voog said, commenting on the party's slide to third place. "They have a significant mass of incidental [voters] and that has started to redistribute itself," he added.

He expects a clearer picture to emerge early next year, as some parties begin to stand out and attract undecided voters.

Longtime Foreign Ministry secretary general and security expert Jonatan Vseviov announced Thursday that he is joining the Social Democratic Party (SDE) and intends to run next spring as their candidate for prime minister. His move could affect the party's next poll result.

"He's certainly well known among opinion leaders and educated people, but little known to the wider electorate," Voog said, adding that while Vseviov has strong foreign and security policy chops, he still needs to prove himself on economic issues.

Mobilizing support

The Social Democrats, previously most popular among younger voters, are now also the top choice among middle-aged voters, narrowly overtaking Isamaa among ethnic Estonians. Voog said this could help offset a weakness, as younger supporters are less likely to vote than middle-aged voters.

Voog said the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) may also struggle to mobilize its supporters in March, as its typical supporter is a man over 60 who lives outside the capital.

EKRE supporters tend to rely on alternative media and the party's own channels, making them less susceptible to major media outlet influence and potentially more loyal.

Emor's latest poll put the party above 13 percent, but Voog said it remains unclear whether EKRE can not just broaden its appeal, but also convert support into votes at the ballot box.

Fight for voters

Voog said right-leaning voters in Estonia may split between Isamaa, EKRE, the Reform Party and Parempoolsed, while more conservative voters may choose between EKRE, Isamaa and the Center Party, setting several major parties up to compete for the same voters.

The Social Democrats, meanwhile, might benefit from voters abandoning the poorly rated Eesti 200, though some may instead shift their support to the Reform Party.

Voog said more conservative voters tend to be less active and turn out to vote at lower rates than those with more liberal views. Less active voters tend to be less educated and find it harder to decide whom to vote for, he explained, adding that they are also likely to consume less media.

While liberal voters dominated the 2023 Riigikogu elections, conservative forces had the upper hand in 2019, and Voog expects conservative parties will likely come out on top again next spring.

World.title: Police suspect bribery offense in roadworks quality control
World.content:
On Tuesday, police detained two employees of the Transport Administration and a company representative on suspicion of bribery offenses linked to road construction projects.

The Central Criminal Police suspect a 36-year-old company representative of repeatedly paying bribes totaling at least €2,300 and two Transport Administration employees of accepting bribes in exchange for failing to carry out their duties, the Police and Border Guard Board said.

For example, the employees are suspected of approving a project before it was actually completed and failing to conduct proper oversight.

According to preliminary information, the violations involved two Transport Administration contracts for road repairs in Järva and Ida-Viru counties. The contracts had a combined value of more than €1.3 million.

The suspicions are preliminary and further details will be established during the investigation, which is being led by the District Prosecutor's Office for Economic Crime and Corruption.

World.title: Estonia has a higher education gender gap and few plans to fix it
World.content:
Men make up just 40% of students in higher education in Estonia. Experts say raising the compulsory school attendance age to 18 alone won't close the gender gap.

Education and Research Minister Kristina Kallas (Eesti 200) and Kadri Täht, a professor of work and education sociology at Tallinn University (TLÜ), agree that the gender imbalance is not necessarily a problem in itself. It becomes one, Täht said, when educational choices limit people's future opportunities, reinforcing gender segregation in the labor market.

"Traditional jobs in manufacturing, where men typically found work and where engineers were required to have degrees, have declined," Kallas said. Automation has reduced demand for such jobs, she added, with artificial intelligence (AI) expected to accelerate the trend.

The imbalance is particularly pronounced in health and welfare majors, which encompass everything from healthcare to social work. Last academic year, women outnumbered men in these programs by more than four to one, with 5,553 female students compared with just 1,246 men.

Gender Equality and Equal Treatment Commissioner Christian Veske has likewise warned that the divide could leave society less prepared for crises.

"In a crisis, society needs everyone's skills, but the way people are distributed across educational fields limits that," he said, pointing to Ukraine's experience.

Gap starts much earlier

Both Kallas and Täht said the imbalance has roots in earlier stages of education.

"The education system likely already favors girls a bit more at the basic education level already," Täht acknowledged, citing differences in study habits and learning styles.

She said boys are also more likely to pursue vocational education after basic school. Men accounted for 54 percent of vocational students in Estonia last academic year, and have made up at least half of the total every year for the past eight years.

The professor stressed, however, that this does not mean the education system is designed for girls. Rather, social expectations may be contributing to differences in learning skills and motivation.

According to Estonia's latest PISA results, girls outscored boys in reading by 25 points, while boys led in math by 13 points. Täht said it is difficult to determine whether social or biological factors are at play.

Estonia also has one of the euro area's largest gender pay gaps, with men earning an average of 12.2 percent more than women last year, according to Statistics Estonia, and Täht said even that could be encouraging young men to enter the workforce sooner.

"Even when girls are better educated, we still see men ultimately earning more on average in the labor market," she explained.

Health impacts of higher ed

At the ministry, Kallas pointed to Estonia recently raising the compulsory school attendance age from 16 to 18 as one step toward narrowing the education gap.

Teens in an Estonian classroom. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

She said one of the goals of the change, which will keep teens in school until they've earned either a high school or vocational education diploma, "is to reduce the education gap between boys and girls."

Lower education levels are also associated with other issues, such as poorer health, the minister said.

Taavi Tillmann, an associate professor of public health at the University of Tartu (TÜ), has also discussed this link, telling Novaator that people with higher education levels tend to be healthier and have lower rates of cardiovascular disease — though exactly why remains unclear, even to Tillmann.

Täht agreed that raising the attendance age to 18 could help more boys finish school at the upper secondary level and go on to continue their education, but cautioned that it's still no guarantee more men will actually enroll.

"What matters is that more [boys] actually end up in upper secondary education and then go on from there to pursue higher education," she said.

Few measures target boys directly

Other government efforts include a regulation adopted by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communication (MKM) last November to reduce gender segregation in education and the labor market — although more broadly, the regulation serves to underpin the EU's funding system.

This spring, the State Shared Service Center (RTK) also distributed nearly €2.3 million to projects aimed at addressing the divide, with about 30 percent coming directly from the state budget.

Among the recipients, Taavi Kotka's HK Unicorn Squad received nearly €215,000 to promote girls' interest in technology and engineering, while the Estonian Business School (EBS) received €214,000 for a project to empower girls in STEM and leadership.

Of the 12 funded projects, only three directly encourage boys to pursue higher education: two focus on teachers and one on healthcare workers.

At TLÜ, Täht said the education system should identify earlier what causes teen boys to lose interest in school and continuing their education.

"That way they could be provided with better support and guidance, and they could find their education more meaningful, exciting and useful," she added.

While the compulsory school attendance age was only just raised to 18 this year, women have accounted for around 60 percent of higher education students since at least 2010.

Asked why the state hadn't acted sooner, Kallas said, "Better late than never."

The minister added that there are already so many major initiatives underway in Estonia's education system that the ministry simply lacks the capacity to take on anything new, including addressing the gender education gap.

World.title: Ukraine says two soldiers died after arrested girl sent Russian poison
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian police said Friday they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died.

Ukraine and Russia have throughout their war since 2022 accused each other of recruiting minors for sabotage acts including poisoning.

The girl, who was not named, is suspected of having packaged deadly drugs and sending them to Ukrainian soldiers she contacted by Telegram, said a police statement.

She was arrested by police in Zhytomyr, west of Kyiv, after allegedly following instructions from a Russian handler in exchange for at least 5,000 hryvnias ($111), they said.

After receiving packages with “free drugs”, the soldiers were “instructed to take them on camera”, the statement said.

“The recipients did not know that the capsules contained a lethal dose of methadone,” it said, adding that “two soldiers died from poisoning in the Zhytomyr region.”

Police said they had identified other recipients of the packages, which “prevented four more murders” across the country.

“The young woman was notified that she is suspected of aiding and abetting the premeditated murder of two people as part of a prior conspiracy,” the police statement said.

She was also suspected of “shipping drugs and psychotropic substances for the purpose of distribution”, it said, adding that she faced up to 15 years in jail if found guilty.

Police cautioned that Russia aims “to kill our people and destabilise the situation within the country”.

“Do not accept medication or other substances, as well as food or drinks of dubious origin, from people you do not know well,” police cautioned.

Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukrainian authorities say they have opened thousands of investigations into collaboration with the enemy, and frequently arrest individuals accused of working for Moscow.

In 2023, Ukraine accused Russia of poisoning the wife of Kyrylo Budanov, who was then head of Ukraine’s military intelligence and is now a presidential advisor.

World.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
World.content:
Stockholm – Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Shortly after 0800 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down almost 30 percent.

“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change,” chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, “through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees”.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

“We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges,” Samuelsson said.

“However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient.”

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

The company said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him “no later” than October next year.

World.title: France braces for new protests as Macron seeks to restore order
World.content:
Paris – France was on Friday bracing for a weekend of new protests after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, as President Emmanuel Macron sought to reclaim the initiative and restore order.

Macron, who on Thursday announced that only union demonstrations would be authorised this weekend, was to hold a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and also meet security forces.

He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked a movement that has broadened nationwide into a show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city.

Macron is due to announce “additional decisions” after hosting the meeting of his defence council, on top of the limited curfews already announced, his office said.

At the meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP.

Pierre Sourzat, who heads the organisation Les Lyceens (The High School Students), was sceptical: “He’ll listen to us, pretend he’s understood us, and then nothing will come of it.”

Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday.

In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.

– ‘Police have a responsibility’ –

Demonstrations in Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast have been banned at the weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares.

Marseille authorities however reversed a decision to halt all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.

Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week.

“In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons.

The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors.

A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.

It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote.

World.title: Kering shares tumble as Gucci fails to reassure investors
World.content:
Paris – Kering shares were down more than 10 percent in Paris Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand.

At 0730 GMT, Kering shares were down 10.8 percent at 190.40 euros, their lowest since June 2025. The market’s CAC40 index was down 0.3 percent.

Kering reported late Thursday that third-quarter sales were flat at 3.34 billion euros ($3.75 billion).

Sales at Gucci, by far the group’s largest single brand, fell by four percent to 1.29 billion euros, worse than the three-percent decline registered in the second quarter.

“Gucci has not shown convincing signs of stabilisation,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note.

Italy-based Gucci is key to Kering’s fortunes, but has been in freefall since 2023 as the brand lost its luxury cachet.

World.title: West Bank attack wounds 5 as Israel PM cancels events
World.content:
Hebron – An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and touched off a shootout that ended with two suspected Palestinian assailants dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections.

An AFP journalist who witnessed the firefight saw two Palestinian men in casual attire and armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire with Israeli forces at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city of Hebron.

The journalist reported that Israeli forces eventually shot and killed the attackers, their two lifeless bodies on the ground next to a petrol station as Israeli troops patrolled in all directions.

The Israeli military said soldiers had rushed to the Judea Junction area, also known as the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint, after the early-morning shooting attack.

“IDF (Israel Defense Forces) soldiers eliminated two terrorists and continue searches in the area,” it said in a statement.

The initial shooting wounded five people, two of whom were in critical condition, said Magen David Adom, Israel’s emergency medical rescue service.

The Magen David Adom said one of the victims was a man in his 20s in “very serious condition” with gunshot wounds.

Netanyahu, running for a new term in elections on Tuesday, called for all political meetings to be cancelled Friday due to the attack.

Israeli National Security Minister and far-right firebrand Itamar Ben Gvir, who has been rising in the polls, called for the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority to be dismantled because of the attack.

“The Palestinian Authority must be dismantled and demilitarized, and its terror infrastructure wiped out completely,” he said in a statement.

No evidence suggests that the Palestinian Authority, the Palestinian government in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, was connected to Friday’s attack.

Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief who is Netanyahu’s top rival in the election, praised the response by troops.

“Like all Israelis, I pray for the complete and quick recovery of the injured,” he said.

The incident comes as tensions soar in the West Bank, including over attacks by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters, and days ahead of Israeli elections.

According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces or settlers have killed 1,113 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023.

Israeli figures show at least 49 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.

World.title: South Korea proposes holding border talks with North
World.content:
Seoul – South Korea proposed on Friday military talks with North Korea to “mutually confirm the precise location” of their border and discuss restoring communication channels, after an explosion in the DMZ further strained relations.

Tensions between the two Koreas have soared since the South last month blamed the blast inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) separating the countries on landmines laid by the North, an accusation it has fiercely rejected.

The South Korean defence ministry “formally proposes holding military talks with North Korea to mutually confirm the precise location of the land Military Demarcation Line (MDL) and discuss ways to restore military communication lines and prevent accidental clashes in border areas,” Kim Hong-cheol, deputy defense minister for policy, told reporters Friday.

The proposal comes just days after Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, announced that Pyongyang had moved new troop units into “firing position” along the border.

Seoul’s defence ministry said Friday it was difficult to predict “what further incidents could occur if this situation is allowed to continue unaddressed”.

The ministry said that “three-way talks involving the United Nations Command would also be possible”.

“Specific dates and locations could be discussed through Panmunjom,” said Kim, referencing the symbolic truce village where troops from both Koreas stand face-to-face.

He added they hoped for “a positive response from North Korea”.

The South Korean defence ministry also noted that talks proposed last year with the North did not get a response from Pyongyang.

– Grave situation –

Seoul’s military on Tuesday accused Pyongyang of attempting to shift the blame for escalating military tensions, while confirming the use of loudspeakers and warning shots as “legitimate defensive measures to prevent North Korean troops from crossing the MDL and to drive back troops that have crossed it”.

Jin Yong-sung, chairman of South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff, also ordered the military to “respond with firm resolve” should North Korea use Seoul’s actions as a pretext for aggressive action.

Pyongyang has rejected claims it was behind the explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers inside the DMZ and mockingly dismissed calls for an apology.

The country on Monday called the situation along the border “grave”, saying it was considering deploying additional “tactical strike means” to the area.

On Thursday, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said the North would place loudspeakers on standby along the border “within days” and had put unspecified “new counter means” on alert.

South Korea’s foreign ministry also said Thursday it planned to send a letter to the president of the UN Security Council later in the day over the landmine incident, which it called a “clear violation of the armistice agreement”.

President Lee Jae Myung has called for the North to return to dialogue, an overture Kim Yo Jong later slammed as “the climax of the farce”.

World.title: Asian football endorses Infantino re-election as FIFA president
World.content:
Tokyo – The head of the Asian Football Confederation on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president following fierce criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan.

The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the AFC when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing.

The AFC in August had joined UEFA (Europe) and CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino has faced calls to quit and has lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term.

“I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president,” said Sheikh Salman, in a significant boost to Infantino’s prospects.

“I think you’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent.

“I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.”

Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: “Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past.

“But let’s not relate the two things together. We need to move forward… football is strongest when we work together.”

Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March.

The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

No heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against him so far, despite outspoken condemnation especially from Europe.

Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino over controversies including his relationship with US President Donald Trump.

World.title: Rooney calls United squad ‘selfish babies’ after Fernandes criticism
World.content:
Manchester – Manchester United great Wayne Rooney has labelled the current squad “babies” and “selfish” after a humiliating Champions League capitulation and post-match criticism by Bruno Fernandes of manager Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s men are 13th in the Premier League ahead of Sunday’s visit by Bournemouth and could drop into the bottom three if results go against them this weekend.

With the club beset by infighting and off to their worst domestic league start for decades, Carrick was left clinging to his job after the 4-1 defeat at Como on Wednesday.

Deepening the sense of crisis, the captain Fernandes afterwards took aim at his manager’s tactics, saying United had to be more “brave”.

Defender Lisandro Martinez last week criticised the club’s board for not investing enough in the transfer market.

Rooney, United’s all-time leading goalscorer, said he was in “shock” and “disbelief” at the Como display.

A friend and ex-teammate of Carrick, former striker Rooney pointed the finger at the players.

“When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart,” Rooney told The United Stand podcast on Thursday.

“That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because these players, they don’t want to take responsibility.

“You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.”

He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

“If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.”

World.title: Fodder scam accused nabbed after 25 years, had fled to Nepal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ending a quarter-century-long game of hide-and-seek, CBI has arrested

, a key fugitive wanted in connection with Biharâs infamous

. The suspect had fled to Nepal and was tracked down during a train journey he took upon returning to India, the agency said.

Acting on court orders, CBI had undertaken the probe into the multi-crore corruption scam involving the systematic embezzlement of funds from the Animal Husbandry Department in Bihar during the 1990s. High-profile political figures, including former Bihar chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, along with several senior bureaucrats and suppliers, have since been convicted in multiple cases related to illegal treasury withdrawals.

The agency had filed dozens of FIRs to untangle a nexus of politicians, bureaucrats, suppliers and middlemen who siphoned off public funds through fake invoices for cattle feed, medicines and equipment.

Kumar, alleged to be a supplier, had been on the run since 2001, vanishing into the shadows immediately after the agency filed its charge sheet in the case. His persistent failure to face trial prompted the court to issue an arrest warrant and declare him an absconder, cementing his status as one of the scamâs most elusive figures.

It was a to a manhunt that spanned more than two decades across international borders. For over 25 years, Kumar managed to evade the law by taking refuge across the border in Nepal living under an assumed identity. However, the net slowly began to tighten as CBI officials mounted human and technical surveillance to pinpoint his exact movements.

The breakthrough came when intelligence revealed that Kumar had re-entered India and was travelling by train from Guna, Madhya Pradesh, to Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Acting swiftly on the input, a team was tasked with intercepting the fugitive mid-transit. Units were deployed across Lucknow Railway Station well before the train arrived. World.title: UP polls: Congress shares initial list with SP, seeks 175-200 seats
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress has formally begun seat-sharing negotiations with the Samajwadi Party (SP) in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, submitting an initial list of more than 175 assembly constituencies to the Akhilesh Yadav-led party.

Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congressâ in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, told PTI that the list was shared with SP leaders around two days ago. He added that leaders from both parties would soon hold detailed discussions on the nature of a seat-sharing arrangement.

âI can't give you the exact numbers, but we have submitted a list for 175 to 200 seats. The leadership of both parties will sit together to thrash out the nitty-gritties of the seat-sharing arrangement," Gautam said.

The Congress has reportedly classified constituencies based on an assessment of its electoral prospects, and seat-sharing negotiations are expected to centre on this assessment.

Scepticism within SP over Congressâ seat demands

However, several SP leaders remain unconvinced that the Congress has enough political clout to demand 175-200 seats, despite their successful alliance in Uttar Pradesh during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

The scepticism stems from the Congressâ declining electoral fortunes in Uttar Pradesh since 1989, when it last held power in the countryâs most populous state.





âI think our party leader

has made it clear that winnability is the sole criterion (for contesting the polls). Anyone can demand anything, but in politics, to reach an acceptable and meaningful solution, you have to move beyond posturing,â a senior SP leader told PTI.

The Congress contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently but managed to win just two constituencies, down from seven in 2017, when it fought in alliance with the SP.

That year, the SP lost power after a single term, securing only 47 seats, while the BJP won a landslide 312 seats in the 403-member ssembly.

In 2022, the BJP retained power with 255 seats, while the SP won 111 constituencies.

However, the 2024 Lok Sabha elections offered the Congress renewed hope. The grand old party won six seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the SP secured 37 of the stateâs 80 seats, limiting the BJP to 33, down from 62 in 2019 and 71 in 2014.

The results have strengthened the Congressâ expectations of securing a ârespectable shareâ of seats in the 2027 assembly elections, party leaders acknowledged.

âItâs obviousâ¦ The 2024 Lok Sabha results were proof that together the two parties can make an impact. In politics, there has to be room for meaningful give and take,â a senior Congress leader said.

How the change in UP Congress leadership could influence seat-sharing talks

The recent leadership change in the Uttar Pradesh Congress, with Aradhana Misra âMonaâ succeeding Ajay Rai as state unit chief, is also believed to have been factored into the partyâs efforts to reach an amicable seat-sharing arrangement with the SP.

Some believe Rai was not in favour of a pre-poll alliance, viewing a post-poll arrangement as a more suitable option for the Congress.

However, some party leaders feel that Misraâs âexcellent relationsâ with the SP leadership may have influenced the partyâs decision to appoint her months ahead of the Assembly elections, potentially facilitating negotiations between them

The Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are scheduled to be held in February-March next year.

World.title: Siddaramaiah cries blackmail over ‘fake sting’ video, alleges conspiracy
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Karnataka chief minister

on Friday said he had lodged a police complaint over an alleged âfake sting operationâ video targeting him, alleging that it was an attempt to blackmail him after he lost power.

Speaking to reporters in Mysuru, the senior Congress leader said he wanted the truth to come out and those behind the video to be identified. He also said he had obtained an injunction from a civil court to prevent the video from being given further publicity.

âThis is a false case. This case was done with the intention to blackmail me. Therefore, I myself have filed a complaint so that the truth comes out. The people should know the truth and also who is behind this,â Siddaramaiah said.

He alleged that the video was fabricated and said he had never faced such an incident during his earlier tenures in office.

âI was chief minister for 8 years, at that time no incident of blackmailing me happened. Now I have no power,â he said.

Siddaramaiah named Kripa Alva, a woman from Dakshina Kannada, and Rakesh Shetty as people who appeared in the video. He claimed that Shetty had admitted to carrying out the operation.





âRakesh Shetty himself has admitted that they did it. There is no truth in this video,â he said.

Siddaramaiah said the video first came to his notice on September 26 and denied being worried about the allegations.

âAfter I have not done any wrong, there is no question of me being upset. No matter who sets out to defame me, I know what the truth is. There is no question of me being upset or afraid. This case is 100% created,â he said.

Recalling his political career, he said he first became a minister in 1984 and had faced no such incident even when he was chief minister.

âNow when I have no power, such a conspiracy is being hatched. It is true that their intention will not succeed,â he asserted.

Yathindra alleges Congress links to sting operation

Meanwhile, Karnataka minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah alleged that people from within the Congress were behind the purported sting operation, which he claimed was intended to damage his father's image and blackmail him.

Speaking to reporters in Mysuru, Yathindra said the video appeared to show the involvement of a woman from the Congress who wanted a party ticket from Puttur, along with the head of a media organisation.

âThe whole thing was done to damage my father, tarnish his image, destroy his legacy and blackmail him,â Yathindra said.

The minister, who holds the Urban Development portfolio, said the woman's alleged involvement appeared to be linked to her political ambitions.

âThere is a woman from our party who is involved. As she herself says in the video, she wanted a party ticket from Puttur. Prima facie, it appears that the sting operation was conducted for that purpose,â he said.

However, Yathindra cautioned against holding the entire Congress responsible for the alleged actions of an individual party worker.

âJust because a party worker has done something like this, it does not mean that our entire party is against us,â he said.

World.title: ‘There will be no privatisation’: Haryana CM assures power employees as electricity union calls off strike
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Haryanaâs striking electricity employees on Friday called off their three-day strike following a meeting with chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and power minister Anil Vij.

The employees said Saini assured them that private players would not be allowed to enter Haryanaâs power sector and that parallel power distribution licences would be revoked. Following the chief minister's assurance, they agreed to restore electricity supply immediately.

The next round of talks between the employeesâ union and the state government will be held on November 3.

The strike, which began on Wednesday night, was being held to protest the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commissionâs (HERC) decision to grant a parallel electricity distribution licence to private company Eleven Power for Gurugram and Nuh.

'There will be no privatisation of any kind': Saini

Addressing a joint press conference with Vij and representatives of the electricity employeesâ union, Saini emphasised that there would be âno privatisation of any kind."

He also pointed out that the HERC is an independent regulatory body.

âWe have consistently maintained that we stand fully with the electricity employeesâ union, and we reiterate that position today. It should be noted that the HERC is an independent agency operating under its own Act.





From time to time, we, the state government, are also required to implement its orders and directives,â the chief minister told reporters at a press conference in Panchkula.

âExercising our authority under

, the government has directed the HERC to review the matter and effectively cancel that provision (private power distribution). The government has provided full assurances. The electricity employees have stated that the strike is being called off, and our employees will now immediately resume their duties.

Our position is absolutely firm: there will be no privatisation of any kind,â he added.

How strike triggered chaos

Thousands of households were left without electricity and water, nearly 1,800 manufacturing units faced disruption, and residents took to the streets as a three-day strike crippled power supply across Gurugram, Haryanaâs financial hub, and other cities.

World.title: Government to modify labour survey to capture gig economy, unpaid household workers
World.content:
The Union government has decided to change the design and structure of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) to track digital platform workers and capture engagement in unpaid household, caregiving, volunteer, and trainee work. The PLFS will also include additional questions to measure labour underutilisation.

According to a press release and concept note issued in New Delhi on Friday (October 23, 2026), the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), has proposed modifications to the PLFS sampling design starting January 2027. The survey schedule will also change.

The Ministry has invited comments and suggestions from policymakers, researchers, academic institutions, and the public within 15 days from Friday.

A separate Second Stage Stratum (SSS) will be introduced in the PLFS to identify households with at least one digital platform worker. An additional entry will be added to the questionnaire to determine whether any member of the household has engaged in digital platform work during the specified reference period.

“There will be four SSSs in rural areas and five in urban areas, with 14 households canvassed in each selected First Stage Unit (FSU). This revision in SSS formation is expected to improve the coverage of digital platform workers and facilitate more comprehensive data collection on this emerging segment of the labour market,” the press release said.

According to the concept note, a large proportion of women in India spend considerable time on unpaid household and caregiving activities, such as cooking, cleaning, childcare, and caring for elderly, sick, or disabled family members. “While such activities contribute significantly to household well-being and facilitate the participation of other household members in paid employment, they have not been measured separately in PLFS until now,” it noted, adding that specific questions will be incorporated to capture engagement in own-use production of goods, unpaid household and caregiving activities, volunteer work, and unpaid trainee work.

Additionally, the criteria for sample allocation and stratification have been updated based on the experience of the previous two years. “These revisions are expected to improve the efficiency of sample allocation and stratification and ensure better representation of population variations, which in turn will minimise operational difficulties during sample selection,” the press release said.

World.title: Two workers killed in chloroform vapour leak at pharma unit, TGPCB orders closure
World.content:
Two employees of a pharmaceutical manufacturing unit were killed after being exposed to chloroform vapours that leaked during a production process at Saraca Laboratories Limited in the Gaddapotharam industrial area of Jinnaram mandal in Sangareddy district late on Thursday (October 22).

The deceased were identified as Sudharshan Rao, 44, and Balaji, 27, both natives of Andhra Pradesh. One of them was working as a chemist and the other as a supervisor at the facility.

Following the incident, the Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) on Friday ordered the immediate closure of the unit and directed the Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (TGSPDCL) to disconnect its electricity supply.

According to the TGPCB, the incident occurred around 11.30 p.m. on Thursday during a layer separation process in Production Block-2 of the facility.

The leak reportedly occurred while chloroform was being transferred from a reactor located on the first floor to a receiver on the ground floor. Vapours spread rapidly through the production area, exposing the two employees to the chemical.

Both workers lost consciousness and were rushed to Narayana Hospital, where the duty doctor declared them dead. The hospital subsequently informed the police.

Following the deaths, TGPCB officials inspected the manufacturing facility on Friday and obtained details of the incident from the company’s general manager and deputy general manager. During the inspection, company representatives explained the circumstances surrounding the leak and provided technical details of the production process during which the incident occurred.

Considering the seriousness of the incident, the Board issued closure orders without providing the company an opportunity for a hearing beforehand. It also instructed TGSPDCL officials in Sangareddy to disconnect the unit’s power supply.

World.title: Bharat Petroleum’s net profit dips amid volatile crude prices in Q2
World.content:
Bharat Petroleum’s standalone net profits in the September-end quarter fell 22.5% on a year-over-year basis as volatile crude prices impacted margins following the reignited conflict in West Asia.

The Mumbai-headquartered refiner’s net profit declined to ₹4,993.17 crore in the reported quarter compared to ₹6,442.5 crore in the same period last year.

The state-owned oil-marketing company’s cost of materials consumed soared 44.2% during the period to ₹74,969 crore.

Revenues increased about 29% on a year-over-year basis to more than ₹1.58 lakh crore.

The refiners’ physical performance reported an uptick. It rose 6% during the mentioned period to 10.41 million metric tonnes (MMT).

Domestic sales grew about 6.33% to 13.47 MMT.

Also read | Strike by lorry drivers at BPCL depot in Salem withdrawn

Its peer Hindustan Petroleum had reported a 9% decline in standalone net profits on Thursday.

Delhi-headquartered peer Indian Oil is scheduled to post their September-end financial results on October 30.

World.title: Kremlin says a first tanker of Russian diesel sets sail for U.S. despite Ukraine's protests
World.content:
A first tanker carrying Russian diesel to the United States under a new import agreement has set sail, the Kremlin said Friday (October 23, 2026), two weeks after President Donald Trump said he struck a deal with President Vladimir Putin despite Moscow's invasion of Ukraine.

“The first oil tanker has sailed off to customers, and regular supplies will continue,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said without elaborating.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said earlier this week that the first shipment would amount to 40,000 tons of diesel, according to Russia's Interfax news agency.

Marine intelligence firm Kpler said the vessel was signalling it was headed to New York to arrive Nov. 7 and would be the first Russian diesel delivery to the United States since July 2023.

The abrupt reversal of U.S. sanctions policy on Russia over its invasion of its neighbour was seen as an attempt by Mr. Trump to address high fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.

The diesel shipment of 40,000 tons amounts to around 300,000 barrels, or about 7% of the roughly 4 million barrels of diesel the U.S. economy consumes in a single day.

The import agreement, which Mr. Trump says foresees millions more tons of Russian diesel reaching the U.S. in coming months, is unlikely to make a dent in painfully high prices at the pump or elsewhere, energy policy experts say.

Russia's diesel production has come under strain from repeated Ukrainian long-range drone strikes on its oil refineries. The attacks caused fuel shortages, which have now eased. Mr. Trump last month asked Kyiv to stop the attacks.

The U.S. diesel decision caused alarm and dismay in Ukraine, which has pleaded with foreign countries to tighten sanctions on Moscow and deny it revenue for its invasion launched in February 2022.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called Mr. Trump's decision “a weak decision by strong partners.”

The diesel agreement was a sudden policy reversal, coming just weeks after Mr. Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package that directed him to impose up to 100% tariffs on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas. He later put the measures on hold.

The development is the latest twist in the at-times volatile relationship between Mr. Trump and Mr. Zelenskyy, which in recent weeks has reached a new low.

Moscow airports close

Meanwhile, Russia's civil aviation authority, Rosaviatsia, said Friday afternoon (October 23, 2026) that all four Moscow airports — Sheremetyevo, Vnukovo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky — stopped flights arriving and departing for security reasons.

At Sheremetyevo Airport, passengers were told to take shelter, Russian news agency Interfax reported. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that air defences downed 17 Ukrainian drones targeting the Russian capital.

Meanwhile, Russia and Ukraine exchanged hundreds of prisoners of war for the first time since August.
